text: The overall property is nice. Parking is expensive and so is the internet. Rooms are no better than a motel 6, very disappointed if you expect upscale nice clean modern room. Furniture is dated and worn, fixtures are worn and old, shower curtain was hanging by a screw. They are updating and just a warning you can hear noise from construction, not a huge amt of noise but if your here and working it can be a distraction. great location near shops of sea port village.

Our one-night stay here was among my very worst hotel experiences. We booked because of it's much advertised proximity to Union Station and our understanding that we were booking a "Suite". It's in a grim, sad area nowhere near the station, and has only rooms with unseparated TV areas. The fold out, and the subsequent cot I tried, were in such bad shape that I finally slept on a mattress on the floor! We couldn't wait to escape......

An older Hampton Inn / rooms are nothing to rave over / lobby could use a major refresh! At a Hampton Inn, you typically know what you're getting, and this property is at the lower end of those expectations! Fine for one night, but I'd recommend looking elsewhere (maybe in the Fischers area?) if you have a choice. No restaurant (typical of Hampton) but no decent restaurants in walking distance, and none that I could find within a reasonable drive (no suggestions from the front desk, except which way to drive to find a restaurant).

When staying downtown San Antonio, Hotel Contessa is my only choice I give myself. I have stayed multiple times and have never had a bad experience. Love the spacious rooms, excellent service and great food in a wonderful environment. Just steps from the riverwalk, you wont be disappointed staying here. Pool and Spa are must experience.

Just finished a three day stay at this property and it is among one of the best Hyatt properties I have stayed at. The lobby was grand and the staff was excellent.Rooms were clean and staff was polite. I feel comfortable recommending this hotel to business travelers and families. Hotel is very well located and my room had a sensational view of the bay and Coronado island.

Horrible experience, don't go there, no heater, no service, no information, no blankets, the cold win pass through the windows, impossible to talk with some one, waste of money the experience. The owner, doesn't like to talk, to improve, to find solution. Noise room close to avenue, impossible to sleep

We stayed in a honeymoon suite for our anniversary. The suite had a large whirlpool, jetted tub with a polished marble floor, candles, mini soundsystem, and a place for breakfast. Management delivered champagne to our suite as well as chocolates. The bar was cozy and the bartender and patrons were all friendly!

We visit San Francisco frequently and have tried several nice hotels. The "W" vibe is modern and cool – from the lobby lounge by the fireplace to the fresh and inviting guest rooms. The "welcome" staff always takes time to find us the best room available. The Acura concierge comes in handy, sometimes on a moments notice (this time he gave our party of four a ride to Perry's on the Embarcadero). But it all comes down to the gorgeous dramatic guest rooms!

Bad place all around. The handle to the faucet on the sink was just laying on the sink, had not been fixed. Noisey bed, found it hard to sleep with every turn waking me up. Front desk personal were so so. Room was clean as well as the bathroom, but not enough for me to return again.

This is a really good 3 star hotel. great location and reception. Rooms are nicely furnished, Staff were great help. We had 2 rooms, the normal suite and a largere one with a sofa bed for the kids. Transportation is close by with the sub way. we would stay again.

First and last time I stay at this hotel.. Paid 350$ for a tiny room not even a table to put a phone, had to put it on the floor. The bed is very near the AC and the noise is terrible. Lots of hotels in New York are way better and less costly even if you have to take a taxi or walk to to come to the area. Too bad I am stuck here one more night because it is prepaid this is a bad experience!

The staff friendly and very clean hotel. The beds need to be replaced as they are hard as a rock, could not sleep and the pillows were hard and small. The location was good for access to freeway and downtown area. To make the overall experience great,replace the beds as people do need a good night's sleep to enjoy work and the city.

The staff at this hotel is particularly friendly and helpful. The location is very close to the airport so it is not great for site seeing but it is good for business. The rooms were nicely decorated and comfortable. The walls were a little thin so that you could hear the room next door.

The staff was friendly and helpful but overall the hotel is awful. This was a terrible experience! The room was dingy and dirty...carpet actually turned our socks black. The bathroom looked as if it had NEVER been thoroughly cleaned...mildew,soap scum,filthy toilet and nasty floor! We also were bitten by bugs of some sort the last night.This place needs an overhaul and an inspection. DISGUSTING!!!!!

Check-in at 4:00 pm told don't leave any valuables in car. nothing else, Returned at 9:00pm after dinner with Kids. Sorry no parking you have to take you changes on the street! Attendant told us to park carefully wheels in because police give ticket for little reason or no reason. Choose this place by phone representative of hotels com because of free parking. Hotels.com level 3 service said you have to check the hotel yourself they are not reasonableness for thier reps.

4 people checked in and only 2 towels, one of which had women's make up smeared on it. Ran out of toilet paper because we were only given half of a roll. Tissue box was empty. Charged for ice. 'Free' breakfast was pathetic and not enough for our party of 4. Dirty surroundings and more disgustingly, pubes in the bath tub.

I've stayed at better and worse Days Inns before (and reviewed two that are much worse, see Alexandria, VA and Hardeeville, SC). This one is a good basic hotel, with the normal cheap continental breakfast. Nothing to write home about, but not a horror either. Quite adequate for business travel on a budget. Indoor pool year-round, small but functional.

We stayed at this hotel for a wedding. YUCK. The bathroom was dirty and incredibly outdated. The shower head put out about 5% of the water coming through the tap and it alternated between scorching and ice cold. We could hear everything in the room next door. I've staying in nicer chain hotels (Super 8). Everyone at the wedding reception was talking about how sub-par their rooms were and laughing about the showers. The front desk was completely disorganized and couldn't even provide a recommendation for a Mexican breakfast - in SAN ANTONIO?!! Stay somewhere else!

If you want to meet a pilot, this is the place. Otherwise, it is not so hot. I waited over an hour for the shuttle to pick me up (I was first told 20 minutes and called after forty. I was told it would take another ten minutes and it was another 20). I had a room on the first floor under reception. I heard people in the halls and walking above me all night, whenever anybody came. The ice machine was broken. The tv had something unplugged for which the engineer had to be called.

Stayed at the Rex Hotel for 2 days during our California trip, when we arrived I was disappointed to find a small, dismal looking hotel with a front entrance that was decidedly tatty. Our room was extremely small and the air conditioning noisy. Most unimpressive, but quaint and old fashioned in the dining room/bar, a novelty free glass of wine every evening and complimentary Wi-Fi. Staff very pleasant and helpful, but if you want upmarket this is not the place for you.

We had in Park South hotel on August 2012, was three people. Good room, good bath, excellent breakfast and the recepcionists Damian and Cat ¡the best! very helpfull and smiling always! Location's hotel !excellent! close to metro and in quiet but not boring neirborghood The worse was A/C unit noise, is difficult a quiet sleep with that.

Maybe it's a Boston thing, but I felt that this hotel was overall outdated even though it's been maintained/cared for pretty well. Tiny/old room, tiny/old bathroom, dark/red decor. I felt claustrophobic and caged. Location is pretty good though. Went to Parker House restaurant for breakfast buffet: again tiny and dark dining area, small collection of food for the buffet but the service was very good.

We had a fantastic experience at the W. Eden, our concierge, emailed me three days before the trip and offered her help with anything we might need. Every member of the staff that we dealt with at the hotel was great, but Eden really went above and beyond and made the trip perfect. She took care of everything for us and made the weekend flawless and fabulous. We can't recommend her or this hotel highly enough!

The hotel is absolutely beautiful. Traditional and classic decor. The hotel staff is excellent and their treatment of the residents is impeccable. The food at the restaurant was very good to excellent. Location was very good. Just 5 blocks from the White House. Easy walk to many attractions. Would definitely stay here again.

Big room for the age of the property. The staff was friendly, the room was clean, but needed some maintenance. Price is good for the area, and the river walk is about a block away, so the location is very good. It would be nice if they provided a movie channel like HBO or something.

This is the second time I stayed here, primarily because of it's proximity to my job. It's a Red Roof, not a Hilton, just a Red Roof. The location of the property is great for restaurants and it's not too far for San Antonio's attractions. I got "clean" in the shower and I slept in the bed. That's enough about that. They offer a shuttle service to the attractions and the airport. Basic continental breakfast with a Texas-shaped waffle. Swimming pool looks enticing, but it's not my thing. No complaints, I'd do it again.

The staff were very helpful and accommodated our extra needs. There are several fast and inexpensive sandwich and pizza places nearby so you can save for a splurge dinner. The rooms were clean, but need an update. The air conditioner sounded like an airplane taking off when it started up. It made for several wake ups during the night. The location was perfect for doing anything in Chicago... no more than $10 by cab can get you anywhere downtown. This hotel was very reasonable cost for the area.

Long lines and general apathy is what we were greeted with from the start of our stay. It didn't help that USC fans were trashing the lobby nightly waiting for their game against Stanford. There is no warmth to this hotel. Room was clean. The surrounding blocks are filled with panhandlers. Note: Park directly across the street from the hotel. It is cheaper and you probably will get your car faster

my stay at the blake hotel was not a good one my sheets was nasty customer service was okay they had rats running in the hall way i had a bed bug on my bed. Some of the rooms didnt have power they have a lot of water damage. The cover my bed with old sheets that looks like its never been washed

We were pleasantly surprised by all aspects of the Day's Hotel. The rooms, service, breakfast (although not included), were excellent. We lost an important item in the room, and they were very helpful. While the hallway was still a little shabby, the room looked as if it had just been renovated, and they are planning more renovations. I'm pretty fussy, and I would certainly recommend this hotel and stay again.

I had a wonderful stay at The Surrey last week. The location, just half a block from Central Park on a quiet side street, was so convenient. My corner room had lots of windows and light. The furnishings were chic and the bedding was luxurious, and I loved the upscale toiletries provided. The marble bathroom was spacious and the shower had incredible water pressure. The staff was warm and welcoming, even offering me a hot towel when I checked in. I thoroughly enjoyed my visit to The Surrey and would definitely stay here again.

I stayed here for a few days during a tour of Northern California. The location is quite good as yopu can walk to Union Square in about 20 minutes There are a lot of homeless people about so I wouldnnt recommend walking at night!! The rooms are small but reasonably comfortable and we had a tiny but adequate ensuite shower room. There is a Starbucks in the lobby which is great to sit and people watch in the morning. The inhouse resturant is nice although we only had breakfast there The staff were very friendly and helpful too

I have stayed at this property many times. It just keeps getting better. This 57 room hotel is a great place to stay in the SOMA or Downtown area. Close to public transportation. Free Parking. Upgraded security. Video camera's and a weekend guard. The Guard is really not needed at this SAFE property. One of the few hotel's in SF with good free parking. 24 hour front desk staff. A few smoking rooms. A nice, clean outdoor pool. Friendly and helpful staff.

I have visited NYC many many times and my room at the Hilton Times Square was by far the largest ever plus there is a coffeemaker in the room (don't get that much either). As with all Hilton brand hotels, the hotel was immaclate, staff friendly and helpful. Conveniently located on West 42nd St to theatres, restaurants and bars. All in all, a great place to stay in NYC

The hotel staff was super friendly, clean rooms and they did everything to accomodate any request we had. Best hotel we have ever stayed at! Highly Recommend this hotel! This hotel is exceptionally clean and the staff-all throughout the hotel treat you so well, regardless of how you are dressed (gym clothes). Short walk to the Little Italy area for dining - no pressure to eat in the hotel. This was our second trip to Boston and both times we stayed at BHH. Itis worth every penny!

the hotel was very good for our long weekend in manhatten. The location was perfectt in the middle of Manhattan 5-10 minutes to 5th Avenue , Empire State Building, Time Square ect. The room was small but very clean and good enaugh for us. About the noice outside the sleep quality is not very good, but who cares...NY never sleeps :) The Americana Inn is a good choise for sightseeing in New York./Manhattan.

We spent little time in the room which was small, the bathroom doesn't have any room for toiletries. The hotel is in the heart of Union Square. We had a very hard time getting sleep there are several Pigeons outside of the room that make loud noises and bang against the windows. The water heater is also very loud. Hotel is a bit dated and the continental breakfast is a joke.

We recently (6/11 - 6/17) stayed at The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square on 8th Avenue. We were impressed with the doorman, front desk, security, concierge and especially our housekeeper Gladys. Gladys was very pleasant and always greeted us with a smile. She arranged her schedule to accommodate our request for early makeup service. Thank You. The entire staff made our visit to New York a pleasant experience. Our next visit to New York will definitely be HGI Times Square.

Front desk staff is incredibly rude. Especially Tsubasa [--]. If we asked for anything we were looked at as an inconvenience, like towels or directions, etc, as was every other guest we over heard conversations with. John [--] was the only saving grace of our stay. He's actually a nice person! Everyone left with bed bug bites. I didn't realize I needed bug spray IN the hotel. Their shuttle service is a joke. I recommend staying somewhere else!

Comfortable enough hotel adjacent to a good restaurant. Employees wear tacky Best Western polo shirts, whereas their competitors usually dress more professionally. Rooms are small (which is typical of these era hotels), but comfortable enough. Television has only 15 channels of so. Housekeeping does a good job keeping them clean. In-room safe was inoperable, but there are safety boxes at the front desk.

Superior Service! Average looking lobby, but again great customer service. When we checked into our first room we immediately detected a strong moldy odor coming from the bathroom. I believe it's due to lack of fans in the bathroom. We were immediately given a different room which was good at that point. In the morning we noticed that we had visitors in our room, ANTS!. We were on the 10th floor and no food in the room. Parking was an extra $15/night . Only reason this hotel is average and not poor is because of the great employees.

My wife and I stayed in Intercon, SFO for 2 nights in early June 2012. It was quite a disappointing stay for the amount of money we paid for the hotel. There were no specific issues about the stay however we didn't feel any special. Pros - - Conveniently located close to all the major attractions - Decent room as expected from Intercon Cons - - Feels too businesslike - Receptionist and bell boys not the most friendly - Doesn't have the special feel of staying in a star property

Located in the heart of the waterfront. Walk to everything, little Italy, aquarium,restaurants, ball park. The good big suites, fridge,stove microwave and of course the location!!!! The bad swimming pool belongs to an Athletic club lots of restrictions and me with 3 kids under the age of 13. Really stunk Sunday morning open for club only swim class NO Hotel members till noon also closes at 9Pm.

I stayed there for 3 days. The hotel location is good. But this place is far from being a 5 star Ritz Carlton property! The lobby , the bar and the restaurant have a the most ugliest terrible decor I had ever seen in a 5 star hotel! Cheap look! The pool has no chez lounges , nobody gives you towels at all. Service was good. Food was averege. That is why i am giving them a two star.

We choose the hotel for the location – walking distance for a round trip in DC and some good restaurants in the area and for price -$ 100 per night. And these were ok, at least for one night that we spend here. The room is clean, but not at all cozy and is noisy. For breakfast we found a Starbucks in the neighborhood.

Good location for the pier areas, property was hard to unload into and the rooms had chipped paint in bath and a/c didn't work at all. Windows did not open and the blind would not go up the next morning. We stayed in room 370. Would probably look for a different hotel next trip.

This was the filthiest hotel I have ever stayed at. the staff was very unfriendly and not very helpful. I had read some reviews and quite frankly didn't believe them, because I have always had good experiences at Hiltons. I should've trusted the reviews. The only positive was that management did write to me apologizing for the event. Hopefully they will improve, because it could be a very beautiful hotel. The towels and sheets were stained and ripped.

Decided on a last minute Saturday night room in the District. Rate on Priceline was very low as were my expectations. Wow was I impressed! Rooms are brand new and very comfortable. Bar was hoppin', but the best attraction by far is the outdoor terrace. It's huge with seating arrangements and an outdoor fire pit. Bar service is available. Great way to spend the evening. We will look to the Hinckley Hilton the next time we need a room in DC.

Just spent the night here. Nice as well as convenient to the airport. There is a shuttle bus to the airport which takes about 10-15 mins. to get to. Dropped off the car at Budget, then took their shuttle bus back to the airport, then the Courtyard bus to the hotel. We had plenty of time so doing all that was not a problem, & it was something to do. The Courtyard bus will, if it's not real busy, swing by the rental car area pick you up & bring you to the hotel.

I stayed at this hotel last year and was very disappointed in the room maintenance and cleanliness. I corresponded with the general manager and got just the standard meaningless response. When I saw that the hotel had a new name, I decided to give it another try thinking they had new management. Boy was I fooled. Though the location and views are terrific and the reception staff welcoming, the room was horrible and just as worn and dirty as last year. I will never make this mistake again!

Extremely comfortable rooms and very well-trained staff. Beautiful lobby. The spa menu looked fantastic, though I didn't have any services. Dinner at Fearings was one of my best meals EVER. I think I could eat there for an entire month without tiring of the menu, the kind and knowledgeable servers and the view. In-room breakfast was speedy, yummy and well-executed. A wonderful hotel, as to be expected from a Ritz Carlton.

The staff was very pleasant however the hotel is old and dirty. had to change rooms 3 times; and each room was just as bad as the first. Carpets are dirty, stained and do not look like they have been vacuumed. The AC in the rooms does not cool properly and the AC in the hallways is off.

Stayed at the Melrose in October 2012. Enjoyed location and large room. As others have noted, room I had was a little banged up. For example, bi-fold door on closet was off of its track. Bathroom was small. Service was generally good, and people at the front desk were friendly. Housekeeping was good, but hotel lost points by not honoring my request to have my room cleaned in the mid-afternoon when I was out at a meeting. Location is convenient to George Washington University and to Georgetown.

Great stay at this nice hotel. As with other Drury Inn hotels, the staff are super friendly. Internet is fast. The free food and drinks are a nice addition. Room is clean. Note: for some reason, I could not enter the exact hotel address into my TomTom GPS but the longitude/latitude coordinates were printed on the confirmation page and could be used instead. Another note: bring earplugs which you can get at any hardware store when traveling just in case you get a noisy room by the highway - it's bound to happen sometimes !

For $50.00 you can't go wrong. The rooms were clean and everything work so I call that a win for the money. We got in late and check in was a fast as was the check out. Beds were good as was the shower.We ate a Denny's the next morning and their waitresses were GREAT!! My wife and I would stay here again.

This hotel was selected for me by the organizer of an event I was attending. My expectations were low. However, the location is fantastic and the room I had was quite large. Unfortunately, the mattress seemed to be foam, which I found uncomfortable. I also did not like the texture on the duvet. The lighting in the bathroom was awkward. I could not maintain an internet connection in my room. Finally, there was loud construction in the lobby, which were not notified of in advance.

The hotel is perfect for people with a short overnight or conducting a couple of days of business. It is connected to the terminals meaning it's not necessary to go outside or need transportation. Like all Marriotts it has all the travelers needs. If time permits there are some nice nice sightseeing trips available starting at the hotel.

My wife and I stayed at this hotel for 10 days during 2007 and thought we'd go back again this year. We were not very happy as the hotel was undergoing renovations. Our room was nothing compared to the one we occupied during our previous stay. It was small and the carpets were not very clean. The bed was comfortable. The location is good, near all the museums and within walking distance from Central Park. The service and food at the restaurant -Sarabeth was very good.

Good rates, relatively comfortable room, good access to highway, Seaworld, etc., but employees have minimal customer care training. Front desk continually paused our conversation at check-in to answer the phone; no pillow cases on any of the pillows; trash can at front door overflowing; and the front desk called our room by mistake at 2:30 in the morning. Plenty of other hotels to choose from in the area.

Two issues that tell you all you need to know about this hotel 1. Daily internet access 16.95 2. Mini bar empty - small bottle of mineral water 12.95. Told room service I would complain. "Do what you need to do". Possibly one of the worst hotels I have ever stayed in.

We stayed here New Years Eve, the city is just packed at this time, our room was a really good size with a big bathroom. Beds were pretty comfortable. We were hardly in the hotel at all. Our shower wasn't working, but they had maintenance up to fix it very quickly. It was just very average.

The Hilton Manhatten East is very clean, has a really nice bed, and it's close to Grand Central Station. We had a drinks in the bar, and although pricey (or maybe average for Manhatten), they were good. Hilton charges for WiFi, although there was a free AT&T WiFi signal. They also charge to print out airline boarding passes, so not freebees here.

As hotels go this was very pleasant yes the rooms are small but has a great location for all your needs and trips around We wasn't in the room that much just to sleep as we wanted to see as much as we could and found everything very easy to get to from here staff was very helpful and diner wasn't bad in there resturant Would go back

If you do not mind being on a seedy side street but in a decent hotel at a fair price then this is the place for you. The rooms were clean, beds comfortable, with double windows so very quiet. The bathrooms were adequate although hot water took about 5 minutes sometimes. People at the desk were very pleasant for New York.

I have been a guest of Staybrige on several occasion in the past few months. At each stay the staff are professional and have a smile on there face. The rooms are great the food is good both in the morning and evening. This location is close to what I need to do my job. Keep up the good work!!

I needed a place to stay for a while I was in the process of moving. The motel itself is somewhat close to downtown, but not exactly near much. The room had a weird odor and the bed wasn't that comfortable. I wouldn't necessarily say this is the worst experience I've ever had and if you're looking for something cheaper nearby downtown, you could try this place out. However, when considering everything I think it might have been better looking for another place even if it might have ended up costing a bit more.

Dream Downtown met all my expectations, it was fun and cool all the way through my stay. Eccellent staff and helpful, quick room service and all questions answered, not to forget the complimentary champagne. But this is the hotel to visit when you are in the "hip and cool mood" and looking for some fun and partylike environment.

Come on - Stains on the carpet and stains on the office chair? really???? all for the low price of $250 per night - what a bargain!! The lobby and conference area is fine. Everything else was disgusting and they should not be renting these rooms out for these rates. The reveiws here said to ask for a newly renovated room. The clerk told me they are all the same and recently renovated. Ha! Ha!

Classic modern, slightly worn hotel. My husband and 20 yo son and I stayed here one night while visiting family in Manhattan. The space was a bit cramped but not unusual for NYC standards. Staff were friendly and helpful, room was clean and bed comfortable. Nice view on 12th floor and quiet. Would recommend this for travelers looking for basic accomodations at an affordable price. The 96th street bus was convenient to get across town for activities on the West side.

We just returned from a 5-night stay at the Affinia Shelborne. We were pleasantly surprised by the size of the rooms. We had a one-bedroom suite and it was very roomy. Plenty of space for two adults and two boys! It a nice, quiet place close to Grand Central Station. My only critique is that we didn't find the concierge all that helpful. We ended up just figuring out everything ourselves. Internet is $13.95 per day, so we brought our own MiFi.

We stayed 3 nights at Jerry's Motel. As mentioned on previous reviews they were refurbishing some rooms upstairs and the workers started to work at 7:00 am ..... It was impossible to sleep given the racket they were making. No one mentioned it to us when we checked in. The rooms were Ok but definitely old (except the brand new Flat screen TV). The staff was very friendly, the location is great and the surrounding quiet ... and you get free parking. The free Wifi basically never worked and when it worked the signal was very poor.

Location cannot be any better, across the street the reading terminal market,a block away the convention center and a host of restaurants and bars. The rooms are a nice size and were cleand everyday,we stayed for three days and the hotel was clean with someone on hand to help. Will definetly be back.

Got this hotel at a great price ($110) a nice and for the room and location in Chicago that to mean was a steal. The front desk was super nice as well. We only stayed one night but the room was very clean and the bed was nice as well. You are super close the Miracle Mile, the Navy Pier, and the River. I would recommend this hotel again for anyone visiting downtown. One one downside was no fridge in the room.

We were not impressed. The room was small, the air conditioning very noisy, the staff behind reception were surly and were incapable of printing out our boarding passes despite several attempts and what is worst THEY CHARGE FOR INTERNET ACCESS. This is disgraceful and why dropped the rating from below average to terrible.

This is an average hotel in a fab location, we upgraded to a double double room as reading the reviews the beds are quite small, we had a good room on the 18th floor with 2 standard double beds & 2 bathrooms. The room was so quiet it was hard to believe you were in the centre of New York. We paid £479.00 for a 4 night break with Thomson in January 2012 - a bargain. Just a five minute walk from Times Square and many restaurants within walking distance. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

Fine if you are looking for a great location right near Times Square, a place to sleep, and don't care about amenities. The price is right and the sheets are small for the bed, but they are clean and actually crisp. No towel racks, but no bed-bugs either. Would not take fussy friends or family here, but it works well if all you need is a bed for a few hours of sleep.

A friend and I stayed for Thanksgiving week. We chose the location for easy access to Grand Central and cabs and were not disappointed. It was even a short walk to Macy's for Black Friday sales. It's a safe neighborhood with two excellent restaurants right across the street and many more nearby. A free substantial continental breakfast and free wifi in the rooms take the sting out of the rates.

This is pretty much a standard-issue Hampton Inn. It's got all the amenities of other Hampton Inns, but no more. Some of the Hampton Inns have little extras in the room. This one did not, but was certainly comfortable and very close to The Domain, which was convenient. Overall nice, quiet and workable.

The neighborhood was okay, but not very attractive,it wasn't that far to central park or rockeffeler center, and times square is very close. Very nice trendy hotel, music in the lobby seemed a little too loud, and it would get too crowded there. Spacious nice rooms, very good coffee in the morning, and very friendly room service staff as well as the morning front desk. Ana was very sincere and great with helping us organize our day. Overall great stay, a little too expensive but you can get a good deal.

Fairly average hotel - certainly not as exotic or special as other JW Marriott hotels. Rooms were not all that big and were a little old-fashioned in their decor. Beds were very comfortable, bathrooms were a little basic. Breakfast buffet was pleasant - again nothing earth shattering. Very handy for the Galleria mall opposite and the restaurants nearby

The hotel is small and cute, parking is free, nice breakfast and good WiFi and price is good if you are on a budget. The rooms are OK, but the bathroom need a serious updating. it's old, rusty, the water smell like rust, the tub faucet are not working properly at all, old TV, i cannot imagine that in 2012 3 stars hotels still have old boxes TV.

No regular coffee in room (all 3 days). No soap in room (one day). Room not made up (one day). Internet not working (one day - not hurricane related but needed to be able to check flight status). Maids need a checklist and need to be held to it. Shouldn't need to complain about missing coffee 3 days in a row.

Decent location, but I don't suggest wandering around after dark! The neighborhood is sketch, the hotel is okay. Stayed in a room with two twins. The bed was stiff and you could feel ever spring. The bathroom was attached a private which is rare for this price of a hotel in San Francisco. The room faced the road and was loud during the day, but quieted down at night thankfully. I only suggest this if you need a cheap hotel with parking in the city!

After having had very positive experiences in Kimpton Hotels, my expectations were high...but I was disappointed. The location is excellent, within walking distance of North End attractions, Faneuil Hall and the waterfront, and the rooms are nicely enough appointed. Yet beyond that, there is nothing about this hotel that warrants a $395/night (not including breakfast) price tag.

On arrival, I checked my room top-to-bottom for bedbugs and didn't find any, a miracle for a Seattle hotel. I did a follow-up check of every item that I brought home and nothing. I can overlook all the small stuff because I've heard of many stories of bugs and hotels that handle the situation poorly.

Hotel was just what we wanted...a small boutique hotel in a great location. Service was good, staff was efficient, helpful and the price was right! Only complaint, and reason I did not give it five stars, is the rooms could be a little bigger and a little better maintained. The fixtures in the bathroom were falling apart. However, it was clean and the beds were great.

I travel very often to San Diego and this hotel is the worst I've experienced. To start, there were bed bugs in my room. Service at the bar/restaurant was awful, you'll be lucky to see a barman behind the bar. Staff was not very friendly, in one occasion I needed to break a couple of dollars for the washing machine and they were only able to find 4 quarters as there was no change in the bar. There is only one washing machine for guests, which is not ideal when you are on a long stay. Very poor overall.

we went to this hotel from las vegas for our 40 wedding anniversary all though staff was friendly this hotel needs up dating carpet in my shed is cleaner looks as bleach has been dropped on it in places blinds in room very dirty and did not fit right did not take clothes out of case as did not feel the wardrobe was fit to hang anything stayed out as late as possible so we could just close are eyes and not see anything bathroom door would not shut good point towels and sheets changed every day thank goodness

We went as a family. They had ants everywhere. Did not have nothing near by to order from. My son had a accident in the bed. And they did not even have extra bed clothes to give us. ... I WILL NEVER STAY THERE AGAIN. IT WAS THE WORST PLACE I HAVE EVER STAYED AT. ..

It was the least expensive (parking incl) accommodation just about in all of SF when I stayed there, due to the America's Cup Sailing Race. Beds were comfy minus headboards, artwork, mirrors, coat hooks, any sort of hook to hang a shirt, towel, bathrobe, purse, it I felt it was a clean neighborhood establishment. I was able to park the car in the lot several hours before check-in time which balances out standing in the hallway 30 minutes after 'check-in' time watching the maids finish making the beds and vacuuming our room.

Another very pleasant stay.We visit two times a year and are always very pleased with our room,but most importantly the hospitality.Victor at the front desk makes us feel more like family than guests he always has time to spend making us feel welcome no matter how busy it is. If more hotels hired people like Victor trveling away from home would not be unpleasant.Everyone else are also very accomodating and the rooms are very clean and fresh.Also plenty of food choices nearby.Staying again in October. Again props to Victor and the entire staff

This hotel is located right in the center of historic Philadelphia. The room was large and quiet. It was fun to walk from the hotel to Rittenhouse Square. If you have not been to Philadelphia in awhile, the downtown area is much more energetic. The breakfast in the adjoining restaurant was good and convenient.

We found The Casablanca Hotel by looking on tripadvisor and were so happy - It lived up to all the excellent reviews. There was nothing to fault - the staff were friendly and helpful, the rooms were clean and the service provided by everyone was first class. The complimentary breakfast and cheese and wine every evening just added to the Casablanca being a memorable place to stay in New York. In addition, is the location, just round the corner from Times square - just perfect. I will certainly recommend the hotel to friends and family. Tricia W

Most SpringHill Suites are similar but some are a bit better than others. This was an average location - good service, clean room and free Wifi, parking and breakfast. No complaints and service was good. Some of the newer SpringHill have two TVs and a bit more modern. Only a slight disadvantage to this property. Ate at Zapatas Mexican which was very good near the Hilton.

The lobby of this hotel is great, but the room are old and in great need of a major renovation. Great flat screen TV, but the channels are limited. Parking spaces are much to narrow even for my compact car. The worst thing about my stay is that they make you give them a $100 deposit on your credit card, but I still have not recieved my $100 back on my credit card. It's been eight buisness days since I stayed there, and desite repeated calls to the hotel, the $100 has not been refunded. VERY dishonest. Buyer beware!!

Perfectly located with the harbor on one side and downtown Boston on the other. Lots of sights within walking distance. The hop on tour busses stop right around the corner, the metro has a stop right outside the front door. The rooms are very spacious and very clean. Modern bathroom. Alamo/National have their office just a few blocks away so very easy to pick up or drop off your rental car. I'd stay here again for sure.

Although the motel was renovating the rooms, we ended up in a room that had not been redone yet. No towel racks, all the security locks on the door were broken, and there were a couple of large stains on the carpet. The linens and beds were quite nice. I was glad we were only staying one night. The room rate was unacceptable for the quality of the room.

Great location. Big impersonal Hotel. We were on 8th floor. Stayed 3 nights. Our room never got cleaned before 1.30pm even though we were out at 9am and only then when we complained. it was hard to sleep at night because it was very noisy outside after midnight . Wifi was very poor,hardly any signal !

We had a nice weekend in DC. Here are the pros: big room, comfy beds, nice breakfast, good location, good pool, lots of families, fish to feed, flat screens. Here are the cons: it is a little old in place - rusted fixture in bathroom, old dirty tub, missing a whole set of drapes in bedroom so we were up at the crack of dawn. But overall a good place and would return to an embassy suites again. Good value.

The lobby is nice and that is the only thing that is nice. Rooms are small, dark and dirty. Bathroom tiles are all cracked and very old. Bed linens look like they haven't been changed in 30 years. You have to pay to check your luggage. Elevators are dark and frequently broken or stalled. I do not recommend staying here at all.

This has to be on purpose. I'm sure they don't want you watching movies on the Internet instead of buying theirs, but I purposely booked this hotel because we had no power in our home and I desperately needed in connection to upload files and a little AC. The AC is nice, but my PING 117 ms, download is 0.70 Mbps and upload is 0.07 Mbps. If I could find a dial up connection it would be faster.

This Hotel was amazing!!! I believe it is there flagship location, and service is top notch. Parking is kinda hard, and the lot was full when we got there at 1pm on Saturday...but we did Valet parking regardless. Valet parking is $40 plus tax a nice, but all the drivers were very professional. The location is amazing also, and very close to all downtown sites and attractions. The monuments are a little bit farther away, but White House, Museums, ect are really close. I will be staying here again my next trip into D.C.

If your choices come down to a park bench or The Intown Suites, go with the park bench. Worst management and customer service (which there is none) you will ever experience. Everything is broken, elevator, laundry, security door.Housekeeping doesn't clean when they are supposed to. If you don't smoke and enjoy your room smelling of an ashtray, you will love this place. This company has no idea they are in the hospitality industry. They must purposefully seek out the least qualified people they can find and let them loose. Really, stay away, no run away.

A few minor things that I found to be a bit of a disappointment, but not so much that I wouldn't stay there again. Checked in late evening about midnight and there was nobody at the front desk to check me in. Had to wait quite awhile till someone came back as they were probably doing another task. Same exact issue at checkout as nobody was there to check me out. My wakeup call was late as well.

This hotel is in a perfect location. Park you car and forget about it, you can walk to everything that's great about this city. Try Paisano's right around the corner. Casual Italian that serves up big bowls of pasta that will definitely fill you up. The entire staff at The Talbott is wonderful!!

Stayed one night after a very long flight back to the States. Traffic, both cars and people walking, is incredible in this area. Hotel was clean and great view. Staff at front desk were just OK. Did not go out of their way to provide information. The view is incredible and subway station very close to front entrance of hotel.

This is a beautiful property. The friendly staff and the sleeping rooms are simply outstanding. The pool on the roof and sauna were perfect, drinks in the evening and made to order breakfast. Top all this off the Chef Gregory left us with joy and a wonderfully full belly. Kudos Chef Gregory I really hope you get this!

The beds squeaked with every breath I took. Thank goodness there were not any newlyweds rooming next to us. The beds were high and difficult to get into (and I am 6 ft tall). The rooms were very small and the bathrooms even smaller. We also had a meal as part of our conference and the pitcher of milk was sour. Not very good quality food at all. Will avoid staying at this hotel in the future. TIme for the wrecking ball.

The good things about this place is that : 1. It is only a few blocks from the Transport 2. Near eating areas 3. Close to hop on and hop off sightseeing bus stop The downside is: 1. Noisy rooms - you can hear the background noise from the airconditioning/ventilation machines from nearby buildings on the rooftop

This hotel had a great location, but you can do much better for the money. The hallways smelled of smoke, dirty elevators, furniture in the lobby was thread bare. The staff was very helpful. The room was large, bed comfortable but the room was so musty and old smoke lingered. If you have any allergies don't stay here!

Just got back from a wonderful weekend at the Palomar. We booked a one bedroom suite so our teenaged daughter could stay with us. We arrived at the hotel to find a fire truck outside as someone had pulled a fire alarm but the valet attendant welcomed us and we were in the hotel very easily. The rooms are clean and comfortable and we enjoyed our stay. There is a great wine reception every evening and coffee every morning. It's a wonderful location in the heart of Philadelphia.

I'm at the Hilton Garden Inn now. I am staying here only because it was the preferred hotel for the event I am attending. The facility is okay, though it is showing signs of age. The service, though, is disappointing. Hotel staff forget to follow-up on things, don't greet guests when they meet them in the hallway, don't pick up leftover room service articles from the hallways in a timely manner, etc. etc. There are no major issues, but many minor ones. The good news for the hotel: if they retrained their staff, they could fix most of it.

Under construction, no hot water Saturday or Sunday morning, and worst of all, the front desk was completely unconcerned. Also, be sure to check your bill because they did not charge us rates per our Priceline reservation. We had to stand in line over 15 minutes to speak to someone and then they made the change to our bill. Our room was clean and nice enough, but all in all, not a good hotel experience.

Hotel smelled like cigarettes/guests stood right outside entrance to smoke...blowing smoke around the entrance door and covered area. I was advised that it was a nonsmoking facility, however, two men smoked in my hallway while they stood outside their room and talked loudly using filthy language. Children ran yelling all over the hotel unsupervised. One spilled a drink in my hallway and tossed his trash on the floor.

The reason I consider it "average" is because it's not as good value when compared to a similar brand just a couple of blocks away (Hampton Inn). While everything here is adequate, breakfast is not included in the price, and the room (including bath) is not as welll appointed. Having said this, it would still be on top of my list to consider for the Soho area (depending on how competitive the rates are). This is a good base for Soho, Little Italy, the Village, etc.

Eilan Hotel Resort and Spa is the premier place to stay in San Antonio. Even though your in the middle of the city the ambiance of the atmosphere and the hotel remind me of my stays in Europe. Rooms are so detailed and the amenities in the room make your stay more comfortable.The Sustenio restaurant is an absolute must if you are staying at the hotel, or even for a special night out.. G

We stayed here over T-Giving weekend. Love the location, right on the river with a short walk to Old Town, which we liked, but far enough to not be right in the thick of it, which can sometimes get annoying. Overall Philly is a smaller city, so getting anywhere in the downtown are doesn't take too long. The room was really nice and modern. Ask for a corner room so you get both city and river views. Over all, it's a good place to stay. Nothing amazing, but for a weekend in Philly it worked quite well for us.

This motel is very small and certainly not as expnsive as others nearby. The location was convenient for us and it's relatively quiet and clean, but the decor is dark and dreary. Feels dated.The bed would have been comfortable if the sheets and matrass pad had fit the bed properly. Jerry, the owner was very nice and frindly. It's a no frills place and you get what you pay for.

We have stayed here numerous times, and always have had a great experience. This time we had the room with the kitchenette, not that we planned to cook, but was nice to warm up soup and what not. Staff is friendly, and helpfull. Beds are very comfortable, and our room was spacious. Good location, close to almost everywhere you want to go, Sea World, Coronado, Old Tow, The Zoo, you name it, you are about 10 min away.

We traveled to San Antonio for a band contest, so no surprise that a band was also guests at the hotel. When we got in the room, we discovered we were surrounded by band students, so we asked to change rooms. The staff was very accommodating and quickly found us another room. The second room was peacefully quiet and away from the very excited students! Room was spacious, although corner vanity in bathroom was a little small. Hot breakfast was good; typical for this price range. Usually hotels of this caliber don't charge for parking, but this one does.

This hotel offers two different settings one for guests on business and one for rest, I requested to be changed to a type of room where I was going to rest. Both nights I could hear people talking loudly in the hallways and the last night I had to call security at 3am because some guests were running naked and making noise in the hallways. The bed was no comfortable and the a/c does not work properly.

I spend At leAst 3 night A week At this location . the rooms Are AlwAys cleAn And smells fresh. the beds Are even better. flAt screen with mAny chAnnels. full breAkfAst the works from 5Am TO 9:30Am sAusAge, eggs, All types of breAd And muffins. mAke your own wAffles And choose mike, juices And mAny different types of teAs And fruits. cAn"t sAy enough About it . wAsher And dryer if needed hot tube, exercise room And A nice cleAn pool. Security cAmerAs Always A Plus. give it All A"s

We stayed here 6 months ago and had a restful stay. This trip the room was so foul smelling got about 4 hours sleep. Wound up leaving the window open with the heater on all night. The breakfast was also very skimpy vs. our previous visit. Looks like business is picking up, so they don't need our business anymore. Will never stay here again!

Hi. We liked the hotel. The price was right. Nice room, but to hot so we had troubles sleeping. We couldn't get the temperature down. The AC work but not hard enough. The other thing that didn't work was our request to get a glutenfree breakfast. We specificly ask about it in an email before we arived. That's a pitty. Now we had to buy our own bread and take it to the breakfastlounge. But otherwise, we loved our stay in New York and we will come back!

This downtown hotel is in close walking distance of the COBO Center and other downtown attractions. Friendly staff, comfortable rooms, good hot breakfast daily and a separate bar/restaurant next door, (Big City Grille) Too many smokers allowed at the entrance of the hotel makes a bad impression. Television stations did not match the in-room guide so you surf the channels forever to find your desired show. Overall, a worthwhile hotel when staying in downtown Detroit.

I really enjoyed my stay at the W Chicago-City Center! The hotel has great decor all around and is in a great location, close to the L. And my king room was very comfortable. Staff was fantastic and extremely accommodating. Eden, the hotel concierge, was extremely gracious and offered up fantastic dinner recommendations that were definitely right on point! I enjoy dining out in the city at local restaurants and I was very happy with what Eden suggested.

Rooms were clean, bed comfortable -- they are small rooms no air conditioning, limited air flow via windows- reminded me of staying in Europe. The front desk folks were OUTSTANDING -- Their breakfast was a bit disappointing as we were expecting an area to eat together -- had to pick up some fruit and pastry and eat in our room.

My daughter who lives in Virginia planned a Birthday Celebration at Aloft in Harlem, New York. My daughter lives in Virginia, and I live in Arizona, dispite the distances and the different states the staff helped Jamie plan a wonderful Celebration for me. They treated me like a Queen and treated my guests like royalty, I would do it again. Bunnyhere153

Stayed one night to shop. This is a Condo unit the owners lease/rent the rooms out. Not impressed with the stains on the carpet, peeling wallpaper, stains on bed, no free WiFi". It was so hot in the room, had to wait a long time for elevator (which could hold no more then 4 people at a time!) This is NOT a 4 star hotel... more like a 2 star. Go to the Hilton across the street it's much nicer at a lower price!

1) Did not stand by price confirmed online registration 2) the night i checked in thursday 12/14/12. The manager on duty was extremely rude and disrespectful 3) upon check out when again questioned the price discrepancy of what I had in hand confirmation and what was charged I was unable to get a reasonable explanation they ignored me had me wait for15minutes and no manager came to me I had to leave to attend my forum. 4) I will not return nor reccommend the New Yorker to anyone Elizabeth J Wilson

My company booked me 2 nights at the Madison due to hurricane Sandy. The room was comfortable, bright, and warm with all the amenities you can think of. Especially the complimentary Keurig coffee in the room; it was a nice touch. The property has been recently remodeled and is completely spotless. Perfectly clean, perfect location, perfect stay. I will definitely recommend The Madison to all of my friends and colleagues.

The good points are that it is easy on/off from the freeway, it basically centrally located, under $110/night and the bed was comfrotable with clean sheets and there is free parking.The downside was the the room was in pretty bad repair, the bathroom had mold on the walls and ceiling with metal fixtures rusted and the exterior door required a lot of monkeying with to get it to lock.

I booked this hotel using my Wyndham Reward points and was very happy with it because I saved well over $100 on a particular Saturday night when most other hotels were charging a lot as the city was busy. We got a massive room with two separate double beds, spacious shower - with two tiny frosted windows overlooking an internal shaft. It would have been very depressing to stay there for longer than just the one night. The room was clean, however, and the bathroom a very good standard. The location is quite central with restaurants and convenience stores nearby.

The Redbury needs to decide if it’s a nightclub or a hotel. My room looked onto a pretty courtyard, which at night became a seething nightclub with music pumping until 2 AM. I had read the reviews, but nothing made it clear that there is no escape from the noise. I was in LA for work, so who cares if the rooms are charming if you can’t get any sleep? There are plenty of hotels in LA and if part of your travel plan includes sleeping at night, I recommend you choose one of the others.

The hotel was great. We stayed for three nights and didn't have a single complaint. While the room was small, it was clean and cheerful. We didn't hear a sound from inside our room ever. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. I'd stay there again in a heartbeat.

Two days after my visit I saw a $118 charge on my credit card. I was charged for alcohol from the mini bar that I did not drink. The biggest complaint was that I paid the valet $60 cash for my car and I was charged for it again on my credit card. I found out the valet are not suppose to accept cash due to the automatic billing of the credit card. I ended up paying $105 for the valet parking my car one time.

I recently spent two nights at this hotel. The room was clean and reasonably comfortable. The hotel has a coffee shop, which is located near its restaurant. I wish the coffee shop had longer hours. The staff at the hotel was friendly and although the valet parking was a little pricey, the service was great. The hotel is located right near the water and has awesome views; we stayed on the 20th floor. It is also conveniently located -- it is not far from the downtown stores and restaurants. I wouldn't mind returning.

First thing I noticed was the musty odor when the door was opened to the room. We left the window open while the air conditioning was on, which helped. The "wall" dividing the bathroom from the beds was a semi see-thru mesh on both sides of the mirror. This would be fine for couples but odd if you are accompanied by children. Lighting was not the best. beds were comfortable. Not worth the$390/nite rate. The Bliss products were a nice touch.

The only reason this hotel gets a three is because of the front desk girl Sharee. She was very friendly and helpful. Other then that no remote, room dirty, the guy at check out was rude and had on basketball shorts. This place needs to be seriously updates. Keep your front desk girl it is ALL you all have.

The hotel is acceptable. Remember, this is La Quinta, not the Ritz. It feels safe, which is important to me. Room needs updating, tile is cracked, closet door doesn’t open quite right, but the room is clean. Internet went down tonight, which is a big problem for me. Front desk has been fantastic. You are centrally located, very close to Galleria and about 100 awesome restaurants – but this is not a fine hotel, it’s a hotel that needs renovating, has a few glitches, but if you can deal with that is a good value.

I booked this hotel at the last minute, concerned (as a single female) about the 2 stars, but reassured by booking.com's 'preferred' status. I was pleaseantly surprised - the front desk service was friendly and helpful-called me by my first name & I felt welcomed. Sure it's an older hotel but the bathroom was nice and clean, the bed comfortable - both fresh smelling - and the room overall good.. With new carpeting (and more vacuuming) it would be 3 stars. Will stay again.

First the good...the staff here is very friendly and make you feel welcome. The rooms are good but the bathrooms need a bit of an update. Excellent location. Excellent food and beverages. Now the not so good....Despite making two clear requests at two seperate times the staff AND management totally ignored my reservation requesting a king size bed. The parking fee here is very very high.

The facility is run down and shabby. More importantly, the staff are not just rude but overtly hostile. The reasons to stay here would be the rate and location. Just use a discount booking website and get the same rate and location (or actually better location) at a nicer place. Besides, these people should not be encouraged. At the very least customers should be able to expect common courtesy even if they are staying at a fleabag flop house.

I had heard so much about the hilton bayfront that I couldn't wait to stay there. At $250 a night, I was disappointed....it was an ordinary hotel room...no fridge...$3.75 for a bottle of water...$27 a night for parking $14 a night for wi-fi. It was not a bad hotel....just way overpriced.

It's almost amusing how bad my stay here has been. The walls are paper thin, not helped by the 1 inch gap under my door to the hallway. I literally have a few of a brick wall about 8 inches from my window. The plug in the bathroom doesn't work and they didn't even clean my room today. Horrible, just horrible. The location is great but there are many other hotels in the area that you should choose. Probably the worst hotel I have ever stayed in.

My mom and I stayed here for 4 nights last month in a "deluxe" king room and found it to be vastly overpriced. Based on the description, we thought we would have a view of the lake but from the 3rd floor, you only see the park. The room was rather small and the bath tiny. My mom's side of the bed was uncomfortable, the windows were dirty and the bedside lights were not bright enough for reading. That said, the staff were all very friendly and helpful.

We spent one night in early October and found the small room to be: dated, stifling, a fake window (best of my memory), thus, not a pleasant room to relax. The staff person who came to turned down the bed was friendly and pleasant. Our room was next to the elevator which kept us up. Positives are: walking distance to many locations and complimentary coffee and fruits in the morning. Valet parking is $40 per night. Overall I do not recommend staying except if you need a place to sleep and to be downtown.

Great location & clean rooms & to top it up the famous La famiglia Pizza is right outside the hotel, the only thing i did not like was the bathroom door. but will recommend during my stay it was priced at $185. this was in June 2012 will be back :)

The hotel needs some massive renovations. The only reason why I stayed at your facility was due to all of the hotels being booked up for the Austin City Limits 3 day music event. My stay was my first and last time I will stay at a Baymont. I will say this- The gentleman at the front desk on the evening of Saturday, October 13 was very nice and helpful.

My family met relatives in San Antonio for the labor day weekend at the last minute. The hotel was clean but check-in was very slow and check-out even slower. Lots of dirty dishes in the hallways and the elevators are extremely slow. Final price a little over $100 a night after Hotwire discounts. Never could get the wireless Internet to work.

I was in town for a conference and several area hotels were holding blocks of rooms. The Drury offered the least expensive rate. I did not realize that included in the rate was breakfast, afternoon popcorn and soft drinks and in the evening heavy snacks/dinner and drinks. The food offered in the evening was not fancy but you could certainly make dinner of it if you chose to. The conference I was attending provided meals so I did not try the food but they were busy every evening. The staff was super nice and helpful.

We were here foir two nights. I thought it would be more upsucale. The room was small but even worse the A/C was very noisy. The staff was very helpful but they ripped me $23 per night on the rate (didn't keep confirmation-my bad). The location is pretty good, near the T and restaurants I just wish it was better for $300 a night.

Was the first time we stayed there. As we saw the front and the inside we thought it was ok, but when we got into our rooms, OMG! The air vent was hanging off its hinges, the bathroom had mold and the shower was disgusting. The only good thing was the breakfast and that was the only good thing. The night staff at the front desk were rude. Never again will I stay there.

Every employee of this hotel made sure that we were happy we chose The New Yorker. Of special note was the gentleman who checked us in. We had a small problem with our room and he went beyond what was expected to remedy the situation including calling housekeeping immediately. Housekeeping did help us immediately and was courteous and thoughtful. Good customer service is getting more and more difficult to find, that is why my family and I seek out those businesses that provide the best service. We will be returning to this hotel on every NYC visit.

The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful! Even a quick encounter in the elevator with a member fo the cleaning staff was friendly! However, the hotel itself is in serious need of work. The free breakfast is depressing - located in a basement and very bare. It almost felt like a prison meal. The rooms are very small with beds that are hard/uncomfortable. The worst part was the noise! The pipes were squealing and banging in the walls when the people above me were taking a shower.

I've stayed at the Standard Hotel several times now and always had a great stay. The rooms are really nice and comfortable. And if you get the south side of the hotel the view is amazing! The restaurant and bars are great too, and love the neighborhood. The only thing that would be nice is if hotel guests would be allowed to stay in the upstairs bar past 10:30PM... I guess it turns into a private club then and everyone is kicked out?

Convenient location if you are looking for a historical perspective on the nation's background. The Liberty Bell, Betsy Ross House and U.S. Mint are within minutes of a walk. But if you are looking for a hotel that offers you quality service, amenities and a place to relax and put your head down, look elsewhere. Moreover, the price is far too expensive given the lack of quality rooms and amenities.The rooms are very small, cramped and outdated.

called to check why my room was not serviced. He was very rude "what do you want?" "give me a break! I just got here!" - these were his replies. Asked why my room was not serviced and he got very angry. My bathtub drain is blocked. Paying $220/night for this S@!# hotel.

The suites are big in space but are old and outdated. It feels you are in an 80's room, the bathroom is dark and mine did not have a tub, a lot of water went running out to the outside. For the money I don't recommend it, plus add the $14/day for self-parking and the slow free internet. This hotel would be great after a total renovation since all rooms are suites but until then stay next door at the Intercontinental or Marriott.

I drove up and was like hmmmm???? I went in and was like mmmmmmm? I paid for my rooom opened the door and RANNNNNNNNN back for a refund,,,,,,,, True Story smh The manager even tried to upgrade the room it was just absolutelt scarry. I though that I was going to have to call the authorities if I didn't get a refund. He hated it but he knew why. I would never go back there.

From beginning to end, the time spent at the Seaport made us feel like aristocrats! Staff were amazing and very accommodating, room was beautiful! Have a view of Boston Harbour which made getting up in the morning to attend a conference across the street at the World Trade Centre something to look forward to. Top class!

We have stayed at this hotel several times. It used to be a great place to stay. The price was reasonable; however, definitely not worth it. When we arrived, we noticed that the linens were not clean. There was mascara on one of the pillowcases. There was a hair in the coffeepot in the bedroom. The ice bucket had been filled, yet, one of the glasses on the tray had lip marks on it. No impressed at all!!!!!!!!

This hotel is simple but has everything you need, simple breakfast can be bought in the lobby, the rooms are not too big but well organized, the staff is very friendly and helpfull( they arranged our tickets for the SD padres game) and the allow smoking at your balcony as long as nobody is bothered by that. Location at the beach, unobstructed views...Would defenitely come back

My first Fairmont experience and it was just as I had hoped. The service is top notch and the rooms are large and modern. We went to the gold building and that gave us access to complimentary beverages and hor'douerves. The view of the sunrise over the harbor was spectacular. Out new getaway Boston hotel. Love it!

The accomodations in the room itself are very nice -- comfortable desk, chair and bed -- but it's impossible to get any sleep if you're staying anywhere near the 6th floor where I was. The restaurant/bar in the lobby turns into a nightclub at night. Asked the front desk twice if anything could be done about the music but nothing could be done. Passed my complaint on to the front desk upon check out and got very little sympathy.

Avoid this hotel product if you can stay somewhere else. They are not service oriented. The room has a comfortable bed, and some OK furnishings, however so does some lesser products. Their staff lacks Disney training. Telephone at bedside did not work. Refrigerator was empty and did not work. Their were no snacks in the room. No shower cap even upon request. I had to call and ask for the manager to get my concerns addressed. They are not ready for prime time. Not worth the money. Location stinks.

The room was very average in term of style and decor. The bathroom not very big. The location is not very convenient for week end. There is nothing around the hotel, no cafe, no restaurant, no bar. The shopping area is far away and the Pier also. In the lobby there hot apple joice throughout the day which is delicious.

Checked in early evening. Hotel is slightly runed down, not too clean rooms, but we were tired and only were staying one night. Bed linens were frayed, but appeared clean. The day after I got home, I found seven large clusters of bed bug bites on my upper back, shoulder area. Sent an email to the hotel administration, but never got any response.

the location is perfect less than 100 meter from timesqure the rooms small and very dark the floor is noisey the internet cost 10$ a day when i got the room the toilet was stuck and it took almost an hour to send someone to fix it the tv is great they have many chanels

Nice location. Tiny parking garage for free in the back. Walking distance to yummy restaurants. They either have "heat" or "A/C" on at one time in the hotel. So, if you like to sleep cool, but it is cool outside, they put the heat on. Their reaction: Open the windows!!! LOL!!!! What an adventure!! Tip: Book from the hotel directly and you will save. It's a safe area for kids, families, or people traveling alone. The metro is across a couple of streets.

Excellent location for visiting NYC. Close to trains, Times Sq and easy walk to other shopping. King room was decent size, no coffee in room but adequate bathroom and actually a decent view from 38th floor. TV reception was not the greatest but a decent selection of channels was available. Staff was okay, I was able to check-in early. I would stay there again.

My wife and I stayed here for 3 nights -- Sat, Sun, Mon -- and paid a total of about $500 including taxes, which I thought was a very good rate. Of course this is not a Ritz Carlton, but the hotel more than met our expectations. There was a pleasant small lobby with free Starbucks coffee, 3 computers with internet connections, and the room was very nice, comfortable, and well equipped (including a substantial amount of drawer space). I would definitely stay here again and recommend it to others.

The restraunt next door was of very poor quality. Wait staff was slow and made errors in orders with kitchen staff. It took a long time for food to be prepared. The New York strip was tough and under seasoned. Food was bland, pie crusts heavy. I will never eat there again.

We have stayed in this Hawthorn suites before and the staff were nice enough, but the hotel itself in showing signs of age. Beds were soft and lumpy-pillows too soft. Bathtub was clean, but in need of repair. Room requirement is to leave any used dishes-silverware clean or additional charge would be incurred, however, eventhough we did not use the range, the glass top still had food remenants on it. Apparently housekeeping does not clean the entire room every time guests leave.

The room is tiny and reminds me of the European hotels in that regard. It was clean for the most part although my toilet had tissue in it from someone else's stay so I'm not sure if the toilet was cleaned. The internet worked well. The location was ok - but not close to many trains.

This was my first trip to SF. I got lucky and stayed here at the Baldwin Hotel for one night. The room was nice, clean, and cozy. It was at a great location too, walking distance to public transportation, shops, and eateries. When I come back, I'll be sure to stay here again.

The people are lovely. The rooms are pleasant enough. But the elevators without buttons make no sense whatsoever. They claim they are set up for efficiency, but the opposite is true. I almost forgot. You must bring your own laptop since Fedex/Kinko charges 40 cents per minute. Also, don't consider printing anything on their printers unless you are prepared to pat 59 cents a page.

I stayed with my boyfriend, we were there to see a Giants Game. The only thing I liked about it was that it was closed to the buses, Walgreens and Round Table Pizza. It's not a place it you want to get a goods nights rest, all night you could hear sirens, people yelling, car alarms, people's foot sets above you, and the bed was not that comfortable; I did not sleep at all. Even though it was just us two, the room felt very tiny.

The staff are friendly and helpful the hotel is old and dirty. Had throw pillows for pillows and the carpet was stained and disgusting. The carpet was wet all the time from humidity. I Wifi didn't work 90%of the time had to keep logging in Other hotels in the area are within $10 dollars and much better. Staff are great.

We booked our reservation about a week out from our visit. The pool area was under construction. There were not even any chairs to sit on and garbage was piled up by the pool. At check out I complained that on our 3 day visit to San Diego the pool was under construction and no warning at booking or check in. I got a "soooooorry." We purchased two new swimsuits which were taken from our room. We are waiting to see how the hotel will resolve this.

Being a first time visitor to New York it was all overwhelming to me but doormen were fantastic helping with bags and flagging taxis for me. Desk staff weren't as friendly though so I avoided asking questions. Location of hotel was great with a starbucks just around the corner - convenient since no coffee making facilities in hotel. Room was very comfortable with desk, lounge and second tv just inside door. The whole place was always imaculate.

I agree with what many others have said - too many little things to itemize, but obviously persistent and repeated problems. Unable to check in on time, low water pressure, non-working televisions, runaround on trying to resolve problems. Rooftop bar has nice view - not the best, just nice, but very overpriced & no amenities like other upscale bars offer. Not worth the money & management does nothing to help resolve problems. I'll take my business elsewhere next visit.

I've stayed at BW Airport Executel a number of times and it has always been an excellent experience, made possible by the special staff that can't seem to smile too much or be helpful enough when needed. This last stay was a bit different because the hotel was involved in some structural alterations. Despite a bit of confusion the staff kept everyone informed and the hotel functioning as normally as possible Two people stood out: Terry, at the front desk, and Jim the shuttle driver to just about anywhere. I am looking forward to my visit next year.

Very nice resort! Pools & lazy river are amazing and poolside wait staff were very attentive! Was disappointed on how early they shut down the lazy river & slide and then lock the pool down @ 10 pm with no alternatives for quiet evening swim or jacuzzi. Rooms & restaurants were comfortable. Would like the rooms better if they offered two queen beds instead of two full beds. Communication of events could also be better as we weren't informed of family/kid events when we checked in and missed some fun for the kids.

The room was nice, but the service was horrendous: unresponsive, slow, and misleading. It took more than two hours to just get a package (which we shipped prior to arriving) from the front desk. The wi-fi was NOT free in each individual room and cost $10.99/24 hrs, but it did not specify that it was charged on a device basis until you opened second device. A really distasteful way to trick guests into paying extra more.

This hotel is located in a perfect spot with quick access to the Red Line. I was shocked to find they didn't have flat screen tvs in the rooms, the valet parking next door was slow and tried to overcharge me when I went to leave. Late night front desk staff were less than accomodating. I am undecided on whether I would stay here again or not.

My wife and I stayed at The Ritz at Battery Park for the third time recently. As before, we payed the extra for a room with Club access. This is not a cheap option but worth every penny. The team there are superb: professional, attentive and always friendly. The food and drink are excellent is the ambience - truly great. Add this to the hotel's superb location means , in my view, this is the best hotel on Manhattan!

We stayed here for one night to tour UPenn and I was very impressed. The rooms were very new and spacious. They gave us an iPad for the room which we found very neat and since I am a Hilton Honours member, we got free wifi and a free breakfast which was excellent. There was an omelette station , granola, fresh fruit and more. We ate at the sushi restaurant located right outside of the hotel which was very good. I would certainly stay here again if I ever visit UPenn again.

It is an old building that has not been maintained. The "passenger" elevator says it is a freight elevator and should NOT be used as a passenger elevator. It smells terrible, the rooms are small and dirty. Shared bathrooms that do not seem to be cleaned regularly. The bed was awful and the noise unbearable. I didn't get more than 1 hour of sleep at a time. I was booked for 2 nights but I changed hotels after the first night.

The hotel is perfectly located, across from Carnegie Hall, few blocks from Central Park and Times Square. Stayed in room with 2 doubles on 10th floor (1020)....room small. Door did not close entirely. Housekeeping carts left in hallway at all times. Elevator VERY slow at peak times - waited 15 minutes at checkout time. Heating/cooling unit noisy and lacked heat when we needed it. No coffeemaker or fridge. Toiletries were high quality. Rates are competitive, but you get what you pay for. Will not return.

The room stink and the clim didn't work hard enough...so it makes the room very humid. They need to do a good clean up because the were old dust behind the furniture and in the bathroom. Also it was impossible for the kid to flush down the toilet... We reserved for 4 persons and every day I had to call to have 4 towels. The only good thing...pool and location. The breakfast was uneatable...kids didn't like it at all. Not expensive.

Very disapointed in this Hilton property. While the location to San Jose airport can't be beat, the property is dirty and dumpy. The parking lot had garbage everywhere. My room had old carpet and mismatched furniture. The front desk staff was hurried and not very welcoming. No cookies, even to make that process sweeter...I would stay here again if, and only if, I had to be that close to the San Jose airport.

The hotel was very nice inside and out. The lobby was quaint and offered nice seating. The room was comfortable and clean. The bathroom was clean and had all essentials. That bar and restaurant were nice with good selections on the menus. The pricing was fair and reasonable. At Breakfast we were required to go into the kitchen to fined someone to take our order. The restaurant waiter was nowhere to be found although he showed up later.

Free wi-fi, a smaller that average room and not even a cooked breakfast. Its hard to justify the nightly room rate at this very average hotel. It is well located and is only 11 blocks from the white house - but still for almost $400 a night (including local taxes) I'd at least expect to have a nice restaurant and some other amenities (maybe a pool) available.
