hi was at the hollywood inn expsouth for only one night but got a big room with a king bed and lots of space thte rooms are really great its an average just basic hotel or motel but location is a bit far from attractions in ex hollywood but nearer ex downtown los angheles if you re going there near freeway 101 and not to farr from thing to do in la if you want to great fr johnny b .

The staff at La Quinta were very helpful and made my stay a pleasant one! The hotel was very clean, and they gave me a reasonable discount. I asked the clerk behind the counter about the rewards thing and he livened up and gave me tons of info about how to qualify for rewards.

Bathroom tiles cracked, tub was clogged, took shower in standing backed-up water, gross door handles missing on dresser, paper cups no glass coffee cups like the ones pictured, table was missing wood/chipped, shady location,across the street from a seedy park, wi fi kept dying. Could hear the residents next door getting loud. The staff was friendly and helpful. Restaurant food was just ok.

This hotel just seems like it needs to be refurbished. Room was shabby and uncomfortable. Got bad advice from the front desk re: cab vs. driving and ended up taking a $40 cab ride (there and back) rather than driving and paying a $6 parking fee. The breakfast was awesome though! Business center consisted of one computer off the lobby and two computers in the breakfast room. None of the printers worked and two of the computers couldn't access the internet. I love Holiday Inns and am a Platinum Priority Club Member but won't stay here again.

The hotel grounds and rooms are exceptional, and very convenient to the airport and expressways. We had great service everyday at breakfast and the buildings were always stocked with the bottled water, ice cream, etc. The only distractions during the visit was related to the maid service ( did not follow up on request for additional towels and room was not clean at 4:30 p.m. on one date ). In addition, received incorrect check out time information at the front desk , which ended the stay on a not so good note.

This was our second overnight stay, and we've attended events here many times. We got a reasonable rate that included room/breakfast/parking since we were attending a large group event at the hotel. The service and food was great. Details that we found disappointing include no hot water while preparing for our evening event, three thin pillows for two people, a shower/tub design that made a lake in the bathroom floor when we showered, no "do not disturb" sign available. The Mayflower is a D.C. classic, but it seemed the details were lacking on this visit.

This is a very nice Hilton. Lobby is lovely and there are several places to eat on the premises, including a fitness room and room service. The room was nice enough but for the price it was a little worn and there was no mini fridge which should be standard for the price they charge. Plus they charged for parking which made the room seem even more drab. I would stay there again but I think I'd look at some of the other hotels first, and there are plenty to choose from.

I've stayed at the Drury before but this location was a first for me. I'm still impressed. The price is right and the extras save you so much money. Free breakfast. ANd it is a real breakfast. Eggs, toast, waffles, cereal, oatmeal, yogurt. Something for everyone. The 5:30 kickback is just as nice. On the weekend they have nachos, hot dogs, mac and cheese, baked potato, salad and 1 free drink for the adults. The beds are comfortable and spacious. Free internet. The staff was great. Would definitely recommend.

Considering that on arrival in the bathroom had hairs on someone else. Moreover in the 5 days that I stay you do not make any of the room cleaning except make the bed and change the towels. To complete the room smell was quite rude, I went to several hotels in smoking room and the smell permeated in this one I`ve never felt around ...

Wonderful old classic hotel in mid-town Manhattan. Great location. Within walking distance from Rockefeller Center, Radio City Music Hall, Times Square, Broadway plays, the U.N., and a ton of other attractions. Close to subway lines so it is easy to get to anyplace in New York City. The rooms and associated bathrooms are a little small, but what you would expect from an old, respected hotel like this one.

I'm surprised that this hotel is considered 4 stars. When I stepped into the room I felt like I stepped back in time. The shower was the small 6x6 inch white tile. The bathrooms were clean, but the carpet was questionable. The only saving grace of this hotel was the regency club, which was an awesome upgrade. There were great views from the Regency club.

I recently stayed at this hotel and was pleasantly surprised by the ambiance and overall rooms. The location is stellar, and you are in the middle of Union Square. But the rooms were excellent, clean and fresh. The bedding was fantastic, mini bar was something to be stood by, and overall a very peaceful and serene environment. The lobby has a jazz club that I didn't go to, but it seemed to have a good following when I observed. Overall, I would recommend staying here for any reason.

Nice hotel.. but they gave us a room that over looked a rooftop, we should have asked for a better room with a view of the city. We could only see cement from our window, this was very disapointing. If they give you a room like that ask them to change rooms. Also the doors closing in the hall ways were very loud and woke us several times. Clean and nice room but it was not quiet, we could hear the cars and street noise. I expect quiet for $175.00.

Worst hotel stay in NY ever! Room was the size of my closet at home. Did not get room until 6pm and wasnt the one we wanted.Bed was very comfortable. See through shower to bedroom. A/C unstable - too hot or too cold..Beautiful patio but closed in the evening. Why? Dark lobby didn't even look like a hotel when we got there. Strange lobby entrance, Not very practical layout. would never stay there again.

The Embassy Suites at the DC Convention Center is a great place to stay. Ask for a corner room and you'll have windows on two sides plus it's a bigger suite than most of them. Start the morning off with a made-to-order breakfast. End the day with the Manager's reception for snacks and drinks. Personnel very friendly. I stayed here for three weeks and it started to feel like home!!!

Found the Omni Parker to be a bit expensive for what you get. We travelled with children, one young enough for a playpen. We booked the same room type as grandparents, they luckily got a bit larger room (we had warned hotel of our playpen need) and were able to switch rooms, otherwise we would have had no floor space in the room. Not impressed by the bathroom, tub plug broken and no way to plug sink. Yes its historic, and yes the downstairs is rather grand, and also very convenient for walking but still over priced.

The contessa is a beautiful hotel ,valet ,bellmen ,staff very helpful and friendly ...rooms are beautiful beds comfortable BUT we where in a room over looking the river walk ( extra charge ) and in a corner suite at night you can hear the traffic!!!!! Very loud because apparently they run the street sweeper and maintance the streets at night !!!!!! Oh also ask or a room AWAY FROM THE ICE MACHINE !!! very loud ....the walls are thin... This is why I gave them the rating I did ...rooftop pool and spa are awesome ....

The Warick Hotel is very clean and comfortable and the location is great It is however quite expensive as is the hotel's restaurant ,staff are very polite and helpful, the double beds are not very wide for 2 adults and the roon was not serviced until after 2pm each day not so good if like me you like a nap after lunch. Other than that it was an enjoyable stay. If it was a bit cheaper I would go back

They claim imordered a smoking room I can't believe that smoking is the default choice I had to launder everything when I got home as the room reeked of smoke The ozone machine did nothing No way to open windows? The mattress was shredded on the side Not my favorite

I found the hotel very unfriendly and way too big. I did not even eat there as the wait to get into the very limited food outlets was too long. On Holiday - Do not stay there. If you are on business or a conference then maybe. The location was also not good, behind the hotel, the streets had many homeless hanging around

This hotel is very good for location, value and cleanliness. While obviously a restored older motel, it has been done to a high standard. The only slight negatives are bathroom size and the lack of an in-room safe. There is excellent access to downtown by either the west seattle bridge or by water taxi not far from the hotel. Breakfast was offered at the hotel, or you can take a pleasant walk to the corner of Alaska and California and try a local place - Easy St Cafe was excellent and very reasonably priced.

We stayed for a few nights in April 2012 at the end of our honeymoon, and had a reasonably good stay at the Handlery. The location is quite good in relation to shopping, cable cars, etc, so it was a good base. The room was quite spacious, but the bathroom was a little small and looked like it needed an update. We were quite surprised to have to pay for Wifi, as it was complimentary in most of the hotels we stayed in across the US.

It is not the first time that I stay at the Valencia( it is the 3 rd time) for the convention SABCS, and every time I am pleased to visit this place. You enter in a very "zen" place, the dark might shock you, I just think it is different and I appreciate. The rooms are large, the beds confortable, the service very good and if you need help or an advise you just go to the front desk and find Jacob or Tia, they both have plenty of ideas and are very helpful.

Nice hotel, easy walk to most attractions.Please note added expense of 50 dollars a day valet parking. There were a lot of groups staying. Free breakfast,Get down early as it is hard to find table. Nice variety of hot and cold dishes. Had to keep drapes closed in room because of building next door.Annoying was that room had one comfort chair for 2 people.Nice exercise room and pool.Fishermans Wharf a few blocks away. . .

I have just arrived back from the US i went to stay in Seattle first then down to San Fran for 7 days i arrived in this hole and booked into another hotel, it smelt the bed linen was dirty and no room at all, the web site does not show the true Hotel Fusion, i have no idea where those rooms are because the people we spoke with all said that there rooms were small, i stayed across the road at the Parc 55 at a massive cost but onto the travel agent .......great location but that is it

The location was fabulous, not far from the Boston Common and just a block from an Old Town Trolley stop. Lots of wonderful restaurants within walking distance. However, the hotel room left much to be desired. The entire room was dated, the a/c didn't work properly, the bathroom was so small you had to close the door to turn around, and it was tough to find an electrical outlet to charge mobiles. The WiFi was NOT complimentary (nor was anything else) and parking cost us $46 per night. Stay outside of town and use the T to get into town.

The hotel has recently been remodeled and looks great. However, the location is undesirable if you want to have decent dining options or take a walk. The front dest manager advised not to go outside after dark so we ordered takeout. The road noise is an issue for sleeping so take ear plugs.

Had many maintenance issues upon checking in, GM made excuses after excuses, 2 mornings in a row, woke up to warm refrig. He was the nerve to accuse me of turning down the thermostat, then tells another guest in lobby what happened. SO UNPROFESSIONAL!! Also my 2nd night front desk guy on phone was sooooo loud, uncaring.

Actually it's not as pretty as the professional pictures: 1. unfriendly service 2. very poor "grand renovation" 3. room poor condition 4. standard rooms are very small 5. same days don´t clen the room Only positive things that the hotel was located in a good location. I was in this hotel 6 nights in February. I will not go back anymore.

Plenty of old world European decor and charm is obvious in this downtown classic, as is its well worn state. My room was clean and well furnished, (albeit rather garish with its red and green color scheme); the bathroom plumbing had faucet leaks and was rather dowdy looking w/ all beige and worn antique brass-like fixtures and thread-bare towels. Hotel staff (front desk and housekeepers) were friendly and responsive. Banquet food was surprisingly good w/ very attentive wait staff. In room WiFi worked well and care was taken to supply extra power outlets at the desk.

My family had the misfortune of staying at this Hotel January 2, 2012, prior to our cruise vacation. My vehicle was broken into sometime during the night and my stereo system ripped out and luggage was stolen. I parked right out the front door and was told there were security cameras of the lot. I will not stay there again!

Stayed here for business for one night. They are currently remodeling the hotel, so the future of this Hampton may be brighter. Right now, this is one of the oldest looking Hamptons I have stayed in. The carpet and walls appear to be very old. Service was good and friendly. The bed seemed newer and was very comfortable. If you have to fly out out of the Columbus Airport, this is an ideal location. Otherwise, stay elsewhere for now.

Amazing hotel located south of Market. Close to shops and public transportation. They are in the middle of renovations and will soon be even better. Courteous and helpful staff members helped us plan out our bus routes everyday. In room amenities were so much better than we expected: Keurig coffee maker, flat screen tv, and an iHome phone dock. We will definitely stay here again!

We used our Hilton Honors points and this was a fantastic location. It is on Pike Street and is a half mile downtown to Pike Place Market. They offer a full breakfast AND dinner here and it is a close walk to downtown attractions and local coffee shops (Victrola Coffee was fantastic). Marakesh Express is less than a mile away and has some of the best sauces and Pacific-Korean food around!

The hotel was dirty. I had a terrible odor. Our door looked like it had been kicked in at one point. We were in Boston for a medical appointment and we were very uncomfortable in our room. Did not make for a good night sleep. There was hair on our bedding. The hair dryer did not work. There were stains on the carpeting in our room. The hotel looked very run done. The only thing positive about the hotel was that it was very close to the Children's Hospital.

I stayed at the Hilton Financial District weekly for over 4 months. I have to say the staff are amongst the best. The front desk clerks are very polite and accommodating, the bell staff are very polite, helpful, and go out of their way to greet you by name. The suites are very nice and spacious. I really have nothing but good to say about my stay at this Hilton other than I would highly recommend anyone staying here.

'Pay more for the better things in life.' This old adage is so true. This is a world class hotel in the heart of Chicago's business district. Michigan Avenue shopping is one block away. Touches of quality and class in everything they do. Food and service is 5 star. Spa and health club are fanatstic too.

The elevators were too slow...antique. The hotel is next to a club u can hear loud noise...people yelling, music,cars screeching their tires till about 230am. The walls are thin can hear neighbors talking...and the coffee machine had an old coffee filter...if you're there to party It's decent, if not I would not recommend...not for almost 200$ a night

We spent our first two nights after arriving in Los Angeles and the night before flying back in this motel in summer 2012. The Wilshire Motel has proven to be the perfect choice. The location is very good, the motel is located a few miles from the airport and Santa Monica Beach. Lots of pubs are in within walking distance. A full breakfast with fresh fruit is served. The motel has a lovely vintage charm. The owner was very helpful with any questions. We were five people from Germany.

This hotel is within walking distance of alot of downtown amenities. We love to take in shows at the Improv, a mere 3 or so blocks away. Clean hotel with complimentary bottled water. The only complaint I had from this stay was the air conditioning didn't work well, but it wasn't a big enough deal to even ask to be fixed.

I've stayed at many Doubletree properties. They are usually nice but not exceedingly upscale. This DT one is trying to change that impression. They have valet service - really. Parking was very expensive! It's a huge conference center with a strange layout. You practically need a shuttle to get to the elevators from the front desk. Breakfast was decent, room was fine. Little ele to complain about...

Great if you are attending a convention or meeting. They are building a new tower currently and have plans to renovate the rooms. The rooms are looking tired. The lobby and public space all look great. There is really nothing to walk to in this area. I walked to Chinatown about a mile away and the area did not seem the safest. Taxi lines can be long at times so plan ahead.

This hotel is conveniently located less than a 5-minute walk from Beale Street. Our room was clean, but it had a very strong, unpleasant, Lysol odor. The hotel common areas were mostly clean, but they must not clean the elevators in the parking garage--the same trash we saw on arrival (smashed Jell-O shot cup) was there when we checked out 2 days later. The breakfast is typical hot hotel breakfast--waffles, scrambled eggs, biscuits/gravy, yogurt, fruit, pastries, juice, coffee, etc.

Once we got there the TV was not working. So we had to swap room and that seems very difficult for the hotel. The Bell boys and the drivers was very good. But When ever we asked for something it took them a while to take bring it. But the worst problem was that there room was very dusty meaning that the room was very dirty we found this out as we kept sneezing and once we moved to the Bellagio the sneezing stopped.

I recently stayed at the Westin Grand Central and enjoyed it's proximity to mass transit. The Grand Central terminal is a great place to grab a drink, grab the subway or just pick up a snack to enjoy in your room. The room was average but the sheets and pillows were luxurious. The bathroom was spacious and very clean and there was a huge walk in shower. I would definitely request a higher floor - being right in 42nd street = lots of traffic noise.

We stayed here for one night. There were 4 of us. We were picked up at the airport on the shuttle. We scheduled a pick up time of 5am . The shuttle was 20 min late putting a rush on arriving at the airport. The room was satisfying and quiet.

The hotel has a very good location (walking distance from The Domain), a convenient parking and a contemporary design and cozy. So far so good. The staff is friendly and the rooms are good value for money, the big problem is the air conditioning engines at the exterior: they make a lot of noise. At least on the second floor is impossible to sleep.

the hotel is very clean and the staff are helpful. the carpets throughout could do with renewing, and tea and coffee are only available in the lobby, the lobby is quite small and there is no bar. the location is very good, close to all transport and bars and restaurants and chinatown.There are lots of top stores nearby if you want to shop.

We were passing through San Francisco to go north, and spent some pleasant time here. The hotel has a great location, and free parking… we were around the corner from the brilliant City Lights bookstore, walking distance from a memorable evening meal, and able to get basically everywhere on foot. We didn't have a room overlooking broadway, so it was pretty quiet, too. Rooms are nothing special, but I wan't in San Francisco to stay in my room!

Read some good reviews and thought this would be a good place to stay. This hotel was very disappointing...rooms were dingy and bare. Beds are too hard and small. Bathroom was small and very outdated. Walls were paper thin, so thin that the "fitness room" (2 out of the 3 cardio machines were out of service the 4 days I was there) they claim to have doesn't have early morning or late availability so as not to disturb guests in the next room. Won't stay here again.

-Best thing in the hotel is that it takes you back to a feeling of early 19th century -Big minus is that wireless in the room was not working for most parts in the rooms - even though they adverticed that as a complimentary. One needed to go to a lobby many times to use the internet -Good location for seeing Balboa Park, San Diego Zoo, Hillcrest and Museum area by walking

Stayed here in September. The rooms were clean and well laid out as others who have reviewed the suites have already said. The reception staff were friendly and efficient especially when I asked to change rooms. The original one backed onto the elevator shaft and was particularly noisy. Breakfast was more comprehensive than I expected which was great. I was staying here on business from overseas, without a car, the suites are rather far out from the downtown area.

I am a big fan of the Kimpton brand and this hotel reinforces that. Great location with an inviting lobby and fabulous staff. All the amenities Kimpton hotels have come to expect such as free wi-fi and a well designed hotel room with ample and convenient outlets to recharge all of your phones, tablets and laptops. This hotel also has lovely roof terrace and indoor pool. Sable restaurant and bar also a nice feature. I did not notice the noise that others have mentioned in their reviews. I really enjoyed my stay here and would gladly return.

Typical Courtyard,nice staff and the the new cafe style lobby, which I much prefer to the old breakfast buffet, but come on - no wi-fi? (there is in the lobby but in your room you have plug in a wire! I didn't remember how! too bad, iPaders) Sorry, Marriott, but there is no excuse in the second decade of the 21st century for this.

Room was clean and staff was accomodating, but I've been spoiled by the availability of microwave and fridge. Some how in my haste making the resv I thought there were m/w and fridge in all rooms, not so and not avail for room I needed. My fault for not paying attention. Otherwise stay was okay.

So yes, this place is in greektown, with great greek restaurants very closely located. I was in town for business, so I spent very little time in my room, other than sleep, which was disappointing, the beds are terrible! Also, the wifi is very spotty! However, the hotel is clean, right off the highway, and very closely located to McCormick Place, so that was great. However, it is about a $10 taxi to Michigan Ave, so just keep that in mind.

The Prescott Hotel was perfectly acceptable, but sub-par for a Kimpton hotel. I've stayed at many Kimpton's around the country, and they've become my go-to hotel because I feel like the hotel experience will be more special as compared to the standard large chain hotels. However, while our stay here was fine, this particular hotel is a dated and not memorable for the price. I will choose to stay somewhere else next time I'm in San Francisco (probably another Kimpton).

A real shame... At the rates this place is charging, I do expect a better level of upkeep. Bowed ceilings, peeling wallpaper, splintered woodwork, dank smelling room... I booked a superior double, when I saw what I was given, complained and was given a vaguely better room. Was only on a short stopover so decided to stick rather than twist. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

This is a great location at a reasonable price. And even the street noise wasn't a problem. The room itself was VERY small. But the worst part was sleeping on a brick of a bed. The floor was more comfortable.......literally!!! And for that reason, unless you will not be sleeping in the bed, I can't recommend this hotel.

Here for a conference and decidedly not up to par with most high end conference hotels - even the Hyatt sign on the podium in the ball room was beat up, with the line under Hyatt dangling. Room wasn't cleaned properly, coffee wasn't replenished and staff were not helpful. Impersonal and a little run down

I needed a convenient hotel while my husband was in the hospital and The Inn at Longwood Medical certainly met that need. What I had not expected was the level of service, cleanliness and helpfulness I found. From the Front Desk staff to the management, I felt welcome and important. Even with a challenge with room keys, the staff was patient and extremely helpful. Everyone made this part of my stay easy and comfortable during a difficult time.

Thanks to Priceline the hotel was a decent deal at $149++/night. Rooms were small, but New York is New York. Bathroom even smaller. Old tube tv's were odd. Water pressure was awful. Hotel was relatively clean and nicely located on 48th between Park and Lexington. Staff was friendly. Nothing really stands out(except the price) but would likely return at this pricepoint.

This is a great little find near Times Square. The staff is wonderful, accommodations just great--very quiet. Every comfort has been included. I can only say good things and will be back as soon as I can plan another trip. I have stayed at very upscale hotels all over the place, and this one is right up there with the best. Thanks for a great experience, Casablanca!

One-night stay before a cruise. The highlight was the courteous shuttle service to and from the cruise port. Room had some issues. Parking lot had more...at least half the lights were dead. Doesn't that sound like somewhere you want to park? Graffiti all over the elevator. Carpet stains everywhere in hallways.

This hotel wasn't very clean and very noisy in the night with fights and people getting sick outside in the pool area. Pictures of this hotel are decieving, to say the least. the suite we had, was furnished with a gas cooking stove which had a bad gas smell. so we shut it off at the wall, just so we could stay there. Had we not prepaid and had it not been 11:00pm when we checked in after a long day at Sea World we would have went somewhere else. Sleeping in the car might have been bettter.

Our room didn't have working a/c , which in August is uncomfortable, Staff could be rude. The nicest staff I talked with were a bell captain and the maid. The location was convenient to the waterfront area and to the art museums. I'm not sure the location made up for the poor service.

Pre booked delux rooms with queen beds located near to each other. On booking in two rooms with single beds were allocated. We returned to reception and requested the correct level and were given rooms 10 floors apart. The corridors and lifts were odorous and felt unsafe. The decor is tired and old and need regrading. We chose to cancel and move on despite the lateness. The reception staff, although reluctant and extremely slow, eventually (after some time) re-imbursing our account so that we could move on. NOT A HAPPY EXPERIENCE AND WOULD NOT RECOMMEND TO FRIENDS AND FAMILY.

Not only were the rooms wonderful (we had a 2 bedroom suite) but when we arrived, they were serving dinner (at no cost) and the following morning, there was a great breakfast spread. I wouldn't suggest going there simply for the food, but the entire package was a wonderful combination.

We spent one night here at the end of a week of siteseeing around the San Francisco area. Asked for a quite room when I made the reservation so I was surprised that I was given a room close to the elevators because we all know those are not the quiet ones! Rooms are large, beds are comfortable, but the furniture in the room was worn for the price we paid. Staff was helpful with printing boarding passes and booking transporation to the airport.

This is our 4th year returning to the New Yorker because we are in the Macy's Parade every year, and this is the staging ground for the parade. The room was the nicest yet. Room 2616 was a mini suite. While the hotel is old, and we didn't really have a "view" from our window, I don't think you can beat the price, or the location. The staff was welcoming NY style ;)

I stayed in a fair share of Marriotts as a Gold status member and this one was impressive. I was very happy with the service at the front desk and location of the hotel. Despite its location, I could not hear a thing once I was in the room. It is a great spot to be able to walk out of the front door and get to a number of theaters. If you can stay on the concierge level, it is definitely worth it. The views from the lounge are lovely, and the breakfast was wonderful.

I went to Washington and I rented two rooms in this Hotel Rooms are OK, don't like too much the atmosphere there, but for the price and the location very close to museums, White House, etc is perfect. Parking Garage is a pain, too small and you have to find the way to park your car in a very small space with out hitting other cars. Neighborhood is great and great restaurants in the area.

I arrived to LAX airport at 12am, I have booked this hotel on expedia it was on sale for $89 when I got therei find this is in noway a hotel its more of a motel but what really got me was the smell of the room was old and damp. service was good the breakfast was OK and the service was good.

Just a short stay overnight so we did not partake in the awesome pool/spa area, or go tomtje restaurant or bar. All seemed popular and amazing, despite the party feel, our junior suite was very quiet, the bed and linens were nice, and I liked the overall look and feel of the space. We have already decided that all our overnight stops in Phoenix will be at the Clarendon,.

The Granduca is our choice whenever we travel to Houston. Attention to detail, warmth and charm are all evident in this lovely hotel. The staff welcome you as if you are arriving home..... Very nice! Rooms are spacious and the small kitchen is very convenient. My wife was especially fond of the large walk-in closet. The surrounding area is also very chic and the whole Granduca experience is always first class!

I am on a cross country bicycle and I met Rich who works for the hotel in Florida at the airport. After talking for a few minutes he asked where I was staying. I didn't have a reservatIon in the area so he recommended the Handlery. He said it was nice and convienient to the area I needed to be in in the San Diego area. The room was very comfortable and the other staff excellent. The hotel was everything he said and more. I would definitely stay there again.

We stayed here for 2 nights in 3 separate single rooms with shared bathroom. The hotel is a bit dated and so were the rooms, but they were clean and comfortable. The location is great, felt safe and was a short walk from Pike Place Market. The reception staff were excellent, very friendly. There's a very small coffee shop which leads off the reception was good for a morning coffee. The shared bathrooms and toilets were fine, I never waited to use one. Overall excellent value for money.

Only stayed at this place since it was the cheapest hotel that was available for the night that was close to the medical center and had a free shuttle there. When you walk into this place, it looks more like a hostel rather than a hotel. The rooms are semi-decent at best and they are a bit dirty with leaky plumbing. They have a free continental breakfast, free car parking and free WiFi throughout the property. They also have a free shuttle to the medical center.

Free wifi didn't work, they made me ring the 1 800 number to their ISP, and after 40 mins trying to fix it, it still didn't work. Check out person was to stupid to understand when I tried to explain, so their Satifaction Gurantee amounted to nothing. Room was pleasant enough location turned out to be 1 street away from skid row, so a walk was pestered by bums with their hands out. I wouldn't stay again here, even though I mostly use this chain.

We stayed here for just one night while traveling through California. The price is a little high for what it is, especially since it does not include parking. The whole area in and around the hotel was very crowded with a lot of traffic. Unless you need to be downtown Los Angeles, stay elsewhere.

The Back Bay is a great centrally located hotel in the city of Boston. You can walk to almost all tourist attractions from the hotel. Rooms were small but plush! The beds are extremely comfortable and service was fantastic. Hotel bar was a perfect place to relax after a full day of touring.

If midtown is your base this isn’t a bad option and Penn station couldn’t be any closer. The room I had was quite small, but manageable. The suite appeared renovated, but the bathroom had been overlooked and a bit dated. A portion of the hotel is dedicated to student/educational housing and somewhat takes away from the hotel atmosphere. It's not an issue, just unexpected. They did accommodate an early check-in at no additional cost which was a bonus. Overall it was OK, but I’ll be staying elsewhere next time.

There is not enough parking! The room is the smallest I have ever seen. The price is not worth the room we got. I probably will not be returning to this hotel, but the staff was nice! I was just expecting so much more from this hotel for the price we paid.

We stayed at this hotel the weekend that we moved our son to the UT campus. The hotel staff were accommodating and pleasant, the room was very clean, and the hotel was a short, scenic drive from the UT campus. We enjoyed breakfast at the hotel as well - excellent food and service! We will stay here again the next time we visit Austin.

The property was clean and the desk and bell staff was wonderful. However, the rooms are older and in need of renovation. Additionally, there is some training that needs to be done. I ordered room service twice and both times the tray was not prepared properly (no salt and pepper, no water, no glass with ice for the canned soda). The staff is super friendly and the location is excellent. If you are looking for a clean, comfortable room are are willing to trade some of the amenities, this is the place for you.

I stayed in this hotel for one night and I was only impressed by its location. The hotel is old in my ways! Rooms are old, Carpets are all over and old, their staff is old, and there is no wi-fi in the whole hotel I.e. living in the olden days! There are many better hotels in the city which cost the same but are more modern.

This hotel was a pleasure to stay at. The hotel was elegant, immaculate, and historically interesting. It is within walking distance of the conference center, White House and Georgetown, all places we enjoyed during our stay. We very much enjoyed our 6th floor deluxe king room. The room was clean, quiet and very comfortable, and the bathroom was well kept. The staff was more than accommodating, easily accessible and very professional. Does not disappoint! We will stay there again!

service is a major issue needless to mention the feeling when you would like to take a shower with no hot water and a clogged bathtab all for $200 a night way to go Westin :( Service is another but an AMAZING few individuals the rest of the staff have a lot to learn....When living in the air there are only few things that matters, ...

Stayed in May 2012. At no time were we told (until we drove there) that there would be $43/day parking fee. Generally rooms/hallways/lifts etc are old and outdated. The compressor for the AC/Heating is IN THE ROOM. If you use it, thats all you hear. You cannot even hear others talking. Good location but better Hotels nearby. Don't know why Radisson put their name to this one.

Didn't expect the water stain on the cieling in a room at the Hyatt, thinking a little mold in the rooms since it is unlikely there was a shower directly overhead. Otherwise rooms were unremarkable. Breakfast buffet is $18 a plate for unimpressive hotel food, but many good places to eat within walking distance. Will say everyone from the front desk, maid, and concierge offered the best service I've seen in years.... don't need to valet - cheaper and close at the parking lot attached, hardly any walk

The hotel is a little worn, but for the price you cant beat it. Safe, full service property. Would be nice to have updated TV's. Breakfast buffet is a litte sparce. Bar prices are a little steep, but I would stay there again and would refer others. Has the chance to be a great hotel. Management staff is great! GM is very nice and attentive!

- Mold in bath tub - No wash cloths - Smell in room - No A/C - Has to keep windows open to stay cool - Bad TV picture - Wifi - very slow and unreliable - Clocks set to wrong time - Elevators made a lot of noise and felt unsafe, used the stairs -

We stayed in a regular room over a long weekend. It was a great base given its proximity to Newbury Street, the Prudential and Copley shopping malls, and the Boston Common. The staff were terrific and always welcoming. The restaurant and bar were warm with good drinks and food. The rooms were very comfortable for two and it was a nice romantic base for couples. I had a car with me, and the valet service was quick and responsive. I would highly recommend the MO versus the other options in Boston.

Love the happy hour, and the service was excellent. The only issue was that I woke up in the middle of the night & it was like 99 degrees in my room. The gym was also great and clean. Otherwise, this was a great hotel and cannot wait to enjoy my new year's here!!

We were just going to LA overnight. The hotel was clean, the location was great. You do have to pay for parking, but it was safe and secure. The rooms had a good size lanai overlooking the pool. All in all it was a good price for an average room. They had great tv channels, but we could not access the internet.

This is a pretty expensive hotel and definitely not worth the price. Actually were able to find a good deal on orbitz or travelocity, one of the two sites. The beds are very small. We got a room with 2 doubles and I was surprised by how small their beds were. I probably wouldn't stay here again.

Stayed here about 15 years ago and really enjoyed the experience.Returned because we had such a good time then didn't think of going anywhere else.However the room we had on the 5th floor(try to avoid) was terriblely old fashioned(60s decor)tiny bathroom,two double beds which made it impassable in the room.Booked omni parker select which should give you extras we didn't receive these.Plus side very central but that is the only positive for this hotel.Very dated in a negative way.

Hotel is in a decent location but the whole place is very rundown.The rooms are clean but after some of the reviews earlier in the year regarding rodents and bed bugs they must have had to sort things out.Staff are helpful and there are around 600 rooms so it is usually busy,especially with large groups of young people.There are ice machines on every second floor but make sure you get a room well away from these as they are very noisy.

Spent 7 nights at the new yorker and it was a very pleasant stay. Great friendly staff, great location (close to penn station and times square) and we got a great view from our window! We thought it was a bit expensive at first but in the end still worth it, especially for the great location. Never took a cab, only subway all week long!

THe Hotel staff was very pleasant and helpful. I never had to wait for service or help. I found the rooms to be clean and updated. We even got fresh cookies when we walked into the door. I would stay here again. The location was not to far away from Times Square and 5th Avenue.

We had a family reunion in town with over 13 people and we all stayed at the Silver Cloud at .Lake Union. It was very comfortable, clean, and reasonably priced. The breakfast was very extensive and quite good. The bed was comfortable, and it had a real blanket instead of the down comforter, which I find too hot. Sink outside of the bathroom was nice.

I recently stayed here for 4 nights. Great hotel overall. Rooms were very spacious, clean, and modern. Beds were comfortable. Room service was wonderful and fast. There is a starbucks open 24 hours in the lobby that is very convenient. Tons of restauants and bars within walking distance. Mall is right next door. I very very impressed with the Hilton and would stay there again.

This hotel was extremely dirty. Burn holes in the comforter. Carpets were filthy. Bathroom was disgusting. Left my car in the long-term parking and upon my return no one answered the phone for pick up from the airport as I was instructed to do once I arrived back into the airport. I had to get a cab from the airport back to the hotel. This was absolutely the worst experience in a hotel that I have ever had. Do not bother staying here!!!!!!!!!!

We've stayed in Jerry's motel for 3 nights, rooms were a little bit shabby, but very clean, and we've had all necessary things: iron, shampoos, free wifi and parking. It's not far from centre and very close to chinatown. And we've got free snacks when we arrived, that was very nice. The only disadvantage I can imagine - walls are thin, you can hear people talking in next room.

We were given an upgrade to a 44th floor room. Not sure how much of an upgrade it was (except for the view), as the room looked older / less newly decorated than many others on the hotel site. In addition, smoke from somewhere nearby (the smoking floor described as "isolated"? the meeting rooms on the top floor?") drifted down through the ventilation system and the odor was strong enough to make me feel distinctly ill. If you are sensitive to smoke, ask where this so-called isolated smoking floor is and make sure you are nowhere near it!

Reserved a room for 3 nights. After the first night we were forced to down grade to a smaller room because they booked the room for someone else even though I had reserved it for 3 nights. Originally had a double king bed and we were moved to a room with just one king bed making it very cramped for the remainder of our stay. Front desk was very blunt about moving us and there wasn't anything we could say or do to stay in the same room that I had originally reserved.

We choosed a smaller 'boutique' hotel, and the high expectations were met. Great location in Midtown close to Bryant PArk and Grand Terminal. A pretty calm area, close to many interesting sites, a lot of shopping, many good restaurants and 25 minutes walk from Central Park. The service is great at the hotel and we very much enjoyed the nice buffet breakfast and the possibility to take a cup of tea and a cake during the day and a nice glas of vine with cheese before going out for dinner in the evening.

The service is most important to me when I travel. We travel frequently. The staff was friendly and attentive. Room service was fast and the food was delicious. The spa and lap pool were amazing. The hotel is close to all of the attractions or just a quick cab ride away. The Four Seasons has never disappointed me.They always treat our family as if we were VIP's.

We take a trip to the HHC every year. I love this property. Everything from the customer service to the raccoons that stalk you at night by the lazy river. Minutes from sea world . The spa is hands down one if the best i have been too . You ate able to get a day pass to their sister property just down the street . They have 2 water slides with a lazy river..

I spent a week in the North Tower in room 2531. I had a great view. The room was comfortable, clean and staff were friendly. The Lobby Bar had cold drinks but was under staffed. The main restaurant is closed for renovation. The Lobby Bar is not set up for eating and the staff are not restaurant professionals. The pool area is nice and kid-friendly.... The chlorination is way over the top!

The hotel is very small, hard to find and not in a good location. It can work for business travel, but definitly not for vacation or families. The restaurant and bar in the roof has a great view and young people, but the food almost sent my son to the hospital... Asked for a breakfast at the room that never came, but was imediatly charged. It's not a hotel for vacation or families, maybe a good one for couples or single people. I have to recognize it's new and modern, with good amenities and wifi.

Handlery is tired. Its pretty ugly. Its a little dirty. Its overpriced. The staff is very nice. It is right on Union Square. Our room was in the older motel like part of the hotel. It was quiet. The pool looked pretty bad but we did not use it. Our friends told us the tower rooms were no better. So, in summary, you can do better and you should.

This hotel is a favorite and a tradition for many football fans going to the Oklahoma/Texas football game, catering to OU fans. Staff is friendly and efficient, good breakfast buffet. Only knock on this establishment is the old cathode ray tube TVs in the living room of the suites. Come on Wyndham, upgrade to the 21st Century!

Overall experience was good. We stayed @ the 18 floor tower 3 renovated floor and room. My only concern was the tiny bathroom and the lack of drawers. The rest was fine. The lobby is big and busy. The personnel was nice and efficient. Only 1 restaurant and 1 Starbucks sadly the restaurant on the top floor with amazing views of San Fran is out of business.

The renovated rooms are ok but everything else about this place feels like a prison. There's a cafeteria with limited hours serving mostly greasy short-order type food. Bar closes at 9:00 and guests are "discouraged" from bringing their own alcohol into the rooms. Really?! 99 percent of the business here seems to come from guaranteed contracts such as corporate and gvt trainings, etc, so no real incentive here to care about the customer experience. If you're stuck here like me (not by choice) then I feel sorry for you.

We had a pleasant and hassle free stay. Rooms were spacious and beds were comfy. Plenty of outlets for chargers plus free wi-fi. I liked the water saving toilet "half-flush" option. Wish I could retrofit my home toilets! The main reason for the four star rating is the average quality breakfast buffet for $10.95. Hey - at least offer fresh waffle maker at that price!

My family and I stayed there on a Sea World vacation and hands down this hotel has the best staff I have seen in a very long time. Ok so it is an airport hotel so dont expect a view .. and the rooms were your typical fairfeild inn rooms.. however you cant not beat a staff that is friendly, helpful, and just fun ..they all were a great added bonus to our trip.. This is a great place to stay.

Planned to take my family for a weekend in the city and had booked my rooms well in advance through SPG. On arrival discovered that the reservations had not been made as requested. On escalation to the Front Desk Manager every attempt was made to accomodate us and the staff took care of us and went above and beyond to make our trip successful and memorable

I changed hotels halfway through a 2-week stay in Arizona, after being disappointed by the first one. When I arrived at this hotel the location and exterior did not impress. It just looked iffy. Fortunately I went inside. It was a great place to stay, with a nice courtyard in the interior, a wonderful bar/dining area on the 5th floor, plenty of parking, and great staff. I'd definitely stay here again.

Decent staff, few services, property getting a bit long in the tooth, and nothing attractive/special about the property (to the rear is a massive, sprawling, un-unsed parking lot, to the front is I-40). For a roadside stop driving cross-country it does the job. I noticed that this is where older Courtyard furniture seemed to land to live out its final useful days. However for nearly $100/night, find a Motel 6 - aside from a wanna-be breakfast and small indoor pool, there's not much difference. The value just wasn't there.

Everyone was very helpful and courteous all during our stay. We were given good directions to places when we asked. Also advice given regarding the subway fare which was very helpful. The restaurant service was also great and the food was very good. Would return on next visit to NYC! Thanks Alex, you have a great staff.

We stayed at the Library for a week in May and it turned out to be a perfect choice. The Queen-rooms are cosy, spacious enough and although looking out on 41th St. kept the city noise away. Most of all we enjoyed the friendly service and the possibility to relax at the lounge in the afternoon with wine and cheese. Other clear Pros are the nice included breakfast, the central location near Grand Central Station and the roof-top bar an 14th floor. We will definitely come again.

This hotel is clean. We love the family suite. However the hotel layout is very confusing. We checked in around midnight and after 15 minutes to find the room, we couldn't open door. The keys đínt work. We had to go back to the front desk and the clerk told us that this the room may be been occupied already !?!? ... She gave us another room and told us if it doesn't work again, come back and she would give us another room. Wouldn't the hotel know which room being occupied? Very strange experience!

This was a very nice hotel. Although it was not right in the middle of the action, it was close enough to walk to Time Square and catch a bus to other attractions. It was also only a few blocks from the Empire State Building. The 5pm wine and cheese hour was a nice touch. The room was nice and the beds were very comfortable. The staff was very friendly and accomodating.

Four people in room and given one set of towels. Room cleaned the next day no towels, had to ask for toilet paper. Never once was the counter in the bathroom cleaned. Shuttle was excellent but needed a stool to get in the van height too high for patrons to get in without a chance of injury. Pool was clean but needed a rail to get up stairs.

I stayed at this hotel for one night on business and attended a meeting in their function room. There is definitely a 1960s vibe to the place. Public spaces could definitely use and upgrade. My room was fine--exactly what you'd expect--clean and spacious. The pool area was very pleasant. The food was surprisingly good. I ate lunch there at the restaurant and it was very good value. The breakfast buffet was very good. I was attending a function and I have to say that the luncheon provided was way above the level you would normally expect at a corporate event.

In many ways this is a perfect hotel. You stay right in the center of downtown, and while the whole place could benefit from a makeover, it provides exactly what you need when on business - a clean room, a great bed, and a great location. No frills, but basically, and let's face it, a hotel room is where you spend time sleeping, showering, and spare time on the internet. The price is right, and if you want a good, basic hotel in Chicago I would stay here again.

Although the is suppose to be a 4star hotel, I found it to be very small. The agent upon check in was very friendly, and well educated on all knowledge of property and surrounding area. The king room was small. I felt like I was in a tiny box, with a long narrow bathroom. The restaurant was a HUGE disappointment, one of my guest ended up ill from the meal.

this hotel does offer free wifi in rooms, but no free breakfast. many hotels -embassy suites do. If you ask for free wifi you frequently will get that also at embassy suites. We booked a two room suite at the garden inn but there is no door between the living area and the bdrm. Since we get up at different times we prefer a door. Also, the bdrm was freezing and the living area was hot. We moved to embassy suites after the first night.

It's a nice and small hotel. The elevator is tiny, we almost couldn't enter with the baby's stroller but everything was great. We needed to sterilize at least twice a day our baby's bottles - they don't offer a microwave inside the room - so we asked the staff to sterilize for us at the hotel's basement. It's at Union Square neighborhood, 2 blocks from the square! And 2 blocks from Powell street.

The location is great and the price was right but the room smelled musty. Plus our room was too close to the firehouse across the street and the screaming sirens woke us up all night long. If you do come, ask for a room away from Arch St and the noise.

I am always disappointed in hotel beds and had seen previous reviews that complemented the Hard Rock bedding. Very pleasantly surprised - higher quality bedding and comfortable mattress. We had a suite which was very nice. Excellent location in Gas Lamp district with many restaurants to choose. Easy walking distance to the harbor. Very pleasant staff.

This was our second stay at the Radisson Martinique. The location is excellent for families visiting NYC - whenever you want to go shopping (Macys 2 min away) or sightseeing. We were offered an upgrade to 17th. floor with some more space - and enjoyed it! The restaurant is worth while visiting - not only for breakfast. The staff were very helpful and could provide a good offer for taxi to the airport.

The St. Regis is a very elegant hotel in a great location. We stayed in the St. Regis Suite, and the bed was very comfortable, sheets very good quality, shower was great, living room area very nice, but the standouts in this hotel are the beautiful lobby and the excellent restaurant. Hotel staff was also very accommodating. The rooms are a little pricey, but it was a special occasion for us and we could not have been more pleased.

I have stayed here several times. The majority of the rooms I had stayed in had broken door jambs--they had been kicked open in the past. The repairs were sloppy and invited easier future break-ins. As a man, this does not freak me out too much. I notified the managment and eventually the La Quinta chain managment. I stayed there again and there was no change in the sloppy repair of the multiple break-ins. If you value the safety of your property or your family, you will find a better run hotel in which to stay.

One night stay on a weekend. Positives: very comfortable bed. Nice, quiet view from south side (back) of hotel, free WiFi. Negatives: small, cramped room - even by NYC standards, overall cleanliness leaves something to be desired, only two elevators for a decent sized property, everything seemed a bit "tired". Suggestions: ask for a high floor, rear / south facing room. Garage available down the street for $20 / night, but I found on street parking fairly easily (was a Sunday)

Pros- great customer service. Beautiful views. Can hear the sea lions at night. Airport shuttle that will take you to places on shelter island. Cons- thin scratchy towels. Strange damp spot on floor of room Ancient furniture and televisions. Resorts are supposed to have bath robes. terrible food ( how do you mess up eggs and potatoes?). Need a car do go almost anywhere. Flat cheap pillows. Room phone broken.

Regarding accessible suite on third floor. The good: Front desk excellent. Room clean and nice, though the bed could have been better. Even room service was good. They brought out the best from the tiny property they have (palm trees, tropical plants, etc). The bad: Persistent freeway noise makes you feel like you are camping on the emergency lane. Access to/from freeway and parking are a nightmare.

don't choose this hotel if you are in a business travel in SF: tiny rooms, almost no breakfast (breakfast is OK if you are in a youth hostel but in such an expensive hotel...), dark dining room, no chance to have a quite dinner at all, bad service in summary...

I stayed at this hotel during a convention at the Hilton-Americus. I was expecting a hot spot and a cot. The staff were nice and helpful. The room was a typical holiday inn express that was remodeled. The extras made the hotel fabulous. The indoor pool and Jacuzzi was great just a little heavy in the chlorine. Breakfast was tasty, and the 4pm hot baked cookies are great after a long conference day. Parking is secured with Houston police always stopping by for cookies.

On the plus side, the Roosevelt is ideally located midtown close to Grand Central Terminal, the lobby is very impressive, the doorman outside is a fun new york character and the lobby bar is packed every night with all sorts of interesting people. On the other hand, the rooms are generic and a little dingy with cracked tile in the old-fashioned tiny bathrooms supplied with nonabsorbent towels. These are not rooms you'll want to spend much time in, which is good because you're in New York City and there's so much to explore.

My white socks looked like I was playing outside in the dirt after walking on the carpet for a couple of hours. Breakfast was lame but good for a one day stay. Traveling for business this would not be my first pick in this area by any means. Hotel needs some TLC to bring it up to a average hotel. Clearly the Choice hotel chain is on a decline in Quality at certain locations.

The only saving grace of this hotel is the location. Our room had a super firm, sideways turned king bed. A duvet cover with no duvet, a remote that didnt work and stained stained stained carpet. The bathroom was tiny but the tile around the shower looked new as did the granite on the counter. The staff was friendly.

Stayed two nights and were very pleased. All the staff were so friendly and helpful. Location is good for art galleries etc. It is simply an excellent five star hotel. The spa is very nice. Our room did not have an easy chairs which I guess is my minor negative.

We have lost a complete day in fixing our booking problems : we booked one room with 2 double beds, we got 1 double bed in the room. Rooms really old and in very bad conditions, not refreshed. Staff (except one) not ready to give you time. In one word it's a big factory...

It's a decent hotel to stay in the center of time square, easy access to everything and close to train station. If you stay in lower levels, the noise including siren can be disturbing, but overall the hotel service and the conditions are fair to the price they charge for.

Hi everybody, We staid at the Wilshire Crest Hotel for 5 nights last week, us two plus our two children (13,10). All of us enjoyed very much the nice breakfast, the comfort shower, the smiles on everyones faces, the free parking & the very fare price! As Israelis, we appreciated the nice jew neighborhood & the presents of vegetables + fruits at Breakfast :) We very much recommend the hotel. Yossy & Sigal Levy Israel

What can I say... The price was right, the location was great, the staff was amazing, and the rooms gorgeous. I consider it the perfect hotel. Amazing amenities for a NYC hotel (free wifi, wine, snacks, etc.). Beautiful hotel, super friendly and helpful staff. The ONLY complaint I can think of is that the elevator buttons shock you all the time! Not sure what's up with that!

Rooms were clean, great location, right at the gates of Chinatown. Curtains let too much light in at night and the windows need to replaced with double pane to lessen the street noise. I was in a room across the street from the wine bar and they dump all the bottles in the early morning hours and that's when the trash is picked up and the noise woke me up.

This was a beautiful hotel when built and the architecture still is. Unfortunately it is now in need of a lick of paint and new carpets. The service here was good and staff friendly and helpful. The hotel bars and restaurants were overpriced. The location makes it good for people on business but not so good for tourists.

Words cannot express the sheer luxury associated with Four Seasons Chicago. I stayed there in June with my wife, for my birthday, and the stay was absolutely magnificient. The room was exceptional and the staff at Four Seasons Chicago really understands how to pamper their guests and cater to requests. Words cannot express how positive I feel about the quality of the Four Seasons as luxury hotel choice. Additionally, the location is incredible and gives you prime access to everything in downtown Chicago. You will feel like royalty by choosing Four Seasons Chicago!

Spent labor day weekend at the Mark Hopkins. The service was remarkable. Caroline in housekeeping was AMAZING. And seriously with the help of her and the amazing concierge desk, all our requests were made possible. Everyone at the hotel truly makes you feel at home. Never before have I encountered such fantastic service. Also we spent our anniversary there and upon returning to our room they had a dessert tray congratulating us. So incredibly thoughtful :) Would definitely go back and recommend to all my friends.

We had a one bedroom suite which was excellent, small bathroom but manageable. We found the location to be excellent with plenty of food and beverage shops close by. Also the subway is very close. All in all I would highly recommend this property unfortunately I did not check the extra taxes that were added onto our bill.... these were "NY State tax, NY City tax, NY City occupancy tax and NYS hotel unit fee" total per night of US$59.87. As far as we were concerned these should have been explained when we made the booking.

it was not good at all. The night when I checked in the men over the counter was very rude to me, yelling on me that "Did you get a name?". I cannot believe this is how a hotel treats the customer. Then I found out the WiFi does not work at all. They only use a D-Link home router for such a big motel. If you are three rooms away from the office you will get no signal. The AC is very very loud

Stayed for a week to access the Convention Center. Room was disappointing at these prices. I thin k $13/day for WiFi in a room priced over $300 is "nickel and dining" guests. Concierge level plain and cafeteria-like. Excellent location with access to mall and convention center, restaurants.Food service for functions in hotel was very good. Slow elevator service.

Attended a conference at this hotel. Food Service staff were rude and service for convention meals was bad. Front desk was rude. Bell Captains great. Concierge great. Being that some Staff was good, I suspect that the leadership of guest services is the issue, the high volume managers (convention services and front desk) need training. This property has no Concierge lounge so if your a Hilton Honors member stay elsewhere. Better places in this wonderful city for a conference

We stayed 4 nights at The Whitehall Hotel. The location was outstanding, one block from The Hancock Building, less than one block from many bus routes, less than one block from The Magnificent Mile! The hotel itself is a little worn, the rooms are small but the staff were very pleasant! Would I stay here again? Yes just for the location alone!

The DC Grand Hyatt is not really "grand," but more a comfortable business hotel. Nothing special hear but the crab sandwich at the sports bar (quite tasty!). This hotel will suit most business travelors, and can be a nice place for those others that want a comfortable/affordable/centrally located place to stay. Not much to complain, or to write home about.

The security there and cops show up and are allowed to just walk into your room without your permission. If you plan on drinking they will come in and write tickets. Just a for-warning for anyone wanting to do that. You sign a waiver saying you are under 21 when checking in and thats why they come check your rooms.

This hotel is OK but it's about a 15 minute walk to Union Square. It's got a 24 hour gym (not huge) but good for those of us with jetlag. The rooms are comfortable but perhaps the decor is a little tired... but it does have free wifi which is ideal for the business traveller. I didn't go in the swimming pool but it looked a bit small. Again, it's OK and I wouldn't complain if I had to go there again but I would prefer a hotel closer to Union square with all the shops and restaurants.

This hotel could not be better placed but it really is a Conference hotel. An example, we stayed on the Concierge level which meant beakfast etc. was included. For the first few days we were on our own as business travellers had their own dining facilities, then at the weekend, standing room only. The rooms were clean and other than a shower that was almost impossibe to get at the right temperature we had no complaints.Like all large hotels in big cities it is very impersonal, but if location is of paramount importance, then it is fine.

We stayed at the Westin Park Central while we attended a conference. The staff was excellent; they were friendly and sincerely accommodating. The furnishings are somewhat dated, but the room was clean and the bed was wonderful! Two gentlemen at the restaurant, Cafe' on the Park, served us very well . . . Oscar Del Cid and Isau Rios. Both were beyond kind and served us in excellence, without being overbearing or annoying.

Well I was here during sandy hurricane, beautiful soho view from my room, nice and cozy. But everyday I need to leave a note to room attendant what needs to be replenish. Have coffee maker but they won't provide any stirrer, have towels but they won't replenish toiletries . I stayed there 1 week kind of frustrating, You need to pay wifi $10 for 24 hours. That was not my expectation of Sheraton groups.

Our family of 4 stayed here for one night on our way to our final vacation destination. The hotel is obviously new which is always nice and the staff was very accomodating. The large, new upscale mall next door provided an opporunity for everyone to stretch their legs after a long day in the car and in spite of the rain. Breakfast was very good. We'll definately stay there again if the opportunity arises.

It was fine. They obviously spent a lot on the lobby & not much on the rooms. Our room was outdated with atrocious carpeting - ugly & dingy. Palette of room is too bland, no beauty or care went into it. Rooms are an afterthought here. Tv was not HD which is insane at this price. bathroom was nice and our overall stay was good. Staff is friendly & helpful. I like hotel rooms at this price to be clean & modern, not bland & dingy. We expected more for the price. Would try another hotel when we go back.

The hotel front desk clerks were amazingly nice, helpful in directions and transportation options. The maid was very responsive to the size of our party. The walls however are terribly thin and the sofa bed had to be the worst I have ever slept on. The location is ok but will only go back after a renovation. Loved the staff though!!!

We stayed here while a relative was having open heart surgery at TX Childrens' Hospital. Seemed expensive to us since it was on the list from hospital of places that had "special prices" for patient's families. It was cleaned and breakfast decent. Within walking distance of the hospital. It could be expensive if a family had to stay for a long period of time.

At the last minute we needed a good and inexpensive hotel to stay at. We were traveling with one 11 years old girl. The hotel was well situated across from the Lincoln Center, it was clean, the staff was friendly and we got an upgrade to a suite for the same price. We loved staying there and highly recommend it!!! we will stay there again and again when we return to NYC! The Rodriguez Weill Family

i often stay at this hotel when taveling on business to NYC , it has a very cool vibe to it and a great location , rooms are sometimes small but the staff is always happy to help out with an upgraid when avail , Especially catherine front desk manager , she is really great and and always does her best to care of me and my crew .

Stayed at the Marriott back in February. The lobby was very nice and was able to check in around 12:30p coming straight from the airport. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room itself was very nice and clean. Only down side was the size of the bathroom but worked out just fine. The location of the hotel was great within walking distance of everything we were looking to do. Moreover, the exercise room and pool area was kept nice but may have needed some updating. Overall great stay, I would stay here again.

We arrived early and were told we could pre-check-in and they would call us when our room was available. Never got a call. Went back to the hotel to see where things were at and found a lobby full of unhappy folks. Not sure what the issue was, but they weren't turning the rooms around quickly enough to keep pace. Some didn't get their rooms till early evening. Otherwise, rooms were ok.

Whilst the Hotel was adequate for our needs it's location on the outskirts of Tenderlion leaves a lot to be desired. The area contains many homeless and beggars who became a nusiance whilst not threaten. Our overall opinion of San Francisco was one of disapointment being expensive for drinks and food and the locals not the most friendly of people compared to the Southern States.

Short version....everyday we had to track down essentials that should have been in our room. 3 days only 1 regular coffe for 2 people....broken hair dryer, make up mirror did not work, no heat in bathroom, no bathrobes in room, no water pressure in shower. Ice bucket sat outside our room 2 days,the one that was out there when we arrived! We never did get an ice bucket. Only one lotion in room the whole time.....did not restock water glasses. These are all things that should not happen.

Impersonal.clean. Not at all charming. Everything costs extra--wireless, water in the gym, entrance to gym, seals on the refridge-. No complaints about noise. Everyone working there--concierge, reservation staff, parking attendants, hostess, customer service reps-- behaved like they were under a lot of stress. No wonder! 2,200 rooms. Largest hotel in NYC. Surely management can give their hard working employees a little more Kindness so it trickles down to the guests? Not a place to stay for romance. Maybe business. Maybe family since location is good.

All of staff were nice-thank you for hailing a cab on a hot day (sorry, can' remember the doorman's name). Having soymilk was nice, too. Oh, of course, I enjoyed champaign every evening. Although it was pretty hot out, the ceiling fan in the room was effective -we did not have to turn on a/c at night.

We are seasoned travelers, and were shocked at the dirt and condition of this hotel. The room was dirty. The light plates and door were grimy, dirty towels left in the bathroom, tile floor not swept or mopped. The desk area was sticky and had beverage rings on it. Very disappointing. Desk personnel was friendly and efficient, that was a plus.

This hotel is in need of renovation. The rooms have carpeting that is showing signs of wear. There was no iron in the room and the ironing board was rickety. Just didn't feel like we were staying in a 4 star hotel. The staff however was friendly and the parking garage can be accessed from the hotel elevators. The location is just across from the Galleria mall and Grand Luxe and Cheesecake Factory are within walking distance.

Bugs in the room. Told the front desk and they said they would fix it; came back at the end of the day and found more bugs in the tub. Carpet in hallways very dirty. Rooms seems to be refinished, but very poor work in my opinion. I will not stay here again.

This isn't a bad place if you want to save a few bucks and don't need a lot of room. The studio rooms are very small, but have a kitchen which is nice. Request an inside room to cut down on the noise from the street... 71st is a busy road. The people at the front desk really aim to please and that's what make this place a pleasant place to come. Good location, just enough off the HWY to make it easy but not too noisy.

Very small bathroom..shower over small bath...room too small to use without door open (reduced size door)..no cotton buds, shower caps, etc..but Hotel will provide if requested..I paid $400 per night..I rate this room worth say $200...Nice room, but bathroom was so bad. 1 x tea bag provided + 1 bag of sugar..no milk. hardly worth the botther !..location is good, nice street and quiet, lots of restaurants nearby. Can walk to White House.. This Hotel is worth considering, but need to pay less than me!

The Kitano is a very professionally run, clean, well maintained, spacious hotel. The staff are helpful, the location is great, within easy walking distance of everwhere in midtown. As such there is nothing really bad to say about the hotel. I guess, just on a personal level it didnt leave me with the kind of energy that NYC itself does, a difficult thing for a hotel you might think but it can be done. However if youre looking for a well priced well located hotel you wont be disappointed

Considering the fact that the Liaison is billed as four star and costs a pretty penny there is not much to recommend it beyond location.The hotel rooms lacked 1) refrigerators, 2) microwaves, 3) couches, had no 4) exhaust fan in the bathroom, no 5) wireless internet in rooms without additional cost, 6) analog television reception was unclear. The hotel itself 7) lacked front desk or concierge customer service and no 8) shuttle service. 9) No coffee or tea was available in the lobby in the morning 10) etc. etc. etc. I could go on for days...

We stayed here for two nights. Great location for the riverwalk area. Hotel is within walking distance of mall and riverwalk. Hotel was clean and beds were comfortable. The King sleeper room has plenty of room. The staff was very helpful and friendly. Parking price ( $15/ night) was acceptable compared to surrounding hotels ($ 20-25/ per night). We would definitely stay here again. Hotel offers great deals online.

I liked the free internet, free bottle water, and the hotel being close to the metro. The staff is also very friendly. Little annoying things included, an unreasonable long wait to get checked in (3 receptionists 2 helping one guest and the third seemingly chatting with another about other hotels?), no local TV stations working, a somewhat tricky room key (remove slowly), and very hot hallways (it was an unusually warm Dec. day). I'd stay there again if the price was right, but wouldn't pay a premium.

Dont stay here! It was dirty! The website said they had a pool but when we got there it was drained. We asked and the manager said its been drained for a year if you dont like it go somewhere else! Horrible hotel only one working elevator and one working ice machine for 17 floors. The worst place I have ever stayed.

I stood one night at the Double Tree Hotel in San Diego and paid a bill of USD 325 for a room with view to airport and highway, a window that didn't close properly and let me enjoy all the noise from outside, cushion covers that were not properly washed, with smelly towels and a poor selection of soap and shampoo. The only positive point: my room was far away from the noisy ice machine. There are far better hotels in San Diego and I strongly recommend to avoid the Double Tree Hotel.

The Houston Hyatt was listening when someone said location, location, location. Too bad they were not listening to the lesson about updated and clean bathrooms. Nasy bathroom.. really? Hyatt is suppose to be a quality hotel chain. This property is not meeting that standard. Marriott has nothing to worry about.

We stayed at this hotel for a show at the Cobo Center. Great distance from the center. Breakfast was average. Coffee was not replenished thought. I was under the understanding that there was 24 Hr coffee. Disappointed 3 times! The elevators were super scary. One of the elevators we went into wouldnt even close! The others shaked and rattled. Ice machines were a joke! Never any! On a good note the rooms were clean and the staff was very friendly. But never got my extra towels I asked for!

I stand by the quality of the hotel itself, but the management has scared me away from returning again! Visibly drunk owners who yell at you every time they speak and lead you on a wild goose chase around the hotel instead of checking you in promptly, treat their employees like lesser people, and swear in front of the guests... hmm, that just doesn't match the charming ambience of the building. The front desk staff were okay, but certainly not exceptional. Several of the nice folks that were there last time I stayed have gone now. What a bummer.

The Sheraton doesn't offer anything out of the ordinary, but it is dependable and well-located. Staff was friendly, breakfast was good, the room was OK but needs a little updating, and the grounds and pool are attractive. You can do a lot worse. We asked for a quiet room and were happy to be given one. We were guests for four nights and there was only corridor noise on the Sat. night - though at 3 a.m. That's the guests' fault, however, not the hotel's.

The Palmer House is an older, classic hotel. Everything appeared to be well kept up. Room was very nicely equipped but rather small at least by more modern standards. New electronics with HD TV, including digital service on most channels. Comfortable bed and bedding. Bathroom was small and the shower a little dark and rather tight,

We had an overnight layover at IAH and selected this hotel because it had a free shuttle to the airport. You are not allowed to make reservations for the shuttle. The shuttle was full and we were forced to take a taxi. The management told us this happens often and offered little sympathy.

We stayed two nights at the Sheraton Austin. Last time we came to Austin, we stayed at the Hyatt and found it a little too far to walk to everything. This location was perfect! Walking distance to the capital, UT and 6th street. Room was clean and bed comfortable. We had a late dinner at the bar, delicious Hummus and Pita Bread appetizer. Definitely will stay here on our next visit.

Great room for the price but the main reason we stayed here was the airport shuttle and free parking while on vacation. When we got there, there was no record of my advanced booking of the shuttle. They were able to pick me up so it worked out. When we returned, the shuttle was suppose to pick us up(I made the reservation when I checked in). Once again no shuttle. However the hotle covered most of th cab fair.

front desk staff were extremely rude, to the point me and my family left the city a day earlier than originally planned... And lack of thorough communication among staff delayed our check in by approximately 3 hours which is unacceptable due to having small children. Will never consider staying at this hotel again!

I've never written a review of a hotel, though I rely on TripAdvisor all the time. I've chosen to write because of the terrible customer service that I received here and the ridiculously outdated rooms that are straight from the 1960s. In addition, the bellmen damaged my laptop while it was in storage for the afternoon. This hotel is not up to SPG standards.
