Parking was really expensive, the dining areas were crowded for our event. Stayed here cause out convention was here and they gave us a decent rate. We only had one meal and it was hot and good, with good service. the room was so tight the servers were always bumping us.

The hotel is an easy walk down to the inner harbor, the convention center and Camden Yards. The service at the front desk was very good and attentive, but the property is showing some signs of needing attention. By no means are the rooms bad, but the carpets show signs of needing cleaning in places, and the furniture and fixtures show plenty of signs of dings and chipped paint. These are minor detractions, and you will find that the Sheraton "Sweet Sleeper" beds here are as comfortable and crisp as you might expect.

I can tell you just this words " DO NOT BOOK A ROOM AT THIS DIRTY AND HORRIBLE HOTEL" I have paid 3 nights for this hotel to expedia But i didn't stayed and couldn't get back my money. Room are so dirty and whole hotel smells cigarette.When i went to room i feel myself in horror movie.Do not look the pictures on hotel website.The photos was taken 20 years ago.Nothing is same at hotel currently. Please friends do not waste your money !!

Good location. We were on the 4th floor, it was quite a walk from the room to the elevator. There was some noise at night from doors banging and suitcases, but not too bad. The room was nice and clean and the bathroom a good size. We got 50% off parking as we booked through Virgin. No breakfast included.

We stayed at the Hotel Palomar for a girls weekend in town. Nice location and rooms were well appointed. Valet parking was a bit of a fiasco, but overall would recommend. Close proximity to el, Michigan Avenue shopping and good restaurants. It's a little touristy, but for folks from out of town, this is good :)

After staying at a few budget motels within Arizona, we were expecting the Red Roof Inn to have a few more of the amenities that the others had. There was no fridge or microwave, and no coffee maker in the room, although there is coffee available downstairs in the lobby. There is nothing really nearby to the inn, aside from a mexican supermarket and fast food places. The room was very clean, but the two beds in the room were only double. Perhaps if space is an issue for you, you would be better off booking a king room.

Best hotel staff we've experienced in many years. Antwan, Peter, Rony and Ken were so pleasant and efficient. Even the smallest request received an immediate response with a "smile". The entire staff was attentive and engaging. We rode the elevator with several members of the staff at different times. Each time we were asked how we were enjoying our visit. The hotel is clean and well kept. We will defiinitely choose The Strand when we go to NYC.

this place makes youn feel better than home!!! the beds are so soft when you lay on them you wanna just stay sleeping!!! its nice and clean with the best servise!! nice breakfast in the morning!!clean pool!!!! the best staff in the front desk!!!! Francis is verry nice and always smiling. vibian always at your service and Mary the boss is always checking if you are comfortable!!!! this place is about customer servise!!!

Offered airport shuttle, but none was available to take me to the airport, Promised they'd be there to pick me up, Did not show up, finally told me to take a shuttle. The room reeked of smoke so much that when I got to my destination, friends could smell smoke on my clothes.. When I complained the manager just said sorry.

Stayed for one night October 26, 2011. Not really dirty, but ugly/in need of repair. Room 219's bathroom counter was half torn-off, wallpaper (if it can be called that) was peeling off the bathroom wall. Halls looked dirty and smelled of smoke. Front desk even looked trashy, staff not very helpful. No pride of ownership at all.

For San Fran, rooms tend to be smaller for the price. This hotel however had very outdated bathrooms with toilets looking as if they were from army barracks/guys locker room, was very small, and did not even include a basic coffee-maker. There were limited plugs for charging phones/camera etc and the front desk staff, albiet friendly, were less than knowledgeable about surrounding restaurants/coffee shops. Overall just outdated, lacking attention to detail for the price. The location is great but there are ample other hotels in the area for around the same price.

Chicago has always been "my kind of town" and now the Talbott is my favorite hotel in the Windy City. A lovely boutique hotel, close to the Magnificent Mile. The staff was wonderful - friendly, capable, great attention to detail and couldn't do enough for you. The IT manager actually typed a letter for me that had to go on some fairly complcated statioenry so I would not miss any of my meeting and there was no extra charge. Food was very good, bar and restaurant service great. This is a real gem.

The hotel is hidden but its quiet and safe. I enjoyed my stay and was surprised at the attention from staff. Every staff member you encounter talks to you and the room was very nice for 75 bucks. I had small issues such as water marks on the mirror and needed a couple extra towels but I called down to the front desk and it was very quickly taken care of and apologized for several times. I guess there is a change over in staff and I think its helping. I will definitely stay here again.

Return from Panama too late for connecting flight so I stayed here with check in @ 2AM! While the LAX airport is lousy in every way (one hour taxi from touchdown, 20 minute bus ride to gate, one hour wait for US Immigration/Customs) this hotel met all needs for quick check-in, clean and quiet room, prompt and courteous airport shuttle, and surprising full breakfast with real eggs! While I hope not to use LAX again for flying, if need be, this place is just fine!

I think this is the most out-standing working at this hotel I find her as a magnificent worker!! Because of her I will return!!! And by the way I am talking about Claudia Cardoso. She just has to be one of the most sweetest people I have ever meet!! I hope you guys tell her about my review because she deserves more than to know! She is fantastic with customers!!!

with a little effort the quality of that hotel could improve considerably, but the owner and staff DO NOT CARE: they have clients even if they keep the place shabby like it is now, just because it's new york and there are always tourists... it's revolting&insane that the prices are so high for such a shabby place...

We just spent two nights in the Austin Sheraton and while the location is great, the hotel is not up to snuff for the Sheraton brand. The hotel room was much dirtier than we would expect. The towels had hair on them, the tub wouldn't drain and the hotel info cards were pretty filthy. Also the hotel and hallways had a very musty smell that made it quite unpleasant to walk to the room. We definitely will look for another place to stay next time we are in Austin.

The staff were friendly and the hotel was very clean. Within a few blocks walking distance to the Science Centre, Monorail and Space Needle. The free breakfast was a nice touch. We originally had reservations at the Best Western, but were turned away by them as they would only accept a credit card as payment, not cash or debit card. The Best Western sent us to the Travelodge which does accept cash as payment. We are thankful they did as we were very happy with the Travelodge!

We found the hotel to be adequate and clean, the staff was courteous and friendly. Our Room was average size, but too close to the elevator, which we could here constantly "swooshing" up and down. The restaurant was nice but quite expensive; there is a simple cafe next door for breakfast. Parking is valet only, and $40 a day, but they were very responsive about getting the car whenever we needed it.

What a great trip we had to New York, and the Warwick Hotel was a major reason for our great time. The location is absolutely unbeatable-Times Square, Central Park, Rockefeller Center, even the subway is just a short walk. We upgraded our room and were pleasantly surprised by the size. The staff was incredible, including helping us to check in as early as possible after taking an overnight flight. Can't wait for our next trip to New York.

I had the pleasure of staying at the Affinia Shelburne on business a few months ago and this was one of my best experiences at a New York hotel yet. The staff was personable and attentive. The room was clean and comfortable and the roof top veiws- priceless. I will definitely be back!

I do not like to write bad reviews but I really felt like saying this. I mistakenly stayed at Deca during my one week CE course at UW. The rooms, commodities and service are those of a 3 star hotel but they charge like a five star one. You can hear everything from the next rooms and the hotel does nothing when someone is being too noisy.

I had no hot water, the t.v. was broken, it smelled, we could hear the people next door (thin walls), it was sketchy at night, the exercise equipment was also broken, and worst of all the staff was so rude. This hotel charged me for a night's stay that i wasn't there for, and then couldn't reverse the charges and gave me some weird line about not believing me. The manager, Angela Hentz, said i was mean. I had to dispute it through my credit card company. DO NOT STAY HERE!

This room was a great value for 4 of us splitting the price. We were able to avoid the parking pass because it is an easy walk to the fairgrounds. It was the perfect base place and the beds were very comfortable and it was quiet. The hotel is older,and there is nothing fancy about it, but they do thier best with what they have. The shower leaked under the wall into the bedroom and one of our suitcases got wet, but they willingly gave us a discount.

I was relocated after Priceline.com messed up my booking, and the hotel sent me here. The room was dirty, the towels and sheets smelled like hospital linen. The breakfast sucked, the wifi was weak. I kept using the stairs, I was worried that the elevator would get stuck. Do not stay here if you want a clean room, and do not use PRICELINE....

The hotel was in a great location but the staff was horrible. The front desk manager was an absolute nightmare. He had no customer service skills, super rude. The room was very dirty. The towels in the restroom were stained, possibly soiled. The hotel needs some renovation. Also the hotel charged an additional twenty dollars to check in early. we checked in an hour early and they would not even waive the fee. Very disappointed with this hotel. I have stayed in other Ramada hotels and the stay was pleasant.

My stay Was Ok....Room was not clean the way it should have been clean upon check in. I had some personal issues that i needed to talk to the manager about. I think his Name was Rian,or Ryan, and he seemed to not care with an attitude!.So because of him im not staying there anymore,and plus the cleaniness ofthe hoteland rooms.

The room felt like a prison cell. It was tiny. The window looked out to a brick wall only a few feet away. The drapes covered up the HVAC system. The shower head came out of the wall perpendicular to the tub and sprayed everywhere but on me. The bathroom was a six inch step up compared to the level of the rest of the room. The continental breakfast was the only highlight.

Great location, near clubs and restaurants. It's a Marriott, can't go wrong with it. Nice rooms, great amenities. The only downside is that AT&T doesn't have a good signal in the rooms. It is not a complaint about the hotel, just something to be aware of if you are depending on your cellphone to make calls / surf the net.

A very nice hotel with a cool/quirky feel. The rooms were a little small but I also don't really need a ton of room in my hotel, and that's also typical for boutique hotels, I think. The staff was very helpful when I asked for help, which I did several times. Gas fireplace and squishy couches in the lobby were nice, and good location. I would definitely stay again.

We stayed here for a night due to a long layover from HNL to ABQ. The room was just OK. What really disappointed me is that there were room service plates all over the place. The plates we saw when we arrived were still sitting in the same place when we left in the morning. There was certainly more than enough time to get those picked up overnight. It left an impression of a dirty hotel.

Don't bother staying at this establishment as the service, level of cleanliness and quality of rooms are probably better at a Holiday Inn. Our room smelled of pet urine, there is absolutely no venilation in the bathrooms, the shower was falling apart, the linen was tattered (including the spa robe), etc. Expect beauty and grandiosity at the lobby-level, but not beyond. Do your self a favor and continue your search. I will never stay at the Waldorf again.

Service was fantastic, location was great and value was great. Very nice hotel but it needs a renovation in the near future. The rooms are good but not great. The shower was OK. The lobby is really nice. I would stay there again for sure. But when I think Ritz-Carlton I think "creme de la creme" and this didnt quite meet my expectations. Also they charge for wi-fi. But the gym is really great! And the staff was helpful. It rained the whole time and there were ample umbrellas for guests to use.

Great location!! Very welcoming and helpful staff!!! Neat and clean rooms - nothing fancy, but just perfect. Good size room, good size bathroom and a really nice bed!!! We stayed on the 8th floor and had a nice view. Can definately recommend this hotel if your looking for a no nonsence hotel in a great location. Will for sure stay here again if we go bcak to Boston in the future......

Excellent hotel with very helpful staff and concierge. The rooms are large for a city centre hotel and very comfortable. The concierge and reception staff could not have been more helpful. Breakfast could be taken in the railway themed bar which was ok but a bit dark and dingy for me but there weren't many alternatives immediately nearby...service for breakfast was excellent some days and average others. We had Dinner in the hotel one night because we were very tired, the service was good but the food wasn't.

Been there in August and one really good thing is the location right beside Beale St and all those terrific blues bars! This is what really stands out. Room was very large, as well as bed. Decoration is very old style, you can check it out in their website, but you probably won't spend so many time in the room. Front desk is just ok, providing basic information, but far far from being friendly. It was worth the price and close to Beale, so all the rest didn't bother us at all.

Hotel location, staff and aesthetics/decor were all good. I was slightly disappointed when I called room service and asked to order a soup from the full restaurant menu, but was told the only options were on the in room dining menu (or I could come down to the restaurant). Gratuity and service charge were 22% of the total bill. The disclaimer stated 16% was gratuity with the remaining 6% an administrative charge. However, hotel charges an additional $5.00 in-room charge -- which was a first for me, and seemed quite high.

The worst mattresses I have ever experienced in a hotel this nice.... see the pictures. Beautiful hotel with a great location, excellent service, and great views... but what difference does that all make if the beds are less comfortable than the industrial carpet lined concrete floors. The second night we changed to a room with a king bed and a roll away which was slightly better. $17 self parking $26 valet per day plus very pricey typically unimpressive hotel food breakfasts. No coffee maker.

This was my first business trip to NY and I was delighted to stay at this comfortable and clean Inn with such helpful staff. They were accommodating, personable and genuinely helpful -- but be sure to ask. There was an ample breakfast buffet each morning and although I was longing for some fresh fruit, it was satisfying. The location is great! It's only about 6 blocks to the subway, the 1/2 price Broadway-play ticket kiosk, and an even shorter walk to all the sights and activities of the seaport.

My wife and daughter stayed at this hotel in June 2012. This was a last minute booking and they just needed a place to sleep for one night. The location was convenient to central Austin and UT. They stated that the front desk employees were very nice and very helpful. The rooms were adequate and clean. They had no issues during their stay.

The hotel is in a great location. The service was great. The place was very clean. The rooms was very tiny for the price. You can stay at another hotel for less money and be more comfortable in your room. No room for your bags, no room to put your toiletries,

This hotel is a wonderful place as a base for a leisurely trip to the nation's capital or a serious business meeting. At night, the hotel turns into a peaceful place to unwind after a busy day. The hotel also has a great lounge area to offer an excellent choice of drinks (wonderful decor!). The hotel is a great fit for mature guests.

Copley house is a series of charming "Brownstones" very convieniently located in a leafy historic area within walking distance of the Metro, restaurants and the large, central shopping mall. It is a quiet street where residents obviously take pride in their homes and gardens yet very close to trendy Royalston and Newbury Sttreets The obliging,efficient reception staff provided all the necessary maps and information we needed .and when we left some important medications behind,these were couriered to us in Washington the next day. We felt that we were experiencing the local "colour" and history in staying here

My husband and I stayed at the Eliot for our anniversary. We arrived Easter evening. The staff was helpful, polite and professional...and you get a real key! Our suite was newly updated, everything immaculate. The location was convenient for everything we wanted to do. Parking was handled by valets as the parking situation in Boston seems to be impossible. I highly recommend the Eliot.

Our room seemed to be showing some wear and tear. The mattress was not comfortable at all. Felt like I was sort of falling into the middle of the bed. Not horrible but I wouldn't give it top ratings either. Wireless very difficult to get onto. We finally gave up.

Stayed 3 nights in a room with kitchenette because hotels thru-out Chicago were booked full. Lots of space. Kitchenette had microwave, stove, mini fridge, sink, utensils. However, carpet, bathroom & room itself generally felt dated and heavily used. Had to call housekeeping once to get toilet to flush. They responded immediately and sent someone up with a plunger. Room was a bit noisy with people out in the hall and doors opening/closing. Free washers & dryers for guest use, plus free detergent and Bounce. Free purified water is available in the hallway (they provide re-fillable plastic bottles).

This hotel was nice but nothing special. Great location if you want to be in Times Square. Carpet in the room was worn and dirty. 2nd floor lobby was very dark. Key access in elevator was not operational, anyone could use the elevator (poor security). No place to pull off of the street to unload your car, just the curb.

The Grand Hyatt is in a terrific location. We upgraded to the concierge level which I would suggest as you get a great cont breakfast every morning (in NY this saves a bunch of $) and waters, sodas, coffee, etc. You also get free internet but you have to remind them to reverse it from the bill. Service is fine for NY, the bathrooms are very small (typical NY) but all in all a very nice stay. The concierge in the lobby was very helpful and the hotel seems well maintained.

Stayed for 2 nights in the W Hotel DC, check-in was very professional and offered me a choice of rooms due to my platinum status. However, on second night there was music until 1:30am in the bar upstairs that I could hear in my room. Called the concierge repeatedly and they said "this is the W experience". The concierge was rude and dismissive. They're more concerned with their bar guests experience than their business travellers sleep on a Thursday night. Not staying here again.

A three day post cruise stay at the Westin, was the perfect pick-me-up for the experiences of the Celebrity Century, friendly eager and helpful staff, great for giving tourist advice and assisted with a late check out at 3.00pm when our flight home was at 8.05pm. Great rooms, fast lift, Rooms serviced without fuss, free wi-fi in the foyer a welcome bonus after being out of Scotland for so long. Many Thanks Weir's

We stayed here on 2days, came to watch a hockey game. The room was big but the sofa bed where my daughters were slepping was not good; the mattress was very thin & it felt like you were sleeping in a blanket with bumps; the floor was better to sleep on..no complaints about the main bed. The room was clean, elevator was broken when we got there & there is $20 parking fee per day. I wasn't too impressed with this hotel, I was expecting more for a Hilton hotel & for the price that we paid.

Highly recommended for travel. The staff is as good as you will ever find. The food is superb. We made the mistake of going out for our Thanksgiving meal to a nearby Beverly Hills lux hotel (not a Four Seasons.) Big mistake. They really make you feel welcome in spite of the number of celebs that are around.

please do not book this hotel it is disgusting and you will be very disappointed I stayed there with my daughter we had to change rooms as sheets and mattresses were filthy the room they moved us too wasnt alot better, no hot water so they had to let us use another persons room the corridors smelt of Cats pee and it was very damp. Keep looking for hotels cause there are some as cheap but better quality and clean

Stayed all last week and enjoyed the convenience of this hotel near F line trolley stop and a bit out of the way (quieter) from the mess that is the Fisherman's Wharf T-shirt neighborhood. Good gym. Friendly service staff. The downside was the dated room decor which is dark brown and very heavy. Depressing after a couple days. Also the bed was half-broken. Linens and bath nice. Room service meals are well above average. Hotel restauraunt sports bar (Knuckles) is nice but pricy. Strongly recommend the Breakfast Grill across the street - fast, tasty, good price/value.

Everything was lovely and we enjoyed all the attention to detail. The room was very comfortable and had everything we could think of. Quiet and comfortable for my twin 16 year old boys and for me. We had enough room in the room with a sleeper sofa in one room and a big bed in the bedroom. Bathroom was very nice.

This hotel is very well located near the corner of Hollywood/Highland. The room was very comfortable and clean with a fridge and microwave. The bathroom is big enough but have the shower inside of the bath (not my favorite). The staff were very friendly, helpful and efficient. The only drawback was the breakfast with has to be classified as poor. Exactly the same everyday and limited choice.

I stayed at this hotel while I was in San Antonio. The staff is absolutely wonderful! I have stayed with several different hotels in San Antonio, as I am in town often, and this has to be the BEST hotel ever. Again, the staff is wonderful. I was greeted by name each time I came in the door. This is going to be my new home away from home. I highly recommend everybody stay here!

picked because it was close to airport and I thought it offered free parking if flying from Denver.Found that not to be the case.Also hot tub was out of service.I always use the hot tubs as I am not into swimming.This was a big damper.I was not informed that there were issues with this when I checked in.

My son and I stayed here for a 5 day trip to NYC this month. Really nice and clean hotel, with nice location in the meatpacking district, which seemed to be the "hotspot" for young upscale bars, etc. European style free breakfast daily. Nicely appointed rooms, not large and spacious, but standard size for NYC and comfortable. Located close to subway station for good access to all boroughs. Staff very helpful and friendly with great recommendations for restaurants, sites, etc. Would definitely stay there again.

My daughter lives in San Antonio and we visit frequenty and we stay at this hotel often,however, stayed in this hotel 8/11/12 in a suite and the pool was dirty and cloudy. dogs were barking and kids were running upstairs from our suite at night. The person behind the desk her shirt was so wrinkled what a a bad impression. The place was runned down and diety looking we will not stay in this place again, No free internet service and they could not resolve it A/C not strong enough to cool both rooms

The hotel was nice and clean. We had a king-size bed suite and it was very roomy. The only drawback (and it has nothing to do with the hotel) was the location. It was off of I-270 and the main restaurant choices are fast-food chains. But the area looks like it is being developed more.

Been here three days and only one of the hotel's two elevators has worked the entire time. On top of that the elevator that does "work" frequently doesn't respond to guest's key cards (which are required for guest floor access) so the whole car full of people rides up to the top floor with frustrated guests who then exit as the elevator works its way back down. And stairways are not an option, emergency exit only. If you do stay here don't stay on any floor below six or you'll feel the bass rumble from the lobby bar.

We stayed here for a week, and got engaged in one of the rooms! The hotel had great views over the river and the rooftop restaurant was lovely - breakfast was great. The hotel was clean and spacious, and well-located. We walked everywhere from the hotel. Didn't have much interaction with the staff, and it was quite expensive, but we were happy with the hotel.

I saw very bad review, on line, even then I made my reservation on this property, because I am well aware of Days Inn reputation. At the time of check in feel homely atmosphere.After I got my room key I went to my room and found every thing was neat and clean and I was very Impressed.

The rooms were nice, the service fine. But Friday night partiers outside the room at 2 am, yelling and swearing... not good. Another man and his woman fighting in parking lot 2 days later. And the continental breakfast was pathetic. Frosted Flakes cereal, milk, rolls in plastic and coffee seems like the absolute minimum to qualify for the name.

We stayed here the night before our cruise in July. The staff was awesome. There was one african American lady that worked the front and the bar that I give five stars to. She is a hard working lady who has several jobs. I hope she enjoy the bar recipes book we gave her. We can't wait for our next visit!!!!! The beds was so comfortable!!!

I frequently use La Quintas when I travel and was quite disappointed with the this particular property. Although the staff and management do their best, this is a decidedly older hotel and it shows. The housekeepers need to work harder at room cleanliness and the furniture needs to be cleaned and/or replaced. I usually enjoy the breakfast at La Quinta's, but this one seems to have missed the boat and was lacking. Fortunately there is a great Mexican restaurant next door that serves breakfast, and a Denny's just two exits south.

Not a 4 stars, not a 3 stars, not a 2 stars! We arrived on a Friday afternoon, and our rooms were ready juste at 8PM!! The desk is asked to leave our luggage and return later. The hotel is quite old, everything is well-worn and a little run down. Carpets do not inspire. Strangely, none of services are working: the pool was in the works, as well as the gym. The staff is not unpleasant but it is slow. The WiFi is not free ($ 15 a day!)

Nice downtown location, friendly staff, decent enough rooms. A good choice if you're looking for an inexpensive (for the area), no-frills stay. Neither my girlfriend nor I had any complaints, but neither of us can really remember anything outstanding, either. Seemed to be quite popular with families traveling with kids, which could be a plus or a minus, depending on what you're looking for. Not my first choice for the area, but I'd stay there again and recommend it to anyone looking to stay near the White House on a budget.

I stay at a lot of Starwood hotels and am impressed by the personal service and attention offered with every stay and the general decor and amenities at this particular Sheraton. It has more character than most hotels in this chain, is a great value for the location, and has a nice gym.

The hotel was located near the ocean which made for beautiful scenery, unfortunately the rooms were a little outdated and one of our beds had hair all over it work we checked in. the shower heads definitely could use some replacing. It is not very handicap friendly, we has a newborn with a stroller and it was hard to get into areas. But they were awesome at trading us around the island because we didn't rent a car. With all of that said, I would stay there again. Just with hopes that some changes will have been made.

The location in Japantown is great if you want to take advantage of Japantown. I am a walker; so being fairly far from most of the top places to visit in SF is not a problem. I expected it to have more of an authentic flavor of Japan and the culture. Not really. Won't bother to stay here again.

I frequently stay at the Sheraton Suites and I have to say in addition to the comfort and and peace and quiet,the front desk staff and van drivers go out of their way to assist whenever I need information or a ride somewhere in the area. Keep up the great service!

I agree with the other reviews - too noisy to sleep until the flights stopped and then a very early alrm call as they resumed. Also very basic room which is in drastic need of renovation. My first experience of Super 8 - (but unfortunately my second occurred a couple of days later - I'd booked through Hotwire so couldn't cancel after the first negative experience - last time I use them too as the prices aren't that much lower and they are totally inflexible re changes to plans.

This is a great place to stay. My wife and I have stayed at this motel 3 to 4 times a year for the past 15 years. The service is always great, the rooms are very clear (no bed bugs - ever!) nicely appointed, quiet and very secure. The TV, wireless network, air conditioning, refrigerator and micro wave have always worked nicely without any problems. I would recommend this motel very highly, there is never any problems staying here.

I arrived at this hotel after 11 pm and was a little concerned that the door was locked and a glass enclosure for the only employee desk clerk. However, the property was OK, breakfast was good, and I was just traveling through for a good night sleep. I had my small dog with me so I needed a pet-friendly hotel. It is located right off I-71 so it was convenient and very easy to find.

After reading all the reveiws, I think my expectations were set to high. This is a nice budget hotel, but # 1 on Trip Advisor? Really? We stayed on our way to a cruise ship departure in Galveston and found the hotel to be good value for the money and that's all I can really say about it.

When i stayed at this hotel is was the best ever. Every day you got FIJI water instead of drinking tap water, they offer you there all and every night they come to open your bed up that is of course u want them to any how it was a wonderful stay there and i want to go back soon.

Good value for your money! Nice, clean rooms, free parking, located in downtown Chicago. The staff is very friendly and helpful too! A perfect place to stay, walking distance to great restaurants, shopping and the Metro. Went in for a few days with my wife to go see the Sox play the Yankees. I highly recommend this place (my wife and her friends have stayed here for years.)

We stayed at the Westin Copley Place in April for a conference. We had three rooms in our party. The higher floors definitely have a better view, but the location of the hotel is fantastic. It is steps from the Liberty Trail & the Boston Public Library. Our room was average, but loved the Starbucks coffee machine (like Keurig) in the room. And we always enjoy the Heavenly bed of Westins.

Thank you so much for the wonderful time we had staying at your hotel. The staff were absolutlely fantastic. So friendly and helpful. They took an interest in what our plans were for the day. We had a birthday dinner in the dining room mmmm good. Again friendly staff . The hotel is so convenient to everything. The decor was awesome. We will definitely want to stay in your hotel again.\ Robert and Theresa Cross

I stayed 5 night with my friend to celeberate our birthdays. First impression was good until we step in our "de luxe" room. Actually there was no window, because across the window was wall and I really mean wall. Just horrible! After asking they gave us new room. Staff was ok, but not very helpful. One doormen smelled strongly alcohol, really. Location is great, breakfast was ok ( staff not), rooms okay, if you have a window :-) With good customer service this could be very good hotel.

My wife and I booked this hotel online, the website is misleading; this hotel is in the middle of the industrial area nowhere near any of the sites you want to see, it is an old run down place that is in poor condition and not fit for anyone who likes to be comfortable. The area it is in is very poor and seedy and not where you want to stay as a couple and bring your kids there; no way. Stay away from this one, it is not worth the time.

Uphill location, good view but the rooms are small. Shower pressure was very low, at least in our room. Besides a bar of soap, shampoo and conditioner the hotel offers no other amenities; some cotton swabs, comb or toothbrush should be standard for a chain hotel. Bring your own slippers. Overall an ok hotel, nothing to write home about. Practical for biz travelers, not so much for families w small kids.

It was such a great experience to stay in this hotel! We both enjoyed it and we loved the fact everyone made us feel welcome! The staff is so friendly!!!! The pool was relaxing! Our room was very clean and well organized! Anthony was so great! He checked us in after we had a rough afternoon (Rain/Tornado warnings) he definitely made our stay feel MUCH better!!! I would definitely recommend this to anyone!

Walls are so thin you can hear people in the bathroom next door as well as snoring. There is some type of large bus parked outside the right side of the hotel from 5:30am-ish to 7:15am with its engines idling which causes a vibratory noise in the room. Its awful. All the lighting is bright flourescent. Energy efficient...I get it but don't they have subdued energy efficient lights these days? Service was so-so. I mentioned the bus and they rolled thier eyes. The HVAC system is loud and terrible.

the hotel was very big inside with a huge bar and outdoor pull no hot tub the sheets made me and my wife break out, they had bugs in the room.room service it was disgusting.. this hotel may be meant for a low life vacation hotel if your looking for a (want to be) marriot and its not even close folks,stay clear (NOT A GOOD PLACE TO LAY YOUR HEAD!)

Room smelled, the carpet was wet in some portions of the room. I opened the window and paint chipped and cracked and went everywhere. The box of tissues in the bathroom was wet!? This is a classic hotel and could be nice if they were to work on the upkeep and updates. They probably have some very nice rooms - but this one was bad and I've heard from other folks staying with me that the rooms were old and smelled. Disappointing.

Very close to Philadelphia Int. airport. Close to downtown and very close to sporting complexes. The staff was very professional and very helpful. The Hotel itself is a bit dated but very nice, the sports bar serves good burgers and sandwiches at reasonable prices ($12.00 for a huge burger and more fries than you can eat). I wouldn't say this is a "vacation" type hotel, it's an "airport" hotel, the views are parking lots and runways, but for a quick visit to Philly it will meet all your needs.

I actually didn't have high hopes since I had a perhaps inaccurate and outdated view of what a Marriott property is like. However this hotel far exceeded my expectations. Very comfortable bed, quiet, clean, contemporary. Good buffet breakfast which was included in the price. We were on th 26th floor so there was sometimes a bit of a wait for the elevator, but that was minor.

Our family of 6 stayed at the Pearl for 8 days and was never disappointed. The staff was attentive and helpful. Gave wonderful recommendations of places to eat and how to get great deals. Azi, one of the doormen, was fabulous, always remembered our names and gave great suggestions. The rooms were beautiful and spacious and the location was amazing. Just steps away from Hells Kitchen, theaters and Times Square. We will definitely be staying at The Pearl the next time we visit.

I think it is completely irresponsible to continue to book rooms while the hotel is undergoing construction and not let customers know prior to the booking. This is an otherwise nice hotel, but when I'm paying $300+/night, I don't want to be awakened every morning with hammering. Another disincentive to staying at this hotel is the lack of coffee/tea in the rooms. Who wants to go downstairs in the morning to get their first cup of coffee?

One small elevator from the lobby is not what I would expect other than in a small boutique hotel in Europe. The concierge seemed to be surly and a little condescending when asked a simple question regarding walking directions. We parked the car with the valet, which is terribly overpriced at $51.30 per night including tax.

The hotel has a great staff. Check-in was pleasant, friendly and efficient. My room was nicely decorated and quite comfortable. The bed was excellent with a nice selection of pillows. The room and bathroom were not large and there was no view to speak of. The furnishings were good quality and well maintained. There was a large flat screen TV. There were two things lacking that are important to me; no easy chair and no good reading light. Even the lamp on the desk did not have a very bright light.

I have stayed here using my HIlton Honor points and did enjoyed my stay with a good view of Times Square and the convenience of being able to walk out and the hotel and to be in the middle of a happening city! The room is big and the only down side is I would have preferred if the toiletries are of the former brand used. Also I find the bed a big hard to sleep in. All in, recommended! Services is great too.

Stayed for two nights in October 2012. The hotel is all right. It is probably filled during the week and shows the wear. The location is good. Rooms are large. Having the kitchen in the suite is a plus. All clean enough. Price seemed a bit on the high side, but is probably market price for that area of Austin. Free breakfast was minimal. Much prefer the Dunkin Donuts down the road. Nothing happened that would cause me not to stay there again.

Spent a week here earlier this month. It's an ok hotel but lacks the detail to make it a really nice, enjoyable hotel. The positives are: nice location, lovely views of the space needle (from the right side of the hotel :)), rooms are quiet and spacious. However, they charge for internet (I cannot understand hotels of this size charging as much as they do for internet access in this day and age), no shower gel in bathroom, long wait for lifts, no bottled water in the room, and the quality of the room service food was not good.

Don't expect to park a car if your driving, and if you get a parking spot don't go nowhere. You could end up parking several blocks away. Resturants are not in emidiate vicinity. Not a place you want to walk at night. No really close convient stores, so purchase anything you want to take to the room before you get there.

the rooms were clean but very out dated. the shower head was a little short. the location was good we were right off the freeway and there was local shopping just a few blocks down the street. and there was also a few good restaurants to choose from as well. we were only about 10 min from sea world. next year me and my husband are most likely going to find a different place to stay. this hotel was ok for the price.

Charming hotel centrally located right next to the White House. Easy to find food and bars any time day or night. Subway stop is downstairs. The place is quiet, staff is nice. French bistro on the ground floor was excellent, big portions, and reasonably priced (try the tuna). Our AC went out in our room and they moved us within 15 minutes. It was 1am. Could not have been happier. Maybe not a great place for families, but it is ideal for couples.

We are here for the ABO conference, and i am day after day disappointed by the very bad service at this hotel. It might be big enough for a conference for 800 people, but that is were its good qualities end. Check in was a horrendous wait, and food service for the conference has riddled with silly rules about which food live is open and when. Coffee is almost never available and sodas are non-existent. Algenol sponsored an evening, and it seemed very very expensive for what the hotel provided. shame on you

Stayed at the hotel for a quick trip to the city. The hotel is very near Times Square and all of the shows. It is a very large hotel however I thought that Inhira who was the representative that checked me in was great. Really no complaints, a very nice stay close to everything that we needed. Wish that I could stay longer and experience more of the hotel.

I cannot recommend this hotel. We stayed and prepaid 4 nights (3 persons). We had to leave one day earlier than planned. We received no refund, allthough we immediately announced this upon arrival. Our bathroom was leaking water and we had to change room. Breakfast is even worse than continental breakfast. The boiled eggs are one week old on ice. Smelly :-( We will avoid this next time --- a pity! Only full beds available (No Queensize, nor kingsize.)

Hotel is in need for a complete remodel. Run down rooms, halls, Place is on the dirty side. Location is great, but NO parking, If Windsor would remodel, this would be a nice place to stay. rooms are over priced for what is offered. this hotel is Only for a single college kid that is used to sleeping in a dump.

My husband and I had the opportunity to visit Houston this weekend for a short get away and stayed at Hotel Derek, Galleria. The hotel was very nice, great location and the staff were amazing and exceeded our expectations. They were friendly, attentive and very professional. We'll definitely be staying again.

The lobby, pool and bar are a very pleasant setting with lots of greenery and comfortable seating. However, internet access is not included in the room rate and there is no breakfast. In addition, the water restrictors they have put in the sink faucets cut the water flow so drastically, you have to chase the water drops around to wet your toothbrush. Shower was adequate. Rooms are small and dark. Shuttle to airport was fast and efficient.

Stayed at the Howard Johnson for one night. The hotel was fine,if a little tired. The room had a mini fridge, microwave, iron/board coffer maker. Airport shuttle and breakfast. The service of the gentleman at the front desk was very professional and fast. I would stay there again if needing an airport hotel.

The hotel is situated just a block away from the L (elevated train). It is one line to Midway airport and also one line to the museum campus (no transfers necessary). The Museum of Science and Industry is one bus ride (#10) away which is also on the same block as the hotel. Magnificent Mile is a short, easy walk. We were impressed by how helpful and friendly the staff were. Anything from helpful restaurant choices to providing my wife with some bandages, they were just wonderful. The only negative was the lack of a mini-refrigerator in the room.

mold in the shower - wouldn't be too difficult to clean. the cleaners obviously don't step into the shower, otherwise they would see it by the door. no wheelchair access - my mother who had a broken foot had to crawl up entrance stairs. uncomfortable pillows - felt like i was sleeping on a 20 year old cushion. the pictures looked nice! the rooms need to be remodeled like the reception area has been

I could not get out of that hotel fast enough, I didn't experience a ghost but there was just something awful in the air, I felt like I had walked into an Alfred Hitchcock movie. My piece of advice ...STAY CLEAR OF THAT PLACE! I was booked for 3 days, I lasted only 2 hrs and grabbed a room at the Marriott Courtyard.

I stayed one night out of a 3-night booking - actually did not even sleep there the full night. Upon check in, the parking garage off-site in a dimly lit parking lot, unsecured area with lots of seedy people loitering about. The manager/staff could care less. Very disappointed, I would not stay again.

The hotel is nice, however be warned that they will charge your credit card upward of $400 upfront for "incidental" charges that may occur during your stay. This may be standard, but it seems quick sketchy to charge so much up front when they have your credit card information on file and can charge for incidentals after they actually occur).

This hotel was fabulous. Perhaps the best staff I've ever encountered at a hotel. Extraordinarily well-trained. The room was fabulous. The location perfect unless you want to be in the middle of the shopping (it's still close to it). It would be the first choice for us next time in Seattle!

Older motel that needs to be updated; the rooms are larger but older!! Wi-fi is free, but doesn't work properly. Free aiport pickup-the driver is very freindly and has plenty of information to offer. The staff at the motel could be friendlier--the motel needs updating badly. Starting with the comforter and the furniture--There are better places out there!!

The site says they're renovating the pool. However, the workout room is now in a small conference room. The construction noise is so loud throughout the hotel during the day you can't hear yourself think. The breakfast is great but the lines prevent you from taking advantage. The managers reception is chips and most other embassy suites/homewood suites, etc., have real food. The hotel is old, cold and after staying at the Hilton Mag Mile most of the time (which is great), I'll never come back nor would recommend it.

The position is good as we were closely located to Times Square. The room are small. We had the air conditioning leacking for 3 days. Nobody bothered to sort it out. The manager did not do anything about. They promised to send a voucher for a free night which two days later I have not received yet... we shall see

The lobby is very deceiving.This is possibly the worst hotel we've ever stayed in. We were in the north tower....the room was disgusting! The carpet was filthy, the baseboards were full of peeling paint and dented wood.The furniture was chipped and scratched.The lighting was nonexistent. We had to leave the bathroom and closet lights on to work at the desk.There should have been a lamp there.Beds were extremely uncomfortable and pillows "lumpy".... Luckily, we were there only for 1 night. The problem is...management doesn't seem to care as there are no responses to any reviews on Trip Advisor.

Good 3* hotel in Convenient location near to PAHO and GWU. CVS Pharmacy next door with adequate supplies for breakfast. Staff pleasant and rooms clean. Room rate good .We paid double the amount in NYC last Fall for similar accomodation.Bathroom Small by todays standards but not impossible.We would stay at this hotel again.

Room was not clean, base boards missing, Three pillows flat and hard. staff not friendly or helpful (really seemed not to care if we were there or not. Even at the $50.00 price tag....... it was way over priced. I would not stay there again even if it were free.

The hotel was more like a rundown super 8. The beds are select comfort which is fine if you know your number. We both have stiff backs today. bed frames a dangerous 3-8' protruding metal bars on one side. Wife ran into them twice. My wife`s bath leaked into the lobby. No problem for them. Restaurant food OK. Drinks $8.50 for a short shot of booze.

I found this hotel to be very clean and neat for the unexpectedly low price of about $55 per night. The staff were helpful and accomodating. I though the big sign in the breakfast area "MUST EAT HERE IN THE LOBBY" a bit strange. I grabbed my coffee and took it back to my room. The seating area for breakfast is literally right in the lobby. Not exactly comfortable, I skipped the food.

Comfortable, great location, good service, extremely expensive food and room service! Located at walking distance to Yerba Buena Park, Yerba Buena Center for the Arts, Museum of Modern Art, good restaurants, Moscone Convention Center (same block). Water pressure is poor, both in shower and basin. Most staff at Front Desk and Concierge Desk are cordial.

My girl friends and I booked a room for the weekend to celebrate a birthday. We had a great time. The hotel was close to everything we wanted to see. The beds were really comfortable and the room was very clean. Thanks Hampton Inn for the wonderful experience. Looking forward to coming back.

This hotel was chosen by the non-profit for visiting Board members, so I assume the price was as good as was available in the area. The lobby and room were standard big-city but clean and not crowded. The bed was really comfortable. The toiletries were marginal. Still, I've no complaints and would happy return.

Really disappointed in my 1 night here. Although the bar and dining areas were really good with a great buzzy atmosphere, the rooms were very small and looked like they needed a refurb! At $480 a night plus tax, won't be rushing back! Plus side is great location for shops/restaurants etc

There is nothing royal in this hotel! The staff was very friendly, but when we made complaints about our room, they could not do anything, just gave us a paper to fill in which they could then forward to the owner. The room was very small, not very clean and we had no refridgerator. Our wardrobe's door was broken. The bed was quite uncomfortable. Gladly the location was perfect for us, short distance to Union Square and all the nice bars in the North Beach area.

The location is good if you plan to attend any convention... The lobby looks good, the rooms not that good... Room service when there is a convention is always overworked and mistakes are common... I'm still waiting for them to replace the wrong delivery of my breakfast... Average everything; no convention; don't stay there...

Nothing special. Rooms had a chincy coffee maker which only made one cup, no fridge, and the sheets seemed to be very worn. Lots of fresh fruit for breakfast as well as the usual other breads. The airconditioning unit was very noisy and woke me each time it turned on. Ok for a short stay.

The first thing to know is that the entrance is completely anonymous and on 57th street. You go up a bare escalator to a very lavish reception area where the staff are delightful, very friendly and helpful. Sadly that is the only good thing about this vastly overpriced hotel as the corridors resemble a prison and the rooms are the smallest, noisiest and most uncomfortable I have ever encountered

The pretense that the World Center is one hotel, and that the Club Quarters is another ends once you elevate above the first floor.. Then the partition opens and you are in one hotel. The rooms are clean, but small. Free water bottles are available for pure water. Maid service is spotty- we found a used-syringe under one bed. And when the elevators are not all working, it is a real problem both with waits and then crowds. Front staff seemed friendly.

We used our points for a night stay so we could check out Beale Street. The hotel was less than a 5 minute walk to Beale Street. The room was great - the bed comfy. The bathroom was small but it was doable. We did hear some noise from the street but hay it was a Saturday night and everyone was having a great time.

This hotel is a bit shabby and outdated but you could not get a better location for the price and the staff are all lovely. They are currently undergoing refurbishment and I'm sure that means the prices will go up. The wine bar on the 2nd floor was very well appointed and offered good value for money on all house drinks at 50% during happy hours. The breakfast offered could be a little more interesting but it was quick and efficient to start your day. 2 computers available all day for free internet access and wifi throughout.

Buy a tent, sleep on the street.Do not spend a penny with them.No bar, no restaurant, taxi fare will cost you thirty five dollars to go eat a hamburger , no hot water in the shower, no one cares, they tell you , you should expect this, you're on the eight floor, and for all this this they charge you over $200. per night plus taxes.Then when you fill in the form , they apologise to the people , unsuspecting though they are, that are trying to check in, they tell them. YOU are holding things up.

Front desk reception was great and they gave me a nice upgraded room as I am Platinum level priority rewards. A nice property and they have happy hour with beer just shutting down as i arrived. Breakfast bar well attended to, with the average............. Generally a verry pleasant and good experience.

My husband and I went to cool off from the Arizona summer and much to our surprise it was 105 degrees the whole time we were there in Denver. The hotel was very nice and the staff was very well trained. Our room was spotless and very comfortable. They also served fresh coffee iin the hall which was delicious. We had planned on doing a lot of walking but it was so hot they offered a town car to take us to our destination. Great job! We will be back.

Arrived after 3 year's absence. Lobby and fireplace sitting area was new. Stayed on the 32nd floor in a Club room. Now room is modern and comfortable. TV comes with Internet capabilities, cool. Some amenities missing like slippers, bed was too soft and wouldn't work for someone with a bad back. Concierge is tried and true for many years. They give good info

This is by far the worst so called designer hotel in L.A - worst location of all, you would just never stay downtown, you're only here because your work has put you up here. You can hear the traffic, I even heard the person above me going to toilet. Cheap looking interior in the room, like Ikea. The service is terrible, the parking a ripoff and the internet is the slowest I've been on. Absolute ABOMINATION is how I would describe it.

The hotel is in a great neighborhood; perfect for a stay in Washington DC. You can do some sighseeing during the day and in the evening come back to this neigborhood for bars, dining and to sleep. The hotel is average. I liked the fact that you can cook your own dinner in the room. I am not impressed by the service. We needed to change rooms (no additional costs, which is good!), because the bed was too old and bended. Be careful and check at check-in!

Upon arriving at the Hotel Contessa, we were greeted by Eddie G. and his associates before we even got out of our cab. Eddie uploaded our luggage from the back and greeted us by name. This was the warmest welcome I have ever received at a hotel. Almost every time we left or returned to the building, staff members were waiting to open the doors and greet us. The hotel is beautiful and the beds extremely comfortable. We highly recommend the Hotel Contessa.

We went to a special VacGough package offered by this hotel. When we got there we were informed they were doing a remodel from the top down. There was extreme noise starting at nine a.m. Including Saturday. There should be a discount during this time. The elevators require card key access to the floors but the light in the elevator is poor and people struggled. The restaurant is good and the staff for the most part was very good. There is a Starbucks just out of the front door.

I was very pleased by decision to stay here. I had read all the positive reviews and they are spot-on. The room was impeccably clean and comfortable. I've spent twice as much or more staying at "luxury" hotels and not been as impressed as I was by this place. They offer a nice continental breakfast which was a pleasant surprise, enough to get you going on your way for the day. I'll definitely stay here again next time I'm in Phoenix.

It was pretty good, but not great. The valet team was great, though a little pricey, I think. The breakfast was free, but not very hot and not always fresh. The room was clean, but didn't always keep things stocked up (tissues, soap, etc.). It wasn't bad, but I expected a little more.

Another superb 5 day break in New York, we stayed at the Comfort Inn again, we definitely still recommend this hotel, superb quality, excellent size room, very clean, really good bathroom facilities, just all round value for money. The staff and management provide excellent customer service. Breakfast is good and sufficient for a start to the day. There is nothing at all negative about the hotel and staff. We will definitely be back soon.

AKA has created an apartment feel to the hotel industry which makes it a unique experience. The apartments themselves are very luxurious and close to the White House. However, there are several problems: 1. They do not have a restaurant which makes it inconvenient if you are traveling for business. 2. Some of the reception staff (especially the Asian woman) were very rude and ill mannered. 3. It is not really cheap and they barely provide any facilities that you take for granted in most hotels! Good but not great.

I am a wyndham time share owner and generally find wydham hotels pretty decent. This one however is a real disappointment. Currently under remodel, i can be understanding - try, but however the parts which are done were done with poor care or poor execution. I get the economy is hurting, however a good crew for modeling a room or restaurant cant be that hard to find.

This is my second time to come back in two years!!. The rooms were very clean and felt like new. We stayed for the long weekend. Besides being 5 minutes from Fiesta Texas, it took us 10 minutes to Sea World. Plenty of great restaurants nearby including at La Cantera. With three kids under 4, having the suite and kitchen made all the difference. The staff was friendly and always willing to help. Having the extra room is a must for families!!

Exactly what you would expect from a Best Western in the rooms, basic and predictible. However the breakfast was below average, with minimal choices and I made the mistake of accepting a room facing the busy street -- windows were not well insulated for noise or comfort. Great location close to Santa Clara and the airport.

Good location (can be bad for some because it's close to some nude clubs), good price. Internet is not free and it was horrible for me because I needed internet. My room was a bit noisy because was too close to laundry area and the shower pressure was weak. Room was pretty clean and the service was good. Friendly staff.

Good location, easy to get to, still not worth it. For $200 a night I'd at least like to be able to walk on both side of the bed and actually fall asleep instead of listening to various people shuffle in at odd hours and bollywood music blaring at 2 am. Whoever designed the rooms had a sense of humor, because while they may have contained all of the amenities (minus a closet), there wasn't space to actually use them. It practically felt like living in a dorm.

Let me start by saying, I travel a lot! A whole lot, for work as well as pleasure. As such I stay in a lot of hotels. I have NEVER, EVER stayed in a hotel this nice. That includes Trump Towers in Vegas and New York! This place blows the doors off of both, for one reason the staff! The service, the staff the "gentlemanly" approach was unreal. You owe it to yourself to experience this place. We have decided to return at least once a year. Wow! Wow! Wow!!

The view of the harbour is spectacular. Rooms are getting a little dated, but very clean and comfortable. Price, not bad as Seattle goes, however, the $36.00 for required valet parking hurt. Restaurant service needs to be spiffed up, but food OK, except the Ruben sandwich, unless you have a strong stomach for grease, stay away from it. Would I stay there again - yea, as it is clean the staff are VERY FRIENDLY, and what is not to like about the location.

Rooms are a bit smaller than regular Hilton, but nice. I stayed at the 8th floor that has a nice courtyard (pretty weird having a little park outside your window) Front desk person wasn't too helpful, but in general stay was ok. Breakfast is very good and the location is excellent: just a short walk to Inner Harbor and to the great restaurants in the area. Hotel was pretty crowded, as it was graduation week at Hopkins and the start of Memorial Day Weekend.

The staff is friendly when you check in and the hotel is clean. We were disappointed in the room...the ammennities were used ...empty lotion, shampoo, conditioner...someone just put the lids back on them. The rooms are a little old and outdated for a Marriott property. The location is great if you are catching a cab to the buckeye game.

Kimpton has struck a great balance between cool and comfortable in its brand. The service is thoughtful and efficient, and the amenities are at once chic and practical. Hotel Vintage Park may be my favorite Kimpton so far. The staff is outstanding. The location makes walking to all of Seattle's many attractions irresistible. We stayed in two different rooms after the bed in room #1 proved to be a bit cushier than I found comfortable. The desk staff could not have been more accommodating. The second room was lovely -- ask for 1007.

Functional, business-like hotel. Great views from the bedroom and wonderfully comfortable beds. Best part of the hotel is its fabulous location. Close to a whole host of things such as the the harbour and all its restaurants, bars and shops, or heading away from the sea to the Orioles baseball and Ravens football stadiums. Also easy access to the airport via the very cheap Light Rail.

This place charges $12 per day for internet in your room. Criminal these days, when even the cheapest motels give internet for free. It's not near anything convenient, the Starbucks inside closes very early, and the restaurants in the hotel are overpriced. The minifridge has motion sensors in it, so do not touch anything even to see what it is. One little bump and you're down $10.

Not my favorite Four Seasons, but still a nice hotel in Seattle. Good location, pretty nice rooms and decent food. The service at Four Seasons Seattle is not up to the standard set by most Four Seasons hotels, but it wasn't terrible. The decor is pretty sterile and the hallways have an office building feel. Definitely more of a business hotel. The lobby bar is really nice, with good food, drinks and a great view.

This is a nice Westin -- pleasant staff, clean room, dramatic lobby in a great location. Check-in was fast. But somebody has to explain to me why a hotel that fetches $250 a night still charges $12 for internet. Folks, it's 2012: the days of charging for internet access are over. It's a costly throwback that soured me on the place.

I had a pleasant stay at the Sheraton. Its location is convenient to UT. The hotel is well run and the employees were pleasant. The beds were comfortable but the sheets were a little scratchy. The next time I stay in Austin I will most likely go back to the Sheraton.

we have stayed here numerous times over the past 5 years. suggest getting a suite for a little more space and a room with mountain views. check in is always a pleasure. decent buffet breakfast with an excellent staff. minimal exercise room but ok if not crowded. i stayed here recently even though we had reservations at the jw marriott in cherry creek- 1/3 the price and i got the same nice sleep.

The rooms are huge, and we didn't expect this. Our stay was comfortable and the rooms where quiet and clean. It was great for work and getting together after work. We were close enough to downtown and 6th street that we didn't really take much taxis. The service was good. It was a little pricey for the value, but an excellent stay none the less.

I've stayed at many hotels while in San Francisco and decided to give the Parc 55 a try after a friends recommendation... and I'm glad I did! The location was central, check-in was quick and friendly, and I actually found my room quite quiet, being so close to Market and Powell Streets! The property and room was extremely clean, and I was fortunate to be in corner room which has a spacious bathroom. I will definitely consider the Parc 55 on my next visit to San Francisco. Kelly

With the size of the room, and the condition/service of the room, the price ratio of this hotel is poor than a 2 start hotel outside the city. In room# 26, the air conditon works like a heater, blow hot air instaed of cold air, but can not open the window to let cool air in because big blower is installed outside the window, and makes big noise. No coffee maker inside the room, 175 sq feet will cost you nearly US$550/night incl.tax.

This was a long weekend trip for something to keep the kids entertained. Your going for the waterpark not for the hotel accomedations that were average at best. Hotel entry was neat and rooms were about like average motel 8 or Quality Inn (cheap). Waterpark was good, several slides and "activity" areas and pools. The chlorine level is intoxicating but better that than worrying about growth of things. We were only there in evening 2 days spent the days exploring the vast museum choices of Indianapolis (childrens museum, Zoo,Art Museum,etc)

We valeted our car at the 59th street entrance. The staff left our car on the street for 30 minutes before taking it to the garage. (Based on their own records.) Our car was returned to us the next day with a crushed rear bumper. They hotel has refused to take responsibility. We expect far more from a reputable hotel. Because of the Helmsley our wonderful weekend in NYC was ruined. I would not recommend this hotel and warn all guests to never valet their car.

Believe the other negative reviews you have read. This "hotel" is beyond nasty and does not deserve its star rating. My room was crawling with large cockroaches and when I notified the front desk, the front desk assistant said "I'm actually not surprised." I demanded a refund and was given the runaround. No apology was offered. No offer was made to move me to another room. I checked out immediately and will never stay here again. Avoid this place at all costs!

We stayed here before our trip to London. The airport shuttle is fantastic and the staff were all very friendly. Our room was clean, spacious, and very modern. We were able to walk to a restaurant for dinner and another for breakfast but there are not many restaurants in the area. We would stay here again if we are traveling through and need to be near the airport. There is a train near the hotel we were told but it would take 45 minutes one way to downtown. Would prefer to have free wifi in the rooms.

This Hilton is nothing special. I was surprised by how lightless the whole place was (no windows in the lobby! and a sad view over a roof from my room). Also, nothing special for Hilton Honors members. The gym was small, but modern and not too packed with people. But its location was super close to the Convention Center.

For the price, this hotel is fine. But it was in need of some work, including fresh paint, new carpet, and improved general upkeep. The floor in my room had burns, the coffee table was sticky with years of residue, and the furniture was rather dirty looking. I wasn't necessarily uncomfortable, but it wasn't exactly welcoming either.

I stayed at this hotel visiting family and friends for my birthday 03-26-12 and stayed for 3 nights. The employees were very nice and helpful. The decor is classy and unique and the room I had was big with a view of the riverwalk. The bed, linens and towels were comfortable and the room looked, smelled, and FELT clean. The location makes you feel safe and you almost forget you're in Detroit.

This hotel was fine. The rooms were clean, staff was ok, and the beds were average. The cons were that you have to pay for parking and the water pressure wasn't great in the shower. I just can't imagine staying here again when I can stay at the Doubletree close by and not pay for parking. If I was staying here for a conference, I would likely have been happy with the amenities. Looks like a great place for a conference! But, still, you'd have to pay for parking.

Hilton hotels have become a disappointment. From securing reservations to technology problems to pathetic on site service this chain needs a employee makeover. If I ran my business like Hilton I suspect customers would regularly look elsewhere for accommodations. San Jose Hilton is particularly problematic and my experience on the last 2 stays go way beyond minor annoyances to major inconveniences. Room service at 3 in the afternoon cannot even be bothered to answer their phone much less return messages left on their answering machine. Stay elsewhere in San Jose!

Sorry, never again for me - experienced travelers has no need for worn out hotel. There are too many nice, clean hotels. Double trees are usually very nice. Am diamond member. So I travel a lot. I didn't check age of hotel since Double Tree is usually very nice. I am guessing you could check the age of this hotel and that'd answer your questions. Employees very nice. If your rate is very sweet it may not upset you greatly.

We booked a family suite to sleep 5 adults our booking sheet indicated that we had 2 beds and pull out sofa What we got was 2 single beds and 2 sofa beds The 2 sofa beds were very ordinary also the hotel was old and dated and so was the linen Disappointed Aussie

Overall I had a good experience at the hotel. The thing that was the most frustrating was the elevators. It is neat to see the historical elevators there but not efficient enough (or large enough) for a hotel in this day in age. Would have liked to known about that before I got there.

I have stayed here many times and I miss all the people. It is very nice, accommodating, and the people are fabulous!. George is wonderful and all the people who work there. I haven't been there recently however, if I was going to Denver, I can't think of another place to stay (and I have stayed at many)....

A well decorated motel -cute, but with still the same structure and paper thin walls. Very pricey for what it is. No welcome greeting by the guy checking us in, his colleague eventually offered us the cookies that we're out for guests. We booked 2 rooms paying on the same credit card but had to go through the check in process twice despite providing all the details when checking in online. Had room on 3rd floor -loud traffic noise, a lot less on the ground floor.

Stayed for four nights and were very pleased with the hotel,the location is perfect 2 minutes and you are in Times Square.I shared with a friend and we had a Junior Suite which was ideal as we had seperate rooms.The hotel could do with updating but it was clean and the staff helpful.

First off, some of the best service from the staff of a hotel I have ever had. Great people, especially Armondo are on premises. Location is great, hotel is well maintained. Problem for me is the size of the room, small, very small, so the value isn't there for me. If you never have to do work and just gogogo then this is perfect for you. I recommend with that caveat emptor.

The hotel had all of the ambiance of the International Space Station. I have seen better decor on an aircraft carrier. When I arrived, I was advised by a desk clerk that check in time was 3:00 p.m. and they had guests that had been in the lobby waiting since 10:00 a.m. (this was just before 1 p.m) I never got a wake up call and found a roach in the room. Not a place I would recommend.

Basic but perfectly adequate airport hotel, Stayed one night between flights. Main difficulty was finding the phones at LAX to call for the free shuttle but that needs to be addressed by the airport. Room comfortable with bath. Breakfast was cereals, juice, toast, fruit, cakes to suit most needs. We didn't experience the noise others have reported.

Rooms are nice, maybe a tad smaller than normal but nice. I had room 1524, which had a nice view of the city. They have Wifi but it cost extra,not fair, concidering the price I paid for the room . Parking is $55 per night. Don't worry if you forgot something, there is stores in the area that has a tons of stuff. Excellent, professional staff at front desk. Although we only spent one night at this hotel, I would not hesitate to stay here again,location was great.

I did my researched and found Park Central at 3 nights $1049.00. Checking in.. OMG!! the rooms are old and need serious upgrades. Had a problem with the first room. So they moved us to a room across the hall from the maids service closet. Between the earlier morning noise and other stuff. I must say it was a terrible stay…Thinking back, it was a waste of my vacation I will never get back. I think motel 6 would have been better. Seriously….Consider staying somewhere else.

This hotel is similar to Grand Central Station. Nice and clean, but very busy. Accommodations are typical for NYC, VERY SMALL and CROWDED rooms. It's difficult for a family of four to spend more than a few minutes in a Traditional 2 Double room. Aside from this, the hotel is in a great location. The gym is exceptional. And the staff is friendly.

Stayed for 2 nights. Wish I stayed a month! The hotel is amazing! Great price, free parking, cool staff. Chambers is right there to warm up for nightlife and a last drink when coming back. Loved the pool and chill area. As mentioned on others posts, don't let the neighborhood influence you to give up staying there. It is an oasis. It is truly a cool and nice hotel. The rooms are very comfortable and clean. If I ever go back to San Frascisco, I`m staying at the Phoenix for sure!

The room was pretty worn, and the screen was broken on my window, so I couldn't leave the window open for fresh air. The bathroom was clean though, and even though I requested a room that hadn't had pets in it, I still woke up wheezing, so I'm sure many dogs had stayed in that room. They allow dogs but don't advertise it,which is bad. Won't stay here again. It was inexpensive for a reason.

I was assured at the front desk that I had a great room. It was near the elevator and noisy. The room did not have any appeal and was spartan in furnishing. It was clean but not warm. In fact the heating system did not work properly and the internet service was sporadic at best.

Really well located from each SD main attractions (downtown, Petco Park, Balboa Park and Zoo), almost a walking distance (as a matter of fact, if your are in good shape, you could do it..!!). Personal very friendly, rooms were very clean and spacious, beds comfortable and breakfast was OK. Only thing that should improve is parking, because they charge you 15$ per night to park there...(extra from room rate)

This is a beautiful hotel in a very central location to several areas of Boston. The staff are friendly, the rooms well appointed and the adjacent eateries are excellent. I have stayed here several times while on business and always look forward to return visits. I highly recommended this hotel!

I usually stay near Times Square on my visits to NYC, but this time, I found an unbeatable rate for the MLK weekend for $143.00/night! Now that's a fantastic rate for a King bed, microwave, refrigerator, and fast elevators (for the most part). The best part of the hotel is the free coffee and tea in the a.m., and the 25 steps or so to the N,Q, R line that was essential in getting to Union Square, Times Square and, especially, to SOHO! Great value, clean room, adequate size. Won't go back to Midtown again!

Stayed here when attending #SXSW and was worried about the distance but it was OK with a hired car. However when SXSW did kick-off the taxis were too busy to come out to this hotel so be careful on busy days. The best thing about this hotel is on this particular day when we couldnt get a taxi, the receptionist/sales lady actually DROVE US into downtown free of charge! Apart from that, the rooms were OK - bed was pretty stiff. Breakfast was ok. All very basic but clean.

Just returned from a week in NYC staying at the New Yorker. The hotel is perfectly situated for visiting all the top tourist attactions, many are within walking distance. We travelled from Newark Airport to the hotel in just 45mins! The hotel is opposite Penn Station. The only criticism of the hotel is the size of the room, ours was very small as as the bathroom but as we were hardly in the room other than to sleep it was OK.

This room was something out of the 1940's. Bathroom completely outdated. But the bed is my worst complaint. Didn't get any sleep due to the bed being too hard to sleep on . Cheap 2 " mattress thrown on a board was pretty much it. Next time I'll book the Travelodge around the corner, can't be much worse !! Run away from this place !!!

Reading the reviews and looking at the photo's from this Motel as well as Google maps location of this place,there are Railroad tracks behind it! It is time for New Management as well as responsible Employee's who care about there work! From reading these reviews there are no excuses for what customers have to deal with here! I have stayed in many hotels and motels all over the United States and never have I seen as many problems as this place. It looks like it's time for a change here!

The reception and lobby are dated, the beds were comfy but the bathroom was so damp and dirty that I wore my flip flops while in there. The bathroom walls were damp and had rust and mould stains, the carpet smelt damp and this ruined a hotel with nice and helpful staff. I got the impression this would be more suitabel for people travelling for work, I would not advise tourists to stay here. I wouldnt recommend this hotel to anyone, which is shame if not all bathrooms were this bad.
