I was really impressed by the clean and updated rooms and grounds---Our stay was great with no problems---The staff was very nice and helpful----The breakfast was nice-----The rooms were huge and very modern -----You couldn't ask for a better deal-----The price was very fair---I'll stay there again the next time we're in Memphis, and I'ld highly recommend this site---

We stayed one night at the Royal Palms before returning to the UK at the end of our holiday and without doubt, this was the best hotel we had stayed in during our time in the US. We couldn't fault the accommodation or the service. All the staff were friendly and committed to making guests feel as welcome as possible and Mona the concierge, couldn't have been more helpful. Breakfast was excellent and my husband (who's Coeliac) was very pleasantly surprised to be offered gluten-free toast. The only time this had happened during our trip!

This hotel is a great business hotel. Easy access to plenty of companies. Safe, clean, and a great nights sleep (I've stayed lots of times and never been disturbed by noise from other rooms or outside). There is direct access to the Galleria, a huge shopping mall. The beds are fantastic. Staff friendly. Rooms clean. Gym reasonably well equipped.

The last few times I have stayed at this location I have had to walk pass multiple people at the front entrance smoking. I am a double lung transplant. Is it possible your ash trays can be moved from the front entrance? Is it possible there could be signs no smoking at entrance?

Yes, the hotel has a little visable wear and tear - but for me, cleanliness is more important. And I found my Tower level queen room to be very clean. The service wasn't bad, but wasn't memorable either. Kind of like the whole hotel, really... Best to ask for an upgrade here - and push for the Tower level. Free breakfast and evening snacks. Minus one star for the wireless Wi-Fi charge. The hotel is so large, it should really abolish this antiquated policy - or at least lower it to the standard $9.99/day instead of $12.50.

Stayed here 2 years ago and was happy with the service. I went back to the Bay area last week and found out that this particular Holiday Inn is located just across from Tenderloin District. Tenderloin District is okay during the day but is suggested to stay away after dark. Please be warn that this hotel is located in bad part of town.

The St. Giles should be called the St. Gauge. The miracle is that they can charge what they charge for such an average hotel. After Sandy they tripled their prices. Service was bad. The door to my room didn't even cover the whole entranceway. Decore is cheesy and worn. There is a lot of choice in NY - no reason to stay here.

We stayed one night here and found it to be very basic, more of a budget hostel then a hotel but without the budget price tag.Not a very good area either.( We moved on to the Parc 55 by Wyndham instead better rate and accommodation .) The hotel was clean enough, no bed bugs but very old building, really needs updating. The photos on the website are misleading. I would not stay here again.

This hotel is full of mold and truly run down. The staff may be friendly but i got very ill upon entering my matchbox room. I had to leave the hotel because of a reaction to the mold. No gym very old fashion and no food/restaurant on site. So many other great places to stay in PA. This is not one of them.

This is NOT the place to stay if you're looking for a good night's sleep in Memphis. The hotel is located directly on top of Beale Street and directly across the street from a public park where musicians play into the wee hours. They actually give you complimentary ear plugs at check in - not a good sign. Nice new hotel, nice breakfast, but we were up half the night due to the thump, thump, thump of the music.

It is really a great location but that's about it. We traveled with 3 young boys so proximity to Times Square and Central Park was a big plus. Lobby is decent, staff nice but the rooms are more like a cheap motel. Room size was on small size and carpet, bathroom and furniture all looked sad and worn out. Beds were reasonably comfortable. It wasn't a bad experience but, when in New York again, I would find alternative lodging for the money.

If you are traveling with kids and want to be close to shopping on the Mag Mile, this is a fine place to stay. Nothing about the service wowed me, but it was comfortable and clean. I would recommend this hotel if you're doing the American Girl experience, but otherwise I prefer to stay further away from the Michigan Ave. crowds.

Great customer service, however parking is pricey ($26/night). The food is also excellent. I worked late hours and the food was served late or early in the morning. Customer service is wonderful. They have wash & fold laundry service all weekend, dry cleaning Mon-Sat. PROS Great service Great food Cool bar with balcony Close to restaurants and nightlife House keeping leaves robe and slippers every night CONS Internet is not free Parking is $26/night

The Hotel Beacon was the perfect place for four women from Minnesota to explore New York City. We were so tired from exploring, seeing the US Open, and sightseeing that most evenings we bought wine at the shop next door and food from the great stores across the street and spent the evening in our living room area. Beautiful view of sunset from our window ... see photo. The desk staff was so helpful and very friendly, and the hotel was immaculate. We'll be back!

The Grand Hyatt NYC is a good looking hotel but my room was burglarized. PLEASE hide your property and double check your doors because some are defective. This place is scary so be extra careful as it is connected to Grand Central Station. Latch your doors and check your closets. The security will be of no use and they will try to persuade you to not call the police. Don't listen , call the police. I heard that another room was burglarized after mine and they did not even help to refund my property. Be safe!

My company has booked me into this hotel several times recently and it is not my favorite. It is well priced and thus full of European tourists. The rooms are tiny but not uncomfortable. The elevators can be slow. The thing that irks me most is that they will not serve coffee for one via room service and instead force you to buy a large pot of coffee for $19!!! I find this exploitative. The room service menu is probably the most limited I have ever seen. Very few options and not very good ones.

good hotel, great location, 10 minutes to bryant park or times square. rooms a bit old but clean. Rooms at the back had terrible views of a building site/kitchen roof. Roof terrace fabulous views etc but bar lacks atmosphere. Main complaint is that the air conditioning is old and very noisy, it was like sleeping in a wind tunnel.

This hotel came out of the gate far above its competition. But after a short time it has slide down to average. The service is still very friendly and helpful, but overall hotel management seems to have let down. The rooms are very large and unique. The slipping is occurring in the upkeep and the staffing levels. Both the nightly reception and morning breakfast have fell far below average. Don't expect Embassy Suites level of these services. Overall, still a nice hotel, they just have lost there edge for now.

Not fantastic but okay... It was noisy outside and inside; the air conditioner blasts like some sort of engine and the road-work outside was frustrating at times. The staff were pleasant but didn't seem to have an idea about any of the surroundings. This one is petty but I am gold status and they seem to struggle with by not quite understanding what that usually means...

This is where to stay for a first class trip to see the Red Sox. Great staff and excellent service. This place is top notch all the way. Pricey rooms and room service but worth every dollar. We got a "Fenway room" which had a view looking out onto Fenway Park which is one block away. The subway entrance is next to the hotel for easy access to see the sites. Only drawback is no coffee in room so you hafta wait on room service.

This is place is masquerading as a luxury hotel. It has a large lobby with large murals, shiny surfaces, marble bathrooms, etc. Yet, nothing is really well made or well designed. In our room (granted very large), the remotes needed batteries, the upholstery on the sofa was some kind of plasticized fabric that made noise whenever you shifted your weight, the floor tiles and counters in the bathroom were Cracked and had multiple repairs. The breakfast was an absolute joke. There were four boxes of cereal and some cellophane wrapped muffins.

This hotel is very average hotel however the restaurant, Pier 7 was an outstanding dinner choice for us. We had seafood Newburg and shrimp cocktail which was wonderful and reasonably priced. The free Internet at this property was nonexistent so dont plan on using it. Otherwise an average property with a little bit of a walk to the Metro (DC's subway).

This is our 3 stay at this location in 4 years . We come to Jacksonville for a yearly family get together. Each year there are little things that make the stay not perfect however not grossly unpleasant. The rooms are dated the ceiling fan squeaked in the bedroom and the sliding closet door wasn't fully on the track on one side. The room was clean and comfortable . The personal quite friendly.

I stay at the Crown Plaza River Oaks frequently and I am always greeted by friendly and professional staff. Mandy and other staff members always remember my name, even after a few weeks of not having been there. I enjoy the warm atmosphere and how everyone there make one feel like family or an old friend. I also like the location which is extremely practical and convenient. While the Hotel restaurant and bar serve excellent food and drinks, there are lots of great options in the vicinity. I will stay there on future trips.

It was our first stay here at the Hilton Times Sq, and we can safely say it won't be our last. The location is excellent, amenities top notch, and the rooms very clean and well equipped. The service is excellent, with special mention to Richard at the front desk. He was very friendly, accommodating and helpful - a trait that is shared with staff throughout the hotel. Many thanks!

This is thee closest hotel to LAX, I even saw people walking from the airport to the hotel entrance with their bags. It sits parallel to one of the runways so if you like to watch the planes land and take off, request a room like I did. The rooms are spacious but, they definitely need a refurbishment. Check in was a breeze and there are many amenities to take advantage of...the free wi-fi is great.

Stayed in a Ultra Suite for one evening during the week. The property was beautiful with gorgeous decor, a fun bar, and an extremely helpful concierge. However, I did not get a good night's sleep as the mattresses are extremely soft and offer very little back support. If you like a firm mattress this is NOT your hotel.

This place was weak sauce. Tiny lobby, older property, inept bellhops, and upcharges for double beds on arrival despite reassurances to the otherwise when I called. I was not pleased at all with my stay. To boot the outside still had the putrid stench of sewage post-Hurricane Sandy. There are better options to stay downtown. I rather liked the neighbouring Marriott. The W is also an option nearby, if you are in your 20s, don't mind loud music, or are hard of hearing and consequently unable to hear it.

We stayed 5 nights at Jolly Madison - more about it here http://iain.bz/nyc1 "There is nothing jolly about Jolly Madison Towers hotel just off Madison Avenue – the rooms are tired (like 70′s porno meets grandmas house), even the bellhop suggested that we go out for breakfast rather than the hotel restaurant. BUT for us it was just fine as it meant we spent more time out in the city."

Unfortunately not worth the price. Beds are comfortable, location good, reservation personnel is polite and helpful, there is a fridge in the room. Take notice that there is no elevator. Tv, room and bathroom is worn out. There were small ants around the coffee machine. There wasn't too much noise from the road.

the hotel seems to care more about their business on their rooftop bar than the hotel customers. I was on the 10th floor, and essentially under the DJ on the roof. They were very accomodating when I asked to change to a new room, but was asked "didn't the tell you when you checked it??" Really?? Even in the new room, it is difficult to get to the elevators to your room because there is a significant focus on the crowd going to the roof bar. Stay here if you want to party, but not if you are on business.

This was one of the worst hotels I have ever stayed in! The rooms are way too small, no coffee machine in the rooms, beds were creaky and uncomfortable, no hot water or heat on one of the days. Staff were unfriendly and unhelpful. The only good thing was the location but you can do so much better in NYC.

We stayed there only for 1 night and stayed in one of the renovated rooms, it was very nice room and comfortable bed! I think his name is Marke who works the front desk was very nice, we needed extra towels and he brought it up to our room which was nice of him to do that! Would stay there again! Breakfast was good also.

I was trying to save a buck of my perdiam and stayed at the cheapest place I could find. What a mistake. The wall paper was peeling off the walls, the bathroom was mildew covered. The bed probably had not been replaced since the 1970's, and the entire hotel had a musty smell to it. It says they have a bar... The bar was closed, an employ told me because the owner hadn't paid his state liquor taxes. Just avoid this hotel pay the extra $20 and stay someplace nice. Its really not worth it.

Our room was fine; comfortable, nice bed, great location, except....the bathroom smelled like vomit! We complained, so they came in to do an extra clean and brought in an air ionizer, but it did not help. We thought about trying to change rooms (which we probably should have) but just toughed it out because we didn't want to move again. Otherwise, we liked Hotel Nikko.

Very disappointed in this stunning looking hotel. It looks so wonderful inside - but the staff were pretty unhelpful, very snooty, and they all looked very unhappy (which is always a great clue about well/badly a place is run). Just a generally glum vibe and poor service throughout (I think this is the only hotel I stayed in on my tour of the Eastern USA who HASN'T sent me a customer satisfaction survey...says it all too doesn't it?

I wasn't overly impressed with the hotel. The staff seemed to just be there for the check and the room wasn't all that clean. The internet was hit and miss and while trying to take a shower, it took a few minutes to get hot water. For the price, the stay could have been better.

Stayed here before and it was OK. Not a fleabag, but it's at least functional. Not a vacation or romantic venue. My last experience was very negative; note that I did not say "a stay" since my flight was delayed so I got in at 2AM. I had booked the room weeks before on their website, but they could not find my reservation...and they were full. I was fortunate to find a room available at the Hyatt a block away at 3AM, where we will staying for our future needs in this area.

Pretty basic, surprised they didn't have sealing fans as the room got muggy and hot. The air con was broken, but the location made up for everything!! This is a good place to have somewhere to crash and get ready the next day. Location: Its 100m from the subway. One stop away from the Walk of Fame, Hollywood bars, nightclubs, a few stops more is Universal Studios.

I am not one to write many review, however I would love to hear other peoples experince at this hotel. I stayed therelast night and my neck is still very stiff. What is the deal with the small pillow? The lobby ofthe hotel is very nice, however, the beds are not good. A good thing about the hotel is the two complimentary waterbottles in the room. That isa very nie gesture.

This location is fabulous - easy walk to FlatIron, Times Square. It's clean, a great price, the staff is super friendly, and overall it was a great place to be. I was here for work, so I didn't spend alot of time in the hotel rooms, but when I was here, I felt very relaxed and sheltered from the bustling NYC streets. Would definitely stay again!

We enjoyed the view at night of the Ben Franklin Bridge lit up, lights reflected in the Delawaware River. Waking up to the river view was lovely! The only drawback for the hotel is that it's not "right next to" anything. You can't walk down the street and get a fresh coffee, ice cream or any of the things one might like to have when on vacation. The shuttle service was excellent, however, and the front desk staff were very helpful and professional.

We had stayed in this hotel booked through Priceline. Price was very cheap and we had low expectation. But did not expect bedbugs, But it was the customer service that really made us upset. Tammy, Vivian Xie the manager, They were rude, mean, just evil. We could not possibly stay in the room but couldnt careless. Rather they laughed at us and did everything to give us harder time, It was this hotel experience that really made us not ever want to go back to NYC

I stayed for a weekend night. Had over $2000 worth of luggage stolen from our room. We know it was someone on their staff. The front desk, manager, and security service was all VERY RUDE to us. Did not know protocol or have any solutions to help us when we came back and had our luggage stolen. The sheets had brown stains on them. The sheets were put on backwards. Our shower drained into the carpeting in the bedroom. It was an overall horrible experience. Do not stay at this hotel!!!!!!

I was welcomed immediatly by the staff and check in went very smooth and quickly. Our room was upgraded due to being a member of IHG Priority Club and a fruit backet, bottled water & chocolates were awaitng our arrival. The room had a georgeous bathroom with plenty of ammenties, oversized room and the bed was very comfortable. We had a drink in the restaurant and it was very well appointed. A perfect stay and great value.

Stayed six nights, it is actually a bargain - if you can live with the low standard. Location is perfect with two minutes walk to TImes Square. Clean linen and bath but the carpet wasn't vacumed for at least 2 weeks. Another minus was tha lack of a closet but we got a lot of hangers and with nails in the walls, we managed without it. We'll be back!

Our stay was very enjoyable. The bed was amazingly comfortable, and the decor in good taste (lots of texture, neutral tone, and rich burgandy to soothe the spirit). We were close to everything, walking distance to Pike Place Market. We did the B & B option and was we worth the value.

Wonderful staff--everybody we met. Perfect location. Unfortunately they use extremely harsh cleaning products. On check in day they had just cleaned our rooms. They reeked of chemicals. I asked housekeeping to just replace towels for the remaining 2 nights & that's what happened for night 2. That and the fact that they have sliding doors and balconies helped. Night 3 they replaced all the bedding and that had also been given the harsh chemical treatment. I struggled the entire time with asthma, rashes, red eyes, etc. I'd love to go again, but the chemicals were horrible.

The location is perfect but we booked standart double room with shared bathroom and they gave us twin room with 2 single bed which is cheaper then we pay out, told us they will pay refund and they did not!!! Unfriendly and staff. Room was very noisy and tiny even no space for luggages. Carpeting at all the hotel and room smells terrible, mostly no paper in shared bathrooms. There is only one shared batroom for each floor. It means 6 room using the same bathroom at the floor. Herbert Hotel was the worst hotel I've ever seen, never again!!!

Booked thru Hotwire.com, where they didn't reveal the name until after you booked. This is an old hotel where only one elevator worked, which sucks when you have luggage and kids. You can't walk from the lobby to the elevator up to your room. You have to walk outside and then get on an elevator. You don't have on sight parking. The neighborhood is terrible and not a good choice for a hotel on a family vacation. I WON'T BE BACK!

Our stay at the Hollywood Celebrity was an overal very good experience. You cannot beat the location. The hotel itself is showing its age but is kept surprisingly well. The rooms are basic but spacious and the walls are very thin and you can hear everything around you. I don't know if I'd stay he with my children but for adults it's fine.

Business trip. Stayed three nights. Great location on the Magnificant Mile. Concierge and front staff very helpful. Rooms were clean and had an interesting flare. Hotel very busy - Sept. Three business partners visited the attached wine and chocolate bar. Interesting concept. The service was extremely bad. Staff rude. Not what I expected from this establishment. Has great potential but fell short. Don't bother as there are so really great restaurants surrounding this hotel.

Espensive , Old Beds, RUDE CUSTOMER SERVICES and every morning when you have to take the elevator you Find out that all around smells like a Dirty Restroom!!!! and the bad part of all this you talk about this problems with the Manager he say is because you paid so little you get this services!!!!!

We had an early flight out so we decided to stay close to the airport. This was a great location. Walking distance to the terminal. Very clean. Staff was friendly. Like that there is restaraunt and bar on sight. I also like that there is computers and tablets located in the lobby for guest use. Free wifi worked great as well

Room was small, which is not surprising. I had a view of a brick wall. The service was poor. For example, the number of towels in my room went down every day. My last day all I had was one bath towel and one hand towel. My business partner was given 3 different rooms. He got tired of moving and stayed with the last one because it was the least worst room. For $500 per nite, I would look elsewhere.

We loved the contemporary beautiful Hotel. The rooms were very spacious with floor to ceiling windows for a gorgeous view of the city. The staff everywhere we went in the hotel were outstanding! It was close enough to walk to many places and right next to the cable cars, which we used often.

Lovely lobby and accommodating staff. Duck parade is fun ceremony especially for kids. The room however is a ripoff for the price--very small and the bathroom was even tinier. My knees hit the bathtub when I used the toilet! Do yourself a favor and stay at the Holiday Inn or Doubletree close by and walk over early for a drink in the lobby and to get a good seat for the 'festivities'.

Some way from the centre, and a very typical motel. The staff were freindly, and the reception area warm and comfortable. The room was large, and the wifi was OK, but it could definitely have been cleaner and had an odd musty smell. Good value, but on the whole I would rather not stay there again.

The worst. Aside from problems I can live with (the room was as long as the bed and about 2 feet wider), here are the main complaints: -Internet was barely functional. -No elevator and I was on the 5th floor. Glad I only had a backpack! -Both toilets on my floor were clogged. I didn't want to write the word "feces" in my review, but I feel like I have to. -The bathrooms smelled like mold. Thought I'd save a buck - never again!

I booked this hotel at the last minute with 3 kids age 14-8. I wasnt sure if this hotel was a mistake because it is a 4 star hotel. I was not sorry. The front desk staff was amazing. Very helpful. The kids were given cookies and milk upon arrival. They also brought robes and slippers in each kids size. Eveytime I spoke with anyone in hotel they were friendly and courteous. The hotel was nice, rooms spacious and comfortable. 2 blocks from the White House. I would stay here again!

The four nights I stayed at the JW Marriott Indianapolis were wonderful. The rooms are large, clean, and well appointed. The hotel is within walking distance to a number of attractions; if example, the Eiteljorg Museum of American Indians and Western Art and the Indiana State Museum are across the street from the hotel, and the historic state capitol building is a couple of blocks away. The food served in the hotel's restaurants is exceptionally good. But what makes this hotel outstanding is the staff; they are friendly, accommodating, professional, and they go out of their way to help you.

This hotel is very basic if that. The bed was all springs so very hard to sleep but is was quiet. I requested a wake up call at 6:00 am but never got a call and luckily since I could not sleep on the springy bed I was awake anyway. The location was good and right next to the bus to LaGuardia and the subway. I won't go back.

I stayed on business on the 18th floor where everything was very tired. My colleagues were staying on the 13th floor which had been refurbished, and it was like a different hotel. Make sure you ask for a refurbished room. Reception was understaffed - long lines even for HHonors members. Note also that they will charge you $25 per day for using the fitness center which is daylight robbery!

When I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights, I came back with welts all over my body! I had at least 100 bites. I called the hotel to notify them, and they did nothing but try to convince me that I got the bites somewhere else. Needless to say I will NEVER stay at this hotel again for as long as I live.

I stay in hotels 3 nights every week. This is the the most filthy hotel I have stayed in for years!! Bathroom and bedroom had stains on the walls. Shower had streaks down the walls and needed to be cleaned before I could use it. Coffee maker was unusable due to a missing filter. Alarm clock did not work and was not replaced by the front desk. I've stayed in roadside motels that were cleaner and better than this place. Avoid this hotel at all costs!!

Great location wihtin walking distance to White House and even to Georgetown and J F Kennedy center. Large rooms, really nice and helpful personnel. The area is within George Washington University area, and there is not much reastaurants or other amusements during the evenings. (not for those who are more after lively nigth life). Again I had troubles with the noise coming from air conditon system outside the room, and we even changed room but it did not help. (I am too sensitive to the noise, propably)

...unfortunately the groundfloor rooms are too loud to actually sleep in. For a cheep hotel room everything was accempable with the possible exception of the breakfast offerings which were extremely limited. But the easy with which engines starting and conversations transfered through the exterior walls and doors made this an experience I do not care to repeat.

The hotel itself looks nice, but the service leaves a lot to be desired, the staff is polite but dry, some even botherline passive-aggreasive, the breakfast lacks variety and can go as far as to say that they're quite stingy, the area is ok and the cleanliness was average, overall under-whelmed and would not return to this property which is a shame because I do enjoy most Embassy Suites.

We stayed for 3 nights at the Red Lion. The location of the hotel is fantastic. It is close enough to walk to Pike Place Market, the monorail (for the Space Needle, EMP, etc.) and numerous restaurants. The staff was extremely responsive to our A/C problem (it broke twice and was fine the third night). And, the rooms were clean.

The pretty pictures for this hotel don't capture the experience. Feels a bit like an old Hollywood facade where the front is good but there not much behind the scenes. Not clean and service team needs training. Beds aren't comfortable. Cheap and a decent location but that's it. Bell and front desk were clueless about local destinations, transportation and other typical hotel questions. My non-smoking room had a disgusting smoke smell. When I called the desk to ask for a different room they sent a staff person with a spray bottle of Febreeze. Not good.

one of the biggest reasons I picked this hotel was because they offer shuttle services to Sea World and the Zoo. They forget to tell you that the shuttles only run at 2 hour intervals, and you have to sign up in order to use them. The hotel room was average, a little old and run down. The sliding bathroom door wouldn't shut all the way so there was little to no privacy.

The Blakely is a small boutique hotel in mid-town Manhattan. The rates were a little better than some in NY and the rooms are clean, spacious and the service was excellent. For visiting, the location is excellent, close to Times Square on 55th St. West. I usually stay at the W but the rates here are better and I like the boutique nature of the hotel. About 6 or 7 rooms per floor. No room service but they will deliver breakfast to your room. Free breakfast is available in the hotel restaurant. I'd stay here again.

Overpriced. Windowi n bathroom open to the room, in a double bed room for goodness sakes, terrible view from room window. Furniture had taken a beating and looked so. Three phones in one room, standard size. One worked. Lobby was loud and cold, nice view in the lobby. Wasn't impressed by staff. Cost not offset amenity.

The hotel is okay, and offers some nice ameneites, but I most likely would not stay there again. I should have just stayed at my favorite place, The Embassy Suites. It is hard to offer a fair comparison if you are used to staying at high-end hotels, but overall the hotel was clean, the service was good. Be advised that the nightly rate was out of scope for the value of the room, and there are not a lot of good restaurants in the area.

First, we were given keys to a room that already had guests in it. This calls the hotel's security to question... Then, we entered a room that felt dirty and was falling to pieces. We stayed in a suite and the chair and bench had both stains and holes in it, the wallpaper was coming off and the bathroom was dirty. The only plus was the location as it is right in the middle of Broadway. However, the only way I would return is of the place underwent a huge and much-needed renovation.

Old world elegance, superior location, very friendly staff, fabulous view over the park and the Bay but... no mini bar, no tea/coffee making facilities ($20 to order a cup of tea and a coffee) and $10 per device per day for internet? Left a sour taste for a 5 star rated hotel.

The only good thing about this hotel is the location. It is very basic and has absolutely nothing special to it. At most this is a 3 star hotel. The Wifi, like most places is not free 12$ per 24 hrs and the parking 'oh my god'! 60$ per day. you can park in a publi parking oposite for 30$ per day. I would look for another hotel with more character, which I have heard San Fransisco is full of.

This Hostel was without doubt, the worst I have ever stayed in. The atmosphere was really creepy and conditions were absolutely filthy, toilets on two of the three floors didn't work, taps didn't work and the bathrooms were grimey and literally had dirt covered spiderwebs in the corner! The showers were covere

The first room that they gave me was a non smoking room and it smelled terrible!!! then I asked for an other room which had a poor internet wireless conection. The cleanliness outside is terrible, the irregular floor outside over the halls from each floor make it look insecure. Inside the room was not as clean as it should be, at the bath you could see hair at the floor and the bath tube.

The rooms were nice, but the furniture was somewhat worn and needed updating. The lobby looked like like it was built in the early 70s. On a positive note, their room service was very good, but the group rate I received was still $239.00 per night and we had a couple dozen people staying there. Not a good deal at all. I wouldn't stay here again!

Reception was friendly and cold at the same time. Elevators are slow and small , general apearence of hotel is used old and dirty. I would not advise business trbelers to use this hotel surely not if you want a restfull sleep you might be surprised by the garbage collectors who find it amusing while they are working infrint of hotel to shout and laugh very loud so the entire hotel would wake up. Note garbage collectors are infront of the hotel at 4h30 in the morning.

They have a scam working with a local towing company to have your car towed if you park in the unmarked parking lot next door. On weekends, there may not be enough parking places. The Comfort Inn next door is closed, but they have the towing company tow your car to a lot in Baltimore. The hotel is not clean, either

This place was walking distance to the SeaTac airport. After a flight from Beijing to Seattle, with a long layover following it, I walked out of the airport, past the light rail, and into this place. While it wasn't dirt cheap, it did the job I needed. The staff (Aliya? Aleeyah?) was exceptional. Someone should give them a raise -- the woman helped me get a room, answer the phone, and performed a number of other tasks while she was clearly short staffed, and she made it look easy.

One complaint: If you do have a loud neighbor, you can probably hear them. But, in general it was only loud when folks were getting up in the morning (8a). However, the room was furnished nicely, very clean, brand new furniture, the best bedding and pillows I've stayed in in a while! The lobby and restaurant bar are really trendy and fun - a fantastic breakfast at normal DC prices. If you are driving, park around the corner at "Hall of the States" on E street for less than half the price of the hotel parking lot.

This hotel was a little pricey, but totally met all of my expectations. Great location within walking distance of downtown, great service from the housekeeping to the front desk staff, great ambiance all throughout the hotel, the rooms were very nice and clean and the pool area was like a tropical getaway in the city. They even had a Starbucks in the lobby, definitely a plus! I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to the downtown San Diego area.

For the price, I was expecting much, much more. Great to be small and discreet, but quality of experience just not there. Much press on how wonderful the place is - but this is based upon the previous owner / management. No hot water in $500 suite on arrrival. No apology. Front desk eager but incompetent - booking us into a restaurant which was closed and not taking / relaying messages. Breakfast set-up comical.

My Fiancee and I stayed here for 2 nights while visiting San Francisco and I am so glad we did. It was a typical W Hotel, swanky but clean with a fun atmosphere. The location was great, walking distance from pretty much everything! I would recommend to anyone staying in the area.

Poor customer service from the management staff to accommodate for any inconvenience caused by the hotel. I certify that this review is based on my own experience and is my genuine opinion of this hotel, and that I have no personal or business relationship with this establishment, and have not been offered any incentive or payment originating from the establishment to write this review. I understand that TripAdvisor has a zero-tolerance policy on fake reviews

Generally speaking this seemed like a nice enough hotel. We arrived late and left early so we didn't get a chance to evaluate properly. But what we did experience was our bathroom door would not close unless you pushed REALLY hard...the bottom was considerably out of whack. More importantly though, the shower didn't drain. I mean REALLY didn't drain. Ankle deep water in less than ten minutes. We could hear the traffic a little more than we liked from out room as well. It is very convenient to the airport.

The pros: the Milner is in a great location and was a hundred bucks cheaper than the next option on the week I visited Boston. It's clean and safe. The cons: the decor was shabby, not chic. I was there in the heat of summer: the elevator was broken, and the AC was a crazy loud old unit that reminded me of backpackers hotels in Asia. In fact, the whole experience reminded me of a backpackers hotel in Asia. But would I stay there again? For the price, and given that it's clean and safe, absolutely.

My second time staying here now, I didn't have any issues, the rooms are still so so, it's not high end, but not bad either. The rooms have newer flat screen tvs and are spacious with desks and a sitting area. There is wifi throughout the hotel for free. The staff was super friendly, so nothing bad to say about them. The restaurant was so so, and the staff was really slow in there to notice me waiting, and then to get me a drink and the bill, so I can't recommend the restaurant anyway

This was the second time that I've stayed at the Ritz in Chicago. First time was January 2011 and I received a much larger room and beautiful marble bathroom for $250 or less a night. This time I received a nice room, but much much smaller for over $500 a night in September 2012. Was somewhat disappointed with the value. Front desk people went out of their way to be helpful when checking in as you would expect with this quality of a hotel.

So I loved the Yotel. It was a small space but I loved the vibe. Very clean! Great Staff. I visited the NYC Yotel with my son. It was cool and fun exactly what I hoped for. The most interesting feature was the robotic arm that stored luggage in the lobby. Bed was comfortable though I wasn't sure that would be the case when viewing the futon style automated couch/bed

not impressed the swimming pool was not open nobody let us know in advance that the pool was not in operation the bathrooms could have been a lot better than this one was the calking around the tub to cover the cracks this motel needs a complete make over if i do come back i would not stay in this motel.. I wold rather spend a few dollars more to stay at a motel that makes you feel comfortable and this motel did not do that.

Convienience made this property viable for business meetings in the area. The hotel is very dated and was worth the money (booked on line great deal) but not a place I would take a spouse or partner to impress. If you are driving carry a GPS. As the location is off the highway and basket weaves of the freeways, very complicated from my point of view. Location to a wide variety of restaurants in the area was definitely a bonus. Staff were great but the aged property off set that commitment. And genuine effort.

I have tried many different hotels in NYC and I really liked this one. Front desk, bell boys and overall service staff is really nice. Rooms and bathrooms have a very good size, decor is fine, everything is clean. I liked the location, close to two subway stations on the green line, close to Union Square and lots of restaurants, easy to get from there downtown or uptown. Breakfast is included as well as wine and cheese in the evenings.

We spent two nights at The Surfer, where there is no air conditioning. The room was small, dingy and very warm. Fortunately there was a fan available, otherwise we would not have been able to stay. In addition, the sliding door screen had a broken lock which took quite a while to repair. The setting is nice, close to the beach which is very active with bikers, runners and skate boarders.

They charge for internet, breakfast, and room service is slow. The guy that bought my food said he went to the wrong room and no one was there so he waited. My food was cold and stale and who knows who's been breathing over it. My booking had these services for free but the hotel staff said otherwise. Even one of the staff said my internet is free when i called them from my room but when I checked out the guy said its not free, Found a bed bug on one of the beds too.

Hyatt Place was a clean, updated hotel, with good Highway access, but in the back 50 of a business parking lot. Lots of shopping and Restaurants within walking distance or a quick drive. Pool is decent although kinda right in the parking lot. Fitness room was better than average. WiFi intermittent. Friendly staff.

Extremely disappointed. My room is disgusting. There are hairs everywhere...all over the floor, stuck on towels. The bathroom is gross. The floor is dirty, the shower is slimy and filmy and has marks and moldy areas everywhere. The carpet is gross and has stains. The TV is from 1996. Given a room with a view of a rooftop with pipes and steam. The only thing I can say is that the staff who checked me in were nice...probably preparing me for my disgusting room.

We had a nice stay at the Westin. It's a great spot to stay as it's near trendy Newbury St with shops and restaurants and an easy cab ride to the historic parts. Our main complaint was the lifts. We were on the 35th floor so the view was great but we waited almost every time a long time for the elevator. One time my husband waited 13 minutes!

This hotel was really great to stay at. The staff was extremely helpful with all of my needs. Everything was in a convenient walking distance. There is a 7-Eleven on the corner, which I stopped at frequently. Eastern Standard, which is inside the hotel, had delicious food without having to leave the hotel. The only thing I wish this hotel had was a pool and/or jacuzzi to relax in after walking around Boston all day. All around great accommodations. I would definitely recommend this hotel to others.

From the moment you arrive you feel welcome! What a fun family resort! We will return! Everything you need to have fun is right there. Check it out...you will become a fan! The mature landscape is great too...you won't find yourself exposed to the sun without some relief. There is also plenty of parking.

The hotel was fine. I made two separate reservations for the same trip (one just for Friday night, and then a second for Thursday night). I called multiple times before the trip to confirm I would be in the same room for both nights, and no one could help me. I spoke to someone at the front desk the night before and he didn't know, and I had to make a phone call Friday morning to confirm I could stay in the same room. I would have appreciated a more proactive approach. The remote control was also broken...

Despite some negative reviews...I would say that the hotel is good and I would still recommend it to those people who consider an affordable room rate. Good location--restaurants nearby....close to Union Square and train station. Some hiccups: wifi connection is not that strong.it gets disconnected from time to time. Our room (105) was facing the street....we can hear noises from the streets especially fire truck sirens, which we found uncomfortable when we were about to catch our sleep. plus points: free coffee and tea at the lobby; good gesture for the cold weather in San Francisco.:-)

Ok, so this Hampton leaves you feeling like you need a shower after you leave. The elevator smells like a mechanics shop, the carpets were filthy, and the rooms had sort of musty smell. I wouldn't let my kids take off their shoes until they went to bed. The breakfast was great as per Hampton. I wouldn't stay here again nor recommend it to others. Not my usual Hamption experience at all.

This hotel was quite the find! It's in an excellent location: safe, walking distance to most attractions (including Beale Street), and quite reasonable. The staff was friendly, including the very personable and welcoming lady at the front desk during the day. The rooms were quite nice and very clean. If we ever visit Memphis again, which I hope we do, I will definitely go back to the Sleep Inn!

The Madera is not terribly fancy, but it was clean, quiet and comfortable. Had a great night's sleep. Room was big. Not much of a reception area to speak of, but the Firefly restaurant in the same building was nice to hang out in...their food was creative and excellent, though the drinks were a little pricey ($12.50 for a specialty cocktail.) Took me almost an hour to walk from the hotel to the National Mall. Red line metro stop is nearby.

My room was a no smoking room but it smelled like stale cigarette smoke. The breakfast seemed to be thrown together. Other motels at least one kind of meat. There were signs that warned people not to take food to their rooms or else they would be charged by the manager. The rear doors were blocked open all night. I was awaken at 6:00am when the loud tv in the lounge beneath my room was turned on for the breakfast crowd. The rug needed to be shampooed.

It was a very horrible stay that night in the Baymont hotel. I would not go back and do not recommend anyone this hotel. The Computer is not up to date which room is cleaned and which do not. The front desk has to reissue the room just because this discrepancy in the system. The hallway and outside of rooms are stincky smoke smelling. No AC in hallway and elevator. Bathroom and toilet are not clean enough. the toilet does not flush.

We had a clean average sized room - but we wanted a room with 2 queens plus a bathtub which meant they charged us 30dollars per night extra - if you want a lakeview room you will have to pay 40 dollars per night. We faced the air conditioners but not too bothered as we rarely spent any time in the room Hotel is beautifully decorated and very convenient to the art institute, millenium park and local transport links If you like power showers, the rain shower is not for you! All staff were helpful and polite

Arrived 5pm very quick check in. We had booked a grand queen room, room very large with 2queen beds. No view at all however very quiet and very large room. All staff very attentive, room service very good food excellent. Location fantastic 3 minute walk to union square where all the main shops are.

What more can you say for $49 a night in San Diego. Great location, very friendly and helpful staff, this is at the bottom end of SD budget rooms on hotel circle, so you get what you pay for, Room was clean but tired, and absolutely fine for what I wanted. WiFi at far end of the building is intermittent to say the least. bus stops outside and old town is close as well as shopping district in mission valley. Will you find better? yes, will it cost you more? yes a great deal more!

Just a minute from Times Square. Lots of theatres very close to the Edison Hotel. Room was fine, not too big, but OK. Very very thin walls. I could actually hear the guy in the room next to mine snore! And I could hear his telephone conversations word for word. I don't understand Hebrew, but could easily make out it was Hebrew. This is a very good, efficient hotel, nice, helpful staff. I liked the breakfast restaurant on the premises; not expensive; good food.

The hotel is nicely decorated, and has an excellent location, but seems to be in need of repairs and updating. I stayed on the top floor, which had a great view of the Riverwalk, and the pool, but the carpet in the hallway, and the furniture looked as though it needed replacing. The toilet also leaked, and occasionally had a bad (sewage) smell coming from it. Hotel service was average; nothing incredible.

The hotel may be nice for weddings but it is not for guests. The "wifi," which costs $15/day, is slower than dial up. The "breakfast room" is so small that it is hard to get a table. The drapery fell down in the room. There was no hot water for most of one day. These are just starters. The only positive thing I can say is that the valet is very nice and helpful.

A standard 5+ star hotel that have tried to add some local touches with their own honey, local produce, honey Martini etc. competing at this level I would like to see even more uniqueness. Nice breakfast, however I preferred the menu over the buffet as it (the buffet) was a little limited. Great restaurant and concierge staff, mixed experiences with the front desk. Note it takes special arrangement to get a limo service, and the BMW 7 series they brag about does not provide service to the airport (don't understand why not)

Have travelled a lot and this place hits towards the bottom. The only good thing about this hotel is the location at fishermans wharf, there is no dining facilities, bar or mini bar. We got a room with no balcony only a window that can be opened 3 inches that backs into the car park. Very poor staff who don,t care at all. With one exception guy who stored our bags he was nice ( check in is 4pm we arrived at 320) We wouldn't stay here again

My stay was excellent. All the staff -- front desk, housekeepers, bell staff, catering staff executive office staff -- were welcoming and helpful. I was there for a conference and spent five nights in March 2012 in a great room - 1007. It was well appointed and quiet, although I know that not all rooms were as peaceful or large. The housekeeping staff was very nice to me, including helping me to reunite with my bathrobe. I would definitely go back. Great location in San Antonio.

This hotel does not know the meaning of customer service or cleanliness, front desk staff very pompass and seemed irratible that we were checking. we had to wait an hour after legal checkin time to get a room and when we got the room it was infested with ants. Parking charges was absurd at $35.00 for a hotel guest. But i can give huge props to the bell staff for giving us info about area and transportation recommendations, considering no concierge was around also the transportation service was prompt and on time. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

I can't add much to the other reviews, other than to say that the staff were the most friendly I've had at a hotel in San Francisco, the property was stylish and the rooms were most comfortable. The hotel was a great place to hang out after a day full of activities. The one negative would be the location - it is a block away from some pretty shady action in the tenderloin. Still, I would recommend this to anyone.

The hotel was fine, with great location. We only stayed here for one night, and the hotel was ok. The rooms were very small, but clean. The staff was nothing special but nice. They had complimentary breakfast, we just walked down to have a look, but i would not eat that. Cheap standard, but if you are in NYC to be a real tourist, this location is great. It is close to times square and a lot of shopping.

Went to Chicago for a weekend with my two teenage children. Decided to go through hotwire and book a four star hotel, without knowing the name, but in certain locations. Ended with The Westin. The location was very good and convenient. The hotel was clean. That's about it. The room was surprisingly small. Two double beds in the room, and no room for a roll away. Yes, there literally was no room for a roll away. Bathroom was a bit dated, lobby was smaller. The hotel was ok, I expected more from a four star hotel.

Nice hotel, but skip the room service. Ordered room service and promised delivery in 20 minutes. After an hour called to inquire and they claim no record of the order. Very poor service for this level of hotel. No apology, no reasoning, no making it right. Never this hotel again.

Grouchy receptionist when I arrived at 11pm, incredibly drab and sad colors and decor, including the room which makes any hospital room look incredibly welcoming, no ice machine on the floor where the room was located. In addition $100 fee absolutely not communicated for smoking in the room. There are definitely much better centrally located hotels to stay in this price range in Boston.

This has to be the smallest motel room I've ever seen. It was fairly clean but broken towel rack, two towels for 4 people, no coffee some mornings and no cups the next! I was there for a week w/son and 2 grandkids and you needed a traffic cop to move around! It was NASCAR week and hard to find affordable rooms or we would have left after the first night.

I stayed here on business July 23-26 2012. The hotel was ran by a nice lady who worked quickly to get me situated even though I came before check-in time. The rooms were pretty clean and always well stocked with the essentials. Very cheap, great value. You're right next to OSU. You can walk to a couple good bars and restaurants from the hotel. (and I don't mean the Applebee's and McDonald's. :) ) Despite its motel design with outdoor facing rooms, I was never bothered by noise. Great A/C. Could use more TV channels.

My wife & I recently stayed at the InterContinental Chicago will visiting our son. Everything about our stay was wonderful. Check-in was quick. Our bags were quickly delivered to the room. The room was comfortable, clean & spacious. The pool is amazing! One of the best features is the hotel's close proximity to everything downtown. We highly recommend you stay at the InterContinental on your next visit to Chicago. You'll be glad you did.

Kimptom properties are at the top of our hotel picks list! Nice hotel, great staff/service! Great views of the city on one side and the river on the other. Hip rooftop bar with great drinks. Liked it so much we are considering a repeat stay when we bring our kids to experience NYC.

The hotel was just all right the property needs some TLC not enough attention to detail, room was stuffy, not clean. Had to have to come in the next day to fix the problem. Desk clerks Excellent 5 stars. If you want a good breakfast try Jerry's Deli down the street. Could have been much better.

We stayed for one night only. Great location, friendly staff and I appreciated the muffins and coffee in the morning. We had the shared bathroom which was clean, room was very small but also very nice. It was hot in the room but with the fan on and good firm bed we had a great night sleep.

The Curtis staff and rooms were lovely. But it was an older hotel and therefore you could hear the guest coming up and down the halls. Warm cookie on arrival was a nice touch. Staff was very helpful! We had a package and the wine and vouchers were in our room when we arrived!

Dark, dimly lit and not value for money. Very small rooms which are in need of refurbishment and have tiny bathrooms. Heating/Air Con noisy which is not helped by the poor insulation between rooms and the corridors. Second visit to this vibrant city and had four nights at this hotel but there are far better ones available. On the plus side the staff were very helpful.

I recently stayed at this hotel with my fiance as part of a weekend getaway to NYC. I found the hotel to be very clean. The front desk staff had good knowledge of the area and offered some good advice for getting a cab at 6PM on a Friday! The location of the hotel was a bit of a walk from the SOHO area, but if it is a nice day you shouldn't mind.

The Moderne hotel is very well located for central New York. I was disappointed with the room as it had no view, the room looked out onto the fire escape and the adjacent wall. It was comfortable enough wih a few exceptions we just used it as a bedroom The snacks provided were too expensive. although tea and coffee was on tap in the small lounge. The staff were friendly and helpful. The best thing was the hotels location, I would stay again but make sure we had a larger room.

This hotel used to be the Holiday Inn and they said they did a redesign and clean up of the hotel but it had the worst mold smell on my floor 16th floor a well as in my room. my clothes smell so bad and my sinus as so bad. i cold not sleep. I will never stay at this hotel again. They need to do a major clean up.

My husband and I, and two young adults stayed in a two bedroom suite. Clean, spacious. Housekeeping and reception staff very helpful and pleasant. Included are breakfast, and a few nights a week there is a "happy hour" with beer, wine, some food. So-so quality but a nice touch. We made use of the workout room and guest laundry. Within walking distance of restaurants, theater, opera, etc.

We stayed here recently as a family and chose two bunk rooms as they were cheaper and NY is expensive for a 10 days stay. There are better things to spend your money on! We expected a tiny room but it was more than adequate as whenever we were there, which wasn't often, we went up to the roof area. Very pleasant after a busy day. Restaurant just along the way was excellent - japanese/thai style food. We never waited for the bathrooms and they were always very clean. Location very convenient to subway.

Pros Inexpensive Easy access to DCA ($20 Cab) Free and fast WiFi Interesting old fashioned amenities (e.g. heated bathroom) Cons Overall very aged property Hard, hard uncomfortable pillows Room equipped with old 20" standard-definition TV Incredibly small bathroom with Leaky Tub Was placed in a room in basement in mock "village" with no window. Single representative at desk at check-in, appeared very overwhelmed Annoyingly loud click every time AC engaged

Hotel is near Times Square, but suffers from being surrounded by fast food joints and an occasional strip club. Unfriendly welcome at 0130 from a late long flight. Only room available on 3rd floor facing very busy Eighth avenue. Traffic noise well insulated except big trucks, but worst aspect was hearing and feeling every subway train many floors below. This space should not be sold for sleeping. Room and hotel was clean and bar seemed to have a happy crowd. Charging for internet its outrageous. its exactly the sort of thing that makes me look for a different chain.

All rooms redone late fall last year, so we definitely enjoyed our spiffy room with all the amenities ... shower is excellent ... HOPEFULLY the fairly dismal breakfast area will be the next to get "facelifted." It needs it. Location in Westwood (W LA) is excellent and just minutes from major attractions such as Beverly Hills, Hollywood, Malibu ... UCLA, etc. Also, even though we had a car, it was nice to be able to walk a bit to some locations. Manager (an expat NYer) was exceptionally efficient and helpful.

I loved the location and the view, but for the price I was disappointed. The room was no more than a standard hotel room, nothing special. The water pipes sounded like a jackhammer going off at 6am. The other issue is that one person has to take your luggage out of the car and into the lobby and another takes it to your room. This is not a resort, this extra handling is unnecessary .

The cost was excessive for this standard of room. The location & cleanliness were admirable; however, there were no tea/coffee making facilites or a fridge in the room which is a common feature in most hotels these days. The hotel is old and I was probably built around the 1930's: it shows in the bathroom, fixtures and model of air conditioner in the room. On the plus side: a good central location for 7th Avenue and a stones throw from Times Square, Central Park and most of the other highlighted attractions.

Stayed here on business in June for a week. Perfectly located for the shops on 5th avenue and central park. The check in was super swift which was great but the service experience thereafter was poor. Got woken up twice by the laundry service calling who were asking questions about my cleaning and the maid service did not clean my room to 5 star standards and my shampoo disappeared.

We stayed for two nights before continuing our trip and were delighted with our choice. The staff were very welcoming and friendly. The concierge was extremely helpful and gave us very good advice which proved to be exactly what we wanted. We hired a car - thanks to the concierge - and drove to Long Beach to see the Queen Mary. Leaving the hotel early next morning and taking the courtesy transport was easy and staff were very helpful.

As a an spg member, the extras were great. Club level lounge was very nice and had a beautiful view of the lake. Staff was very nice, especially Tamera in the club lounge. The room was okay after you get past the wierd divider wall. Very nice location. Close to the high end mall and a lot of restaurants. I would stay here again.

I can't recommend the Hungtington enough! Besides being beautiful, with spacious rooms, and having that old architectural charm you don't see in hotels anymore, it also provided beautiful views of the cathedral and the city..and it provided much needed RR for this hardworking teacher duo that needed a break! Oh, and it wasn't bad on two teacher's pocketbooks! Highly recommend...we did use Hotwire, and glad we did!

After a very long trip of riding I thought I'd splurge a little and get my wife a hot tub suite to relax in. I was surprised to find a jacuzzi tub in the bathroom. When I asked the front desk if they had hot tub suites she said "yes, they have jacuzzis in them." So in other words, NO. Secondly, the air conditioner kept cutting in and out during that night, which left the room hot all night. And thirdly, their definition of hot breakfast was packet oatmeal and a toaster for bagels. I would not stay again.

Being very often on Business Trips, I never experienced such a disaster. It is impossible de sleep in tho hotel, people are drinking, shouting around the pool and in the corridor ALL NIGHT long. And I experienced 3 nights there. I was as well with some colleagues and they had the same experience, so it does not depend on the room. Do not go there if you need to rest or on a Biz trip, ever.

We selected this hotel because the reviews seemed very good and downtown located. We stayed in this hotel for two nights and were very disappointed with the service.The hotel is located in an industrial area, next to the highway. If you want to go in downtown is really difficult .... The staff is rude and the rooms are old and poorly maintained.

This Ritz Carlton is definitely not up to par. This would be one of the hotels in a chain that ruins the reputation for all others. Take my advice and spend your money elsewhere. My credit card, as well as, my business partner's credit card was charged for additional charges. The amounts were in correct. I have spent my Monday back at work on the phone with their finance department trying to walk them through how to properly charge the amount for room service. SUBSTANDARD would be the nicest way to describe this hotel.

The location of the hotel was good and they have a good lounge but, for the price we paid we expected a much better room and service. The room was dark and lighting fixture was missing light bulbs. The towels were few and old. the elevators are so slow and it takes a long time to get to your room. On the whole I would not be returning to this hotel and won't recommend it to anyone.

We were told that our room rate would be only $45 a night for doing the Scotts Antique Show, it was much higher. The mattress on the bed was very old and the 2 pillows were flat. When we asked for new pillows we were told there were no others. The room was very musty smelling. We will be returning on Dec 14 and are thinking we will be staying at the Holiday Inn since there rooms were only $45 a night. I've always used Baymont in the past but was very disappointed this trip.

We had a fun time at the hotel. It's nice for an older hotel. Very updated and the rooms are nice. Our bathroom was a little small though with not much counter space. They did mess up our reservation the first night we were there. We booked a king room and all they had left was two double beds. They did find us another room and then upgraded us the following night.

This hotel was ok, no major issues. Breakfast was pretty good and the rooms were clean. The hotel is a little run down in appearance, and there is no elevator so we had to drag our stuff up 2 flights of stairs, which was a minor inconvenience. The water pressure in the shower was AMAZING and the staff was efficient. We wanted to visit Beale Street and Graceland during our visit and the hotels was located within 20 minutes of both. The beds were very comfortable and the price was good.

poor hotel, when i booked it they say they hav a complimentary breakfast but in reality it was burned coffee and a few cookies were their defination of breakfast. dont waste ur money on this hotel. I asked for salt and the man on reception said "sorry this is not a restaurant".

Old, shabby and unkempt. Dirty sink, dirty bath and dank smelling. Old creaky air conditioner. I booked this HI by accident instead of the decent one farther out on Baymeadows. Only redeeming feature was decent WiFi. If I was in the area for more than 1 night I would have walked.

The location is convenient, right off the freeway with restaurants and shopping nearby. The property needs updating, the tile in the shower is cracked and moldy. The refrigerator and freezer was well worn. The shower head is very low for a tall person. Wi-fi worked well and I liked the adjoining rooms to allow more space for my family.

Paid for a suite .. checked in none available (party had not check out and they couldn't find them)... only received an apology.. I said how bout buying dinner ... desk clerk said breakfast ... I said kick it up to your manager..she said she'd call them ...I had to come back down to inquire another clerk apologized said yes. .... Old historic hotel great location ....out dated fixture not sure if that is intentional or not... good food!

Hotel was much nicer than I expected. Stayed here for Austin City Limits. You have to book hotels way in advance for ACL. Good rate. Just remodeled. One complaint is how rude the front desk agent was when I called to ask for an early check in. Check in is at 3:00pm. I asked for 2:00pm when I would arrive in Austin. The man's answer and tone of voice were very disappointing. Clean room. Nice bed pillows. Continental breakfast had good selection cereals, bagels, waffles, burritos, fruit and yogurt.

My stay was only for one night: I wish I'd more time at my disposal. Staff were smiling and helpful without being obtrusive; the setting, including amenities like a roof-top pool, were equal to a five stars' hotel. Of course, Colorado is one of the most beautiful states, (but on my return, the accommodations elsewhere were not comparable.)

This is ridiculous! Why dont they not put guests right next to the construction. My room was right next to it. Walls are also very thin - you can hear your neighbors next door and above you. Would never stay here again. WIsh I would have read the reviews before staying here!

Too bad. It is a lovely building with great pool area, but tyhe air conditioning isn't up to the heat in Phoenix. It would be too hot for Juneau! The management's response was "Well, it's been hot here." In Phoenix? Really? I had to move out to the couch to sleep- it was cooler there. The next night we switched hotels-went to one that was 5 times the age of the Doubletree. Guess what? It was cool. The management's response was the worst part.

DO NOT BOOK...there's no elevator..the rooms are the size of a matchbox...bathrooms are ridiculously small and not very clean...the pictures are very deceiving and the rooms are WAY over priced...although they're reasonable for NYC....but if they're reasonable and look nice they're way too good to be true like this hotel was! Their photographer needs to be rewarded because the pictures and the price got me to book this hotel but the room was so horrible I checked out the next day and found another hotel...

I stay in this hotel for one night from Sunday to Monday. The room was like a small closet. The bed was like sleeping on a jail bunk. The pillows was flat pancakes and my God. The bathroom shower was the worst. The water dripped out of the shower head. Making it very hard to wash up and start your day. I would NEVER stay in this hotel again......smh

Just a block from the Air & Space Museum and close to the mall. Easy walking to just about every DC attaction. Hotel is clean. Pool is great for cooling off on a hot day although not very luxurious. Breakfast buffett is good and very convenient. Bar/restaurant is okay and nice place to unwind. Starbucks in the lobby is a plus. Taxi's always available, never a wait. You do get a little noise from the train track that is nearby but the location is worth it. One block to L'enfant Plaza Metro stop.

A great location and confortable rooms! If you enjoy your sleep then don't stay here. The walls are thin and you can hear EVERYTHING!!! We moved rooms once but it was just as bad. We hardly slept and when we gave the reception feedback - she simply responded with "we'll that's the weekend for you!" I was a little disappointed and won't be staying here again. I can't believe it's 4 stars either!!

was put in a non smoking room that reaked of smoke. i was then put in another room that did not smell of smoke but had burn marks on the furniture and the bed linens. i was very disappointed in this hotel, considering it is associated with the wyndham hotel chain

I had a really great time staying here for a conference. It was for 3 nights and 4 days. The room was nice and overlooked the pool on the 8th floor. The conference was actually in the hotel and the food and the rooms for the conference were really nice. The pool area is amazing to look at and there were a lot of malls and restaurants close to the hotel. The hotel staff was always friendly and they answered all my questions.

We stayed here for two nights this past weekend. The lobby is very nice looking and buzzing with people. The location is wonderful, Close to the Navy Pier and the Water Tower. The rooms are horrid. They need to be updated. Reminds me of a 1970 Holiday Inn room. The bathroom is so small. I probably would not stay here again.

My older brother and my 17 year old son stayed on a trip to flordia last week. We needed a cot or a roll away bed for my son but Johnny didn't have a fold away bed available so he gave us a conecting room for the $10 extra person rate! I found the rooms clean, comfortable and Johnny's hospitality is second to none! Any time I find myself in Indy or anywere near indy I'll be back!

The nice hotel staff tries really hard but their service was slow and inconsistent. The room the second day wasn't completely made up. The air conditioning ran all day with doing much to make the room temperature cool. Check in was slow and picking up my bags upon leaving was very slow. The art deco style demonstrated an attempt of embracing a style, but the room was dated and not put together. The large rooms size and location are a plus, but overall I was less than impressed by the overall service and aesthetic of this hotel.

This used to be a great place to stay but the rooms and hall ways are now worn and dirty. Still lots of people and the bridges bar is still good but the service and the hotel needs a makeover badly. The service has gone down hill but really it is the overall hotel that needs some investment.

We booked this hotel because of the King Tut Exhibit package they were offering but would certainly stay here again! Super location right in the center of Seattle. Close to shopping, the Pacific Science Center, Aquarium, Pikes Market and only a $12 cab ride to the zoo. Very friendly staff and my son loved the fireplace in the lobby. Great food too :)

This hotel is magnificent and really delivers... the first impression from the lobby, the dining room, and all of the details in the guest rooms. But the highlight is the hotel's very own honey - made by bees on the roof. It's a must-try at the lovely breakfast buffet. We had a family wedding trip to this hotel with international guests and it suited everyone... including a hilarious time dancing in the Tonga Lounge. On the downside, they charge guests for internet access. Overall, 9/10.

Rooms were clean and neat. Studio is larger than a normal room but not by much. Good place if you are looking to be close to seattle attractions without being downtown. Very close to UW. I would stay again. Cafe in the lobby area is limited. Underground parking deck was big plus. Booking in advance can save you some money if you have a multi day stay.

I was so unhappy with my stay. I trusted reviews on booking site, which didn't mention 1 thing about the construction nightmare. Don't stay here until construction is done. The lobby is boxed in leaving a small open are on the 2nd floor for checkin. The "extra" staff were not helpful. For many question, like may I have a shower cap and where can I get a soda, I was told to go to the store across the street.

Hotel rooms are spacious & equipped with kitchenette in addition to in house vending and laundry machines. This makes it suitable for longer stay clients wishing to do their own cooking. The hotel is located within 5 minutes to entertainment a food outlets, and some 15 minutes walking distance from major shopping malls. Reasonable priced with free WiFi however, with once a week cleaning, which I found a but disturbing. Good value for money.

Rooms are dated as is the whole hotel, the location was good for where I needed to be, I found it amazing that I had to wait for staff to fix their breakfast in the small breakfast area. This is ok for a cheap business trip and you are there for sleeping only.

Two things stand out - first being the size and attractiveness of th King Suites. I've never stayed in a room that seemed so large, comfortable, inviting and well arranged. The bed was very comfortable, everything was just as it should be. The second very nice thing about this hotel was the friendly staff and management. That's true at a lot of hotels, but when you combine this along with a very nice place to stay, it is a winner in Baltimore. I'm defniitely staying here from now one. Price was very reasonable through choice hotels.com.

With all the renovation going on the hotel is really uncomfortable and for the price ou pa ou can get so etching better. With all going on they should be selling at a 50% discount at least. Location is good but you can find so ethi g better nearby. The rooms are really little and although this was a renovated room the bathroom faucets were loose And not looking good. All corners were Inc,Dan and dusty. Did not like my stay here at all

Walked up to the Front Desk, the individual looked my my profile, called me by my last name and welcomed me back to The Westin. Then he said since I was Gold status, he immediately would upgrade me for free to a larger room with a water view of San Diego. Plus he would have two free bottles of water waiting for me since he knew I was going to use the workout facilities. Starwood SPG program is simply the best!

Stayed 16-18 June. Weekend so they close the club floor "corporate policy" Thanks for nothing. Toilet did not flush properly, had to call for repair. Next morning the shower handle fell off. TV(digital) had pixel problems and poor reception. Called repair again. I stayed the night before at a Red Roof Inn, paid 1/3rd the price but the TV worked and free internet. Hilton get a clue if you want to charge $200 per night at least the TV and bathroom could work. $10 for wireless? Told management all the problems, all we got was "oh, sorry" Confirmation #3475075336

This is my second and positively last stay here at this hotel. They cancelled my reservation and then changed the rate on me at check in, and then told me the manager would fix it on Monday. I got absolutely no where with the manger, reservations, or corporate. There are 100's of hotels so spend your $$$ somewhere else because if you have any issues these people will not resolve them. The location is great but customer service it the worst I have ever experienced.

Due to the hurricane we were stuck in the room for more hours that we had expected to be, The internet service was very inconsistent make the time significantly more difficult. I also would have liked to have been made aware that the room had no window when I made the reservation. It was very difficult to get the temperature down to a comfortable level.

After all the extra "fine print" charges, my $220.00 bill quickly turned into a $300.00 bill ! * Please be careful.* The charges for parking per day alone is ridiculous ! Every spoken word, noise and snore from those around us was easily heard through the walls. The staff was not friendly at all. The hotel had a stench about it on the floor where our room was.

This Hotel was dirty, old and rundown. For what they charge a night they could maybe put some of that money back into the hotel, walls, doorframes and lights were dirty, dusty, burnt out light bulbs, I don`t think the corners of the rooms have been vacumed in a long time, you could hardly see out the windows either. Staff was there but far from friendly, no one seemed happy to be at work, just doing their job....

Just another big city hotel with typical big city rates like $45 per night self parking. Although recently "refreshed" this property is dated in so man ways. The one advantage that is has is its proximity located in the middle of shopping on the Magnificent Mile as well as Navy Pier. It helps to be in their frequent stayer program to catch a small break on the parking fee and getting "free" Internet. When will these hotels catch up to the modern world where all internet access is free.

Great food,really first class clean bedrooms and a lively bar .The hotel is in a good location for the nightlife of Rush street .It is a modern hotel ,the staff are trained to a very high standard and I believe probably one of the best Chicago hotels in a safe area of town with all the good shopping nearby and opposite .The only shame is there is no pool.

We stayed at the Westin Riverwalk this week on a pleasure trip. And a pleasure it was indeed staying at this hotel. Service by the entire staff was terrific. We particularly want to single out a member of the Bell Staff, Jose Alvarado, who was very helpful to us during our stay.

I stayed here on a business trip 3/15/12 I awoke the next morning to ROACHES on the ceiling and desks. This hotel was deplorable. The worst I have ever stayed at. Thank God my wife and kids were not with me. They also stated a mysterious 2% tax would be added on which was unpublished and coulldnt be explained. Please avoid this hotel. It was like the crack infested drug hotels you would see on a movie.

The hotel is situated right on the edge of the rough part of town but is in a good location for walking around the city or taking the trolley. The hotel staff is very pleasant but the room that we were staying in was so incredibly loud. The sounds outside at the hilton across the street made it near impossible to sleep. Next time we are in San Fran we will pay a little extra to be further away from the "rough" part of town and we will hopefully find a room that is not so loud.

There was a mix-up in our room reservations, but the staff handled the situation and we were very pleased with our accommodations and our stay. The location is excellent for walking to many of the attractions and the staff was very pleasant to us and our grandchildren. We all had a wonderful time. The hotel is undergoing some redecorating, so there is a noise factor at times. However, the renovations are beautiful.
