Overall quality of the hotel is good. Wifi in the rooms is expensive, but the lobby is free. Further out from the attractions than I expected, so used the Underground which was fine. Mix up regarding my airport shuttle pickup after hotel staff gave me the wrong information. Aircon very noisy.

This hotel falls way short of my expectations for a 4 star hotel. I had to move to a second room because the smell of mildew in the first room was unbearable. They missed my wake-up call. The bathroom had two lotions but no shampoo. And the toilet wasn't level/flush with the floor so it was wobbly when you sat on it.

honeymoon stay while travelling the coast line . the most beautiful clean modern place we ever stayed. staff wonderful helpful, kind. geat value almost too cheap for such a wonderful room, breakfast is typical american motel , cereal coffee muffin . but could not fault this inn . shampoos towels top quality great location gretta and shane rabbitte

We found the Belvedere to be the exact hotel for us! Central location, friendly staff and very comfortable room and bed. We were recommended by friends to stay here and we were not disapointed. Safe & Secure and well looked after! The elevator could use a bit of help but we were on vacation so we were in no hurry! The room temperature was perfect and cleaning staff were excllent along with the friendly door staff who gave us great tips and directions on this fabulous City that does not sleep!

I checked-in at this Red Roof Inn on the night of the 26th of June for three nights.The hotel is located 10 minutes south of 6th Street and right off I-35.It's clean,rates are reasonable,and close to different highways that one can use to get to where they desire to go with ease.The staff is very friendly and helpful.I would stay here on the next trip to Austin.

The W San Francisco really went above and beyond the Starwood standards. My husband and I stayed for 3 nights for my birthday celebration. The service was outstanding and the room was marvelous. The staff was very caring and pleased our every need. We loved everything about it! Will be staying here every time we visit San Francisco, without a doubt.

Went to the GSA Conference and stayed at the Hyatt Regency San Antonio. Everything was WONDERFUL. The decor, the room, the service - all was great. Hotel is directly on the Riverwalk. It was convenient to everything!. Had in-room breakfast and it was truly wonderful. Beware though, they already include the gratuity and delivery in the amount - so no need to tip extra. Jose Rosales checked me out and offered to print my boarding pass. He provided excellent service.

This hotel wasn't the nicest, but for the price its not bad. The bed and room were nice enough. I did not like the bathroom however. It felt very run down. The top floor is half smoking rooms/half non-smoking rooms which makes the entire floor smell, so if you're not a smoker make sure you ask for a different floor. The location is pretty good though. We took a cab to 6th street for about $10. Also its right off of I-35 which makes it pretty easy to get to.

Dated rooms, terrible service and elevators out. The absolute silliest thing I have ever heard was them visiting the room at 1AM asking for a TV at 50% of volume telling me the volume was too loud and that should could hear it, I stepped out into the lobby and couldn't hear it. The girl sent to my room was also just making stuff up.

very small room ,price parking garge to high, they charge my credit card towice, when i ask them to fix it they said you had two car this why which is not tru after talk to 3 pepole in front desk they find out they did mistake and said they going to fix it but nothing happen yet , im not coming back , they very Unprofessional.

We stayed at this hotel the weekend of July 28. The staff is very friendly and helpful. You will love Sunny & Jaime ask them to show you the handshake. The room was very nice and clean. The free breakfast was delicious! You will really enjoy your stay here. The hotel is located on a quiet street and within walking distance to everything. Thanks for your professionalism. Returning on 8/4 SSJ

Hotel was great, the location for those going to Qualcomm HQ is perfect and walking distance. The hotel is modern with everything you need for a very reasonable price. For those looking for a holiday this is not the place and far from the beach but for business great. Breakfast was great and all you need. Coffee, Tea and cookies can be found in the lobby 24 hours a day for free. Rooms are large and with everything you need.

This was the first time I've stayed at this hotel and I was not disappointed. The rooms are a bit small, but very clean! The location is great - whatever you want to do is within a 5-10 block radius. The staff is a delight, especially Mia - she is very kind and helpful. I will definitely stay here on my next trip to New York City!

Attended a conference in Los Angeles recently and enjoyed my stay at the Westin Bonaventure very much. Loved the city view from my room, because the towers are round providing a much better view. Westin quality and service throughout the hotel, with great restaurants for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Options for fine dining or lighter fare.

I'm a fan of boutique hotels and this place looked nice according to the website. I should have known better and checked other reviews. This place was a dump. Torn carpet, stains, mold in the bathroom, the toilet seat was chipped and worn (seriously? I could fix this in 10 minutes and $20), the bed was uncomfortable and sagged in the middle and the linens were anything but high quality. I have had better stays in a motel 6. The only plus was the great balcony off of the room. But, even that wouldn't make me stay there again.

I was on a business trip and booked this Hotel. If someone is looking for a good location and doesn't care about anything else this would be the hotel for them. The lobby was renovated but deceiving. The rooms were old. Shower was not clean. A/C didn't work and it was 85 degrees that night. Beds were squeaky. Extremely old rugs, doors were scratched and not painted. In all it was a disastor. I have travelled a lot and have stayed in many Hotels. I would certainly categorize this one as the worst.

We booked a King size bed at the Doubletree - Cambell Centre in Dallas,TX over a month in advance. Upon arrival the front desk tells us they have no King size beds. They have given all of them or are saving them for Hilton Honors customers. After some being persistent we received a queen size room that was significantly smaller. When asked about a reduced rate, the front desk person was almost rude telling me that being as this was prepaid he couldn't reduce the rate.

I enjoyed my stay at the Hilton Boston Downtown very much. The location is ideal, and the staff is great…very welcoming and very knowledgeable. I would especially like to thank Ali for making our stay the best it could be. I will definitely look into booking this hotel again in the future. After visiting Boston for many years this hotel was the best for the money.

We booked in and were shown to a very basic room, old furniture and a very outdated bathroom. The pool in the middle of the hotel was dirty with leaves and algae. We booked a bed and breakfast - breakfast consisted of coffee from a machine and cold plastic wrapped breakfast pastries. Wouldn't stay there again.

Hilton website advertised free wired internet. Even after showing them this, I was notified by a snobbish front desk staff that no such thing existed, and I'd have to pay $10/night for wireless. Rooms were terrible. Sure your lamps look fancy, but you don't even have a fridge or microwave. No complementary breakfast, no free airport shuttle, $15/night for a roll-away bed, and they actually wanted $10/night for parking. I consistently get way better service from even the cheapest of economy hotels. I feel used and extorted.

Stayed in the Superior Suite, enough room for 2 adults and 2 teenagers. Bathroom was a bit small, but having the dressing room allowed for a bit more space. Full kitchen and eating area, which allowed for us to spread out a bit. Great having the continental breakfast to start the day. Walking distance to the Capitol building, if heading down to the Lincoln Memorial etc, can be a long walk when hot. Comfortable beds. Guest laundry and dryer. Staff are friendly and helpful. Room was clean and tidy.

Using the bathroom faucet a bunch "gunk" came out from behind the faucet. The fridge, microwave and desk light didn't work. Clerk said "Oh? Sorry." To use the micro we had to move it to the Night Stand and unplug the clock. Carpets filthy. Thank goodness I bring flip flops to wear in hotels. They also need more help on a Saturday evening. People across the hall, awake at 4:30 in the morning, loud, door propped open with noise and smoke going into the hall.

We spent three nights at the Dana Hotel in Chicago recently in this 'just right modern with comfort' hotel -- great bathrooms, bright rooms, deep mattresses. The Dana has the best location in town, great food at Argent, wonderful staff and a super bar - Vertigo at the top of the building. Great value all around!

This hotel took advantage of Sandy by overcharging guests. The internet was non-existent in our room, several electrical outlets did not work, the breakfast area was a mess, and all of this for more than $500 per night. Wrote complaint and received an insulting reply from hotel staff. Very glad that Holiday Inn Hotel bailed us out of this place.

We stayed at the Park central for 4 days in June this year for our Anniversary. We had a great stay at this Hotel and plan go to back when we visit New York again. Want to say a BIG THANK YOU to Kristen Buurmen she made our stay even better by providing excellent hospitality for our Anniversary, but made that extra effort by helping us throughout our visit, she is an asset to the Hotel.

This Hotel is decent, but nothing special. We stayed two nights. It is a bit pricey for what you get. It is located at the north end of Mile High Stadium property, which is convienient for Bronco home games. It appears that there hasn't been much interest in upkeep or upgrades in recent years. We thought the shuttle service would be a nice feature, but found out that the 11:00pm last run time really means don't bother calling for the service after 10:30pm. We got stranded downtown. Dissappointing.

Convenient to sites and public transportation. Affordable price for the city. Followed another reviewers comments. Parking at the hotel is outrageous just go around the corner on Vine St and there are numerous commuter lots. This is a big hotel. Lobby is huge so it feels like a convention center hotel. Elevators are slow. TV stations were quirky. Bed comfortable, room clean, bathroom very clean, would stay there again. Check the cancellation policy to see if it meets your needs. Hotel web site had a cheaper rate after I had booked through Starwood.

Have stayed here several times for business. Have to say the rooms are not that comfortable and of course bc it is NYC rooms are mostly small, but to be expected. Of course, the lobby area is very cool and the location is quite ideal! The staff is decent, not over helpful though.

This hotel combines small rooms (i am aware most Manhattan hotel rooms are small) with bad service, to few elevators and a crowed lobby and queues to reception. i was requested to change rooms, for no apparent reason, i was under the impression the first room was a backup room in case of overbooking as i checked in very late, but I was actually downgraded to a smaller room the net day. In total i must have spend 1.5 hours queuing at reception to change rooms just to find the new room had no space to move.

We stayed 2 nights at the Embassy, Logan airport. The hotel is not located close to restaurants or activities. The rooms were nice enough and clean. We always look forward to the cocktails at the managers reception. In MA or at least Boston,,,they can not give out free drinks at the reception. We paid extra thinking this would be a nice perk. I should have done my homework. Will look for a closer hotel in the future.

Nice boutique hotel 2 min walking distance from Time Square, near a metro station. Staff were very helpful and welcoming. Room was modern, comfortable and spacious. Breakfast was good, not a lot of choice but it was included so we cant really complaint! Free Wi-fi, wine hour every day from 4 to 5 was a nice touch too. I highly recommend this hotel!

I got a good internet deal for this hotel, and was very pleased to receive a free room upgrade almost immediately after I had booked. Rooms are a good size, and well appointed. Air conditioners are incredibly noisy though - so distracting and made it difficult to sleep. Very friendly staff, even helping out with recommendations for running routes. Not a bad start for this new refit, but needs more polish to get a better rating. It's not cheap, but is only decent value at the moment

First off, I was upgraded to a suite (mid-week in February) which was a lovely surprise. Staff was all very accomodating and pleasant. Views from my corner room were just spectacular and bed was very comfortable. Internet was $10 for the day and worked well. Nice location from which to just take a stroll around Manhattan's Upper-Eastside. Close to Sotheby's Auction House and almost under the 59th Street Bridge. Didn't eat in the restaurant, but went and checked it out - - really nice atmosphere and fabulous views. Would stay here again.

Staff is nice but the rooms are small and very expensive, plus they screwed up my reservation. I expected more and was surprised they charged for everything, it was as bad as the airlines. Would not stay again if not foe the convention center which makes the location great for handicapped and in the winter.

The rooms are big & comfortable, and clean. I heard no street noise. The fridge & microwave were nice to have available, & the service was very helpful. No, it's not a fancy place, but it was very close to MCRD, and it met my needs just fine. I look forward to staying there next time I'm in San Diego.

pluses: It is quite close to Denver airport and only about 15 minutes by car to downtown, has a swimming pool and ... rabbits grazing around the Motel :) minuses: Service at the reception was rather unfriendly and mechanical. You have to pay for wi-fi! No fridge, microwave or even a remote for tv. Very derelict neighbourhood. If you have a flight very early it's a good option, otherwise look for other place.

Stayed here for a friends wedding. It should have been clear from the time of making my reservation that there would be problems. Upon entering the hotel, there were a group of irate customers, and a very non interested staffer. The maids down the hall were talking so loud at 8 am that I had to ask them to keep it down. Cute spaces, but too little staff. The Burger joint next door is awesome though.

Hotel St. James is just around the corner from Times Square; and a short walk to Rockefeller Center; you can't beat the location. But the hospitality of the staff was lacking; as were the amenities - no ice, no soda machines, barren (but clean) rooms. For the right price, I'd stay again. But the attitude of the staff really put me off.... therefore, I'd be willing to pay more elsewhere. Another plus - it is next to Cafe Cranberry - a wonderful deli that has all sorts of food and is open 24/7.

upon arrival we were greeted by protester i felt very imtimadated, they also woke us up at 7 in the morning, round the corner was a disco so all you heard was shoutingand screeming from about midnight. The hotel was not very clean and had ripped carpets in the lift. STAY AWAY it spoiled our trip to sanfransisco.

I chose this thinking that it couldn't be too bad if it was close to the airport and they catered to travelers. This place was aweful. The coffee in the morning was as weak as tea and cold. The carpeting was filthy and the latch on the door was loose. I would not recommed this place to anyone.

Good hotel. Clean, convenient, etc... Make sure you insist on a room away from the street however. A fire station is literally 100 yards away and they are busy. Very noisy street side. As many have said the location is excellent for walking to most of the major attractions. There is also a subway station very close. The staff are helpful and welcoming. The breakfast and rooms are also clean and well delivered.

We decided at the last minute to book a hotel near Union Square and this one fit our needs perfectly. We were on the Club Level and our room was very nice and clean, with Aveda products in the bathroom. Front desk service was very friendly. Happy hour was a fun place to relax, and the bartender was really pleasant. Another good surprise was our room was really quiet. Last time we stayed in San Francisco, we heard people outside all night long. We loved this hotel, and will stay here again.

Hotel was clean and comfortable - attended as part of a convention, price was fair for a hotel at a convention. The website misled the 'club lounge' for Sheraton Club members hosting complimentary breakfast and happy hour appetizers - this only applies if you are a premier member their website glaringly misses this "small" detail to the disappointment of this traveler with no apologies by the staff.

Stayed here as part of a work conference. Located on a sad block. Lobby looked like a bus station, and the clerk was chilling when we entered. The room was clean and quiet, but the pillows were tiny squares. Definitely a budget accommodation, and I wouldn't recommend if you are a fan of the finer things.One upshot: The hotel is a short walk down to the Inner Harbor and not too far of a walk from Camden Yards.

We stayed at this hotel on a business trip in Feb. 2012. The hotel is clean, in a great location, and has great water pressure. Room layout is convenient. Beds are reasonably comfortable. Best thing about staying here is the hot cookie you receive upon check-in. (They're really good cookies!) We'd definitely stay here again.

After having stayed at the beautiful and gracious Marriott Marquis in San Diego, I thought a reservation at the Marriott Marquis in San Francisco was a safe bet. I was immediately disappointed. The room I was given was small, the decor outdated and aged, and the basic facilities lacking. The refridgerator in the room was available only for mini-bar selections and stated that personal items would be disposed of. That was the final insult and I cancelled my six night reservation and checked out.

Stayed here one night on our way to South Carolina and were pleasantly pleased. Rooms were HUGE, clean and the bed was very comfortable. Bathroom could use a bit of updating but overall it was clean and towels were not the cheap ones I've noticed in hotels before. Complimentary breakfast was also good.

Suites are a good size, with very interesting use of space. I had a room on the 7th floor, and in my suite the bathroom was at the end of the suite. Kitchens are a decent size, but if you want to do any 'cooking', I had to request a portable cooktop. Room was quiet and had lots of windows to let in natural sunlight. Hotel is close to major attractions and riverwalk. I used the fitness center - pretty small and can fill up quickly at peak hours. I did not have a chance to eat breakfast there.

Save your money and go elsewhere. It is very worn and out-dated. I had to get the maintenance man to come and move the huge tv cabinet so that I could access the room climate control. The staff seemed okay, but did not go out of their way to be helpful. When I wanted to speak to the concierge there was no-one to be found. Apart from this, I found it to be in a good location and there was free wi-fi in the lobby.

Location, Location Location... that's is what it is all about. Front desk service was good. Parking at $38 plus tax per night is a little much, and I would certainly research next time where to leave the car. Right next to Ford's theater and walking distance to everything. It was all we needed as we were not in the room that much. Room was clean and service was just good. Traveled July 24-28th.

Just spent 2 nights while visiting colleges in Boston, and the hotel was very clean, the staff was helpful, the location was centrally located for all the places we needed to get to. As a bonus in the cold weather - there are 2 malls attached to the hotel so it's easy to find something to eat without having to go outside. Plus it was a very easy walk from the South Bay Amtrak station. We had an awesome view of the Charles River from the 20th floor. Would definitely stay there again!

Our online reservation was mysteriously lost, causing costly and time consuming calls to the booking agency to determine what the cause of the problem was (One Washington Circle's incompetent staff). After our stay, mysterious charges appeared on the credit card which were not explained. When calling the hotel (from Australia) to attempt to get an explanation, the staff repeatedly put us on hold, causing more expensive phone calls. A truly awful customer experience!! Avoid this hotel like the plague!!

We stayed recently for a weekend, very nice accommodations. We also had the breakfast buffet included for 2 adults using AAA. By far the best breakfast buffet I have had at any stay. Made to order eggs, waffles and just about anything you could ask for at breakfast. They had a nice pool and spa. The lobby bar was nice and had a wall of TV's if you wanted to catch a game. Location was perfect for shopping, the Navy Pier, and local attractions. I would highly recommend this and would defiantly stay again.

I stayed at 339 West 39th street and it had a Candlewood Suites sign out in front of it,that's where the resemblance to these reviews ends.First off,one of the elevators hasn't worked for 3 days.#2-asked the front desk to have the linens and towels changed once in 6 days,returned 9.5 hours later to find nothing had been done.Called the front desk and the housekeeper told me if the housekeeping sign was not outside the door,it would not be cleaned.The sign magnetic sign says "No Housekeeping Required".I won't be back.

My room was dirty with what appeared to be mold in the bathroom. The pool was a very uninviting shade of green…the area around the pool looked like it had not been kept up for years. I’m not sure when the photos on the website were taken but they are nowhere near to reflecting the current condition of the hotel. The staff was friendly and helpful but the hotel itself is a dump, I would never stay here again.

A good choice : - room are very clean - staff friedliness is above average - a central location for visiting new york - free wifi in the room - quiet room (at least for our room on 26th floor) - free fitness center but - room are very small - breakfast at the hotel is really standard and not fancy - no swimming pool, sauna or steam bath - price is quite high

Not quite sure what all the hype is about. I'm a Starwood Gold member and other than the location was good for me, its not the best property I've stayed at. Building is very old. rooms are big, but old (furniture is updated). Hallways and elevator were freezing, I have heard if you don't stay in the new towers the rooms can get cold as well. Room service was overly expensive. I would say at the Westin on Market street instead...newer building and better set up.

Looks a little more run down than pictures online on the outside, but rooms looked decent. Aside from one woman who worked there being slightly rude & short with me when i checked in, everyone else was polite. Overall my stay was fairly decent until my last morning, i woke up being stared down by a roach 6 inches from my face. & that same woman was extremely unhelpful when i mentioned it.

This is the third time I've stayed at this hotel. It's steps away from the hustle and bustle of Times Square, but is a totally refined, elegant hotel, with excellent service and staff. The beds are great, and while the rooms are small, they're tastefully modern. Great hotel. Love staying here.

I wish I could like this stay but I find it hard to convince myself to do so...everything from check in to room condition, air-conditioning to concierge to check out was disappointing.... I am here only because my conference is here... PS: be careful to check your bill when you check out. The mini bar systems is cranky.

Spent three weeks at Club Quarters Wall Street for an out of town assignment. Very convenient in regards to location to subway stops. Extremely courteous and helpful staff, Sophie, Branden, Liz, Diane and Kirsten, made the stay exceptional, they are an asset to this hotel. I highly recommend staying at this location if you are looking for accommodation near Wall Street. I will definitely stay here again when I am in the area. Thank You.

airport shuttle is not 24hr service. there are 3 hours of the day, they don't even provide service. The business card they give us to call for shuttle to pick up our car (fly & park) is the front office mgr's personal card. of course it go directly into voice mail. Badly run holel..

If you like a long walk on the beach and a stroll through the zoo as well as a comfortable bed in a clean room, all without having to move your car, this is the place for you. The beach is just a short walk away and the zoo is across the street.

Non smoking room smelled like smoke. Was ok, and staff were nice enough, but after a bit of searching found a much better deal 300 yards down the road at the motel 8. Check the coupons in the travel magazines. Can find it at the Austin Tourist Info centre downtown.

In a hotel room, I expect some things to work. Internet access and TV are on the top of the list. In this hotel neither did. The Wireless continually dropped my New IPad and the TV would turn on but I was unable to change channels with either the remote or buttons on TV. While the hotel did offer to fix the TV, the were indifferent about the wireless access. These things should just work, they shouldn't need to be fixed. If my experience was like this, what else is wrong.

I stayed at Roosevelt hotel one night on October 9, 2012. The lobby is nice but everything else seems to be outdated. I was very disapointed with the room which was very small and clearly needed a complete remake, ie wallpaper was coming off, bathroom was just awful, etc. Spend your money somewhere else or make sure to ask for a room that was recently redone.

I stayed in this hotel last week. It is very expensive for what it is. it truly is a Motel, but with the price of a 3 star hotel. Rooms are small, not clean and noisy. It doesn't even have cable. Location is good though. I would't stay there again!!

First there was remodeling to wade through which is understandable but price should have been adjusted to compensate. There were holes in the bedsheets and they were not changed once in 4 days even though the staff was told about it. The breakfast area was not kept clean during the breakfast time. On the positive side the staff was friendly and the rooms were clean.

The property is absolutely beautiful but what is most impressive is the service amazing ,if you need pampering and to be taken care of then this is the place. Great food, excellent menu , lovely gift shop, I am in love Excellent for R&R , business, couples, familly and with the advent of proximity to LAX this my friends is a diamond.

This ids our second time staying at this Westin. It's a beautiful, well-kept hotel in a perfect location. Everything is within walking distance. We had a beautiful view of the neighborhoods in the Back Bay region of boston. The staff is excellent, and we enjoyed the buffet breakfast every morning!!

We stayed here over a weekend in July with visiting family. I was able to acquire the rooms short notice on priceline for a very reasonable price, especially considering the location. We were very pleased with the facility and the service. The hotels has a courtyard that is very tranquil and peaceful. This is a nice place to relax prior to or after experiencing the riverwalk, as sometimes that place can be a zoo. We would like to recommend this hotel for all types of travelers.

The hotel is not bad, the rooms are abnormally large and the staff friendly..Just at closer look the rooms need a little upkeep, nothing major. Location is out of the way a bit which is fine for me. Very small tv in bedroom- had to change rooms as the initial room had a tv in living room but not bedroom...need tv to sleep for me, especially when traveling.

The location of this hotel is very good. Walking distance to shopping, restaraunts, cable car, etc.. It is a nice hotel with a starbucks, gift shop, and restaraunt. The hotel itself was nice and the staff friendly. The rooms were clean and up to date, my only problem is the rooms a rather small.

Barely acceptable. Front desk clerk was not dressed professionally (probably isn't paid enough). Rooms were cleaned, but not clean. Bed was adequate, but on this trip we stayed at multiple locations of La Quinta which is lower priced and they all represented a better value. The neighborhood here appeared to be "sketchy", but we were told we could walk to restaurants which we did. I would not recommend or go back to this place. It was cheap and the establishment reflected that.

The word Suite is a joke and a bad one at best. The room I reserved was so small that the "opened the door and crawled across the bed" cliche applies. Their web site shows suites but their so called suites are 40% more expensive than their cracker barrell rooms. Place was clean but wi fi signal was almost non existent. Never again Wyndham for me.

The russian reception lady was very friendly and deserves a special praise. The 2-bed room was absolutely micro size, the space outside of the beds gave little room for anything. But you get what you pay for, a decent night's sleep for little money 200+ including breakfast. The full "plastic" breakfast was included, but we really do not like it.

The Fitz is on Lexington Avenue and is a pretty average hotel in need of some restoration. The rooms are small....as are most hotel rooms in New York but the staff friendly and helpful. There is a lively bar next to reception and this gets busy in the early evening. If you want to shop in Bloomingdales, this is a 3 minute walk from the hotel.

I have stayed in this hotel 3 times. i like it and find it very convenient for my business. its clean and they change the beddings every day my only problem is the fact that i cannot negotiation my check out time due to the relationship between guests and staff being impersonnal because i guess of the hotel size

i was in a big truck,tracor trailer,i called in advance and was instructed where to park,two hours later as im sleeping,the front desk called me asking me to move my truck,it was parked where i was directed to park,i went and moved it,this is unacceptable,try firing the morons and hiring knowledgeable people,never would i go there again stupidity is not in vougue

location is the main thing going for this hotel, you step out the door straight into the hustle and bustle of times square. rooms were adequate for four adults but the fold out bed was a bit uncomfortable but ok for a few nights. check in staff were efficiant but no more, unlike the door staff and concierge who did everything in their power to make our stay as enjoyable as possible.

Lovely clean hotel. The room was a little on the small side but I expected this in New York. Location on 5th Avenue is perfect - literally two blocks from the Empire State Building and 34th St shopping. What makes this hotel so special is the staff - everyone from the Receptionists to the Cleaners were welcoming and helpful. Would recommend this hotel to others and would definately stay here again!

We proceeded out of penn station to this good looking hotel. From the second we walked in the lights all dimmed, and huge lineup. We get the room and go up the old, old, old elevator and to our suprise the hallways look like the gates of hell. The numbers on the doors are all falling off. We get in the room and the carpet is almost half gone. Theres stains on the mattresses. The toilet is broken, the tub is missing half the bottom and the chairs are half gone. Terrible just terrible

On the corner of union square but no cable car noise Check in and out were fast and easy with friendly helpful staff The room was large for a city hotel with plenty of room and extra furniture like a comfortable lounge chair and a dest with plugs. Nice bathroom. Good temperature control. Very clean. Nice interesting walk to the convention center, top of knob hill, china town, embark aero, theater district.

Nothing particularly notable about this hotel. The under-window air conditioners are a bit loud and the walls are thin but the price is good. The only real complaint I have is that the internet connection is abysmally slow. I travel a LOT (~100 nights a year) and I know what a decent hotel internet speed is like - this hotel does not have a decent internet connection speed.

I travel as a part of my career, both as an individual and with large groups (30 plus people). Each time I stayed with Crowne Plaza Suites Houston I've been more than satisfied. Guest service has been second to none! The lobby and dinning areas are high class and present a very professional appearance. The rooms are always welcoming and spacious. My group and I will stay here every time we visit The Houston area!

This hotel is in desperate need of a renovation. The halls smell like a nursing home, the carpeting is worn, there are stains everywhere.... I could go on. The TV in room is the only item worth anything in this room. I have no idea how this place stays in business???

The hotel is great - rooms are wonderful and service is very good. The entire staff was very kind and helpful. This hotel has a lot happening on weekend - stars, parties, etc. If you want a quiet stay - find another hotel in the city. If you like action, the location and atmosphere at Trump SoHo is perfect for you.

I got sent here because my group ran out of rooms at the four seasons. I will never pay four seasons prices again. This place was just as nice and the food was 10 times better. Every coworker i had over to visit was impressed and thought i was getting special treatment.

Very east village boutique hotel! Great front door and reception staff. We stayed in a corner room and the bathroom was huge in terms of New York hotel bathrooms. Huge bathtub on one side of bathroom with a huge shower on the other. The bed and pillow were very comfy! Very close to NYU campus for any visiting parents.

reasonable price, acceptable room, valet parking for a price. The rooms are comfortable and the staff was professional. The valet went out of his way to accomodate my needs. The hotel is close to the harbor, very convenient for sightseeing. There is no view except another building or the street. I would stay again if it was a last resort. This hotel is strictly business, no frills. There is a charge for everything.

Recently attended meeting at the Sheraton at Keystone Crossing. The meeting room was long and narrow configuration that made it difficult to hear from the back. Meeting room food was average (some said stale) and catered lunches and dinner were fairly mundane. Rooms were higher than what I usually pay in Indianapolis, particularly when you add the internet room charge. A fair amount of construction in the area currently - particularly at the adjacent mall.

It has been over ten years since I've stayed at the Mayflower park, and it is as good or better than I remembered. The staff are so obliging - they do whatever it takes to make it work for you, from the valet parking to the restaurant staff. Very gracious people and a timeless atmosphere. Highly recommend it!

The back bay is wonderful area to explore, but this hotel is rather top notch. I loved our room it was overlooking the charles river, as a spg member it is great ot have the annemites of the lounge, sadly i did not visit the pool, but it was walking distance to the hynes for the conference. and right in the middle of all shopping for sure. safe secure, and just grand, go for a upper level room to see the view at night, it is spectacular. Parking was a bit expensive but you don't want to drive in Boston.

this hotel is perfect for the tourist who wants to be in the middle of the shopping heart of NYC and also be in the middle of the Musicals . You will be right in Times Square At the front desk the people are really nice and helpful. the view from the window is in general really nice as up as u getting your room. The room size is quite nice, nice and modern decoration, rooms really quiet ( wich was really important for me ) a nice bathroom with a big shower I will come again for sure :-)

Well located hotel BUT the staff was very unfriendly (the guy at the front desk made us wait 15 min for our room at 11h30 pm because he was chatting with his friend) and our room was old, noisy and smelt bad. Go elsewhere even if it is a bit more expensive: at least you will be able to sleep and rest.

Beautiful Hotel. Great view of the harbor. I would definitely recommend getting a harbor view. Loved the overflowing pool on the fourth floor. Staff was wonderful and food was excellent from the restaurant. Room service was prompt and everyone was very polite. Love all the art work in the hotel. Very close to Aquarium and other major site in Baltimore. We would stay here again.

For starters the staff is very unfriendly, not willing to help at all.The rooms smell bad, even though they are clean. The "HOT BREAKFAST" consists in cereal, bread, butter, really bad coffee and juice. The Internet Service is by cable, so you have to be connected through an actual cable to have signal. Very old furniture and TV, and their sign states "ALL NEW ROOMS". I don't recommend it at all!

Stayed there 1/23/12 that was enough. Historic yes, nice no. Shabby in all respects. Water does not get hot, TV sketchy, heating in winter abysmal, service indifferent. Air quality in the room is appalling. Internet slow and erratic $12 a day. Other staying there reported the same. I certainly would never take my wife there. All in all the Chicago convention and tourism should get this off there list.

It is hard to beat the location on Times Square. The hotel is efficient, service good, but it shows that it is 20 years old. Rooms ok but not the usual Marriott standard - a bit run down especially the bathroom. At check in we asked for a high floor room and got a nice view from the 39th floor. Friendly staff - helpful. Breakfast far too expensive - result the breakfast room was empty...

The bed was harder than the floor, bathroom is small with water damaged doors -the halls bring back memory of a dorm and open the door and it is old furnishings. Breakfast -don't bother it will be gone by the time you arrive. The plus is wifi and nice laundry facility

We only had one night here. The location is awesome, only 2 blocks from the beach, and right across the street from the San Francisco Zoo, the size of the room was great for a family. It needs some room maintenance, and the breakfast was typical wrapped pastry, fruit bowl, juice and coffee with toast or english muffin, and that was it. Nothing special, but served it's purpose.

We stayed in this hotel for two nights from Sep 21-23rd 2012 with our 2 children, rooms were clean and comfortable and location was Ideal. However on requesting bar staff to fill a babys bottle of milk we were charged $3.20. I have never been charged to fill a babys bottle previously at any hotel. The charge while excessive in itself was not the issue, being charged at all was a really mean gesture and left us with a negative feeling about the hotel.

We needed a room to stay near Penn's Landing for the Saturday fireworks over DE River. It was the perfect location and very reasonable. Considering we paid over $100 more to stay in another hotel the week prior i was happy to stay in a 'mediocre' hotel for the price we got. We'd stay there again. Stay on the river side (you can request this in making reservation) and you'll have a great view of the Ben Franklin bridge and the river.

We stayed long weekend at the Madison Hotel in Memphis. The hotel is in a great location with easy access to most sights. The hotel staff was fabulous. I have never stayed anywhere else where every staff member went out of their way to make sure our stay would be the very best they could offer. Wonderful experience!!

i am a meeting planner, but stayed at this property as a 'regular guest'. The staff is totally guest oriented, the food and beverage service outstanding! katelyn at the front desk was efficient and accomodating, David handled our car arrangements swiftly and was a great source of local information, Marik at the bell staff handled even difficult guests with professionalism and aplomb. Matthew the Saturday Manager was pleasant and truly hospitable. I stay at Omni's frequently on business, and it is nice to know they treat everyone so well- kudos!

The hotel is good for the night so fine for a stop off before you travel. Breakfast is the same as all the holiday inn express's and there is a good sized breakfast room. Pool is fine. Rooms and hotel overall is a bit tired but guess it is pretty well used. Beds are comfy and rooms are quiet. There are better hotels close, but if all you need is a cheap hotel before you travel then this is fine and staff are very friendly.

We checked in for one night. We had to drive north so we had to park our car. We arrived at 10:00, checked in at 8 pm and checked out at 11:30. The parking fee was $110.00, there was no complementary coffee or coffee pot in the room. The rooms were okay although the distinct odor of chlorine cleaner permeated the air. If you need an inexpensive room midtown, this may be the answer BUT let the buyer beware.

The service is fair. Location is great! Room condition ample for business travel. Check-in and Check-out were ultra efficient. Great access to restaurants near by and cabs are not too hard to find in the area. The service, however, have room to improve : such as sending plug adapter to the room took more than 15 min; and there were no one to help me with my luggage when i stepped off the taxi). Bottle waters in the room would be great, there were none. I would give it 3.5 stars instead of a 3 if i can...

We stayed in this hotel for 10 days. Location was excellent and there was hot water in the shower. Room looked bare, when it got cold there was no individual heat supply and all hotel could offer was to give us a space heater. Advertised breakfast was a coffee/tea with some fruit bars. Even that was hit and miss: some days no tea some days no bars. Service in this" breakfast room" was handled by a maintenance guy!!! I would not be writing such a review if the price was $150 a night not $300. Different expectations.

Nice room and not so bad breakfast. People were kind. Only 15 mins driving from the airport. Good for a business trip. It seems not recent but not old. Bathroom so and so. It is not an area for vacation, the hotel is near the highway but in only 10-15 mins of taxi you can reach both the airport and downtown

The room was clean was clean n perfect. But the stuffs are rude. They will treat the customer like the idiot. Especially to chinese, super racist. I won't recommend to this motel. There are plenty of motels or inn with good services. Don't spend money to get yelled. If I can I don't even give a point.

We stayed at the Renaissance for three days while visiting Chicago. It's right on the Blue Line which takes you right into downtown Chicago. Rooms were beautiful and very clean. The lobby was very modern and serene. Hotel desk staff had maps and directions to everything we wanted to see. They were extrememly friendly and helpful. Gino's East is a very short walk. Great place to stay.

The rooms are very outdated and need to be cleaned. There was mold on the ceiling above the shower, little black hairs on all of the towels and in the bathtub. I would never stay here again. I moved to a Holiday Inn Express after my first night. For the same price I get a huge, CLEAN suite.

The hotel is a work zone with corridors with equipment and rooms torn apart. There are no barriers to keep you from wandering in these areas when you get lost due to the poor signs. Exterior doors are not locked and rather scary people are wandering around. The poor was filthy and all the furniture was broken. No wonder it was so cheap.

Stayed for three days in this "dry" hotel and the plusses were it's location beside Graceland and a nice pool area. The minuses were threadbare towels, small rooms and a poor breakfast area and food. Despite many warnings of the possible dangers in doing so ,we experienced no difficulties or dangers as we walked around the general Graceland area.

We recently spent a couple of nights in Chicago at the Hotel Monaco on Wabash near Lake Street. Unfortunately, our room faced Wabash and we heard the screeching noise all night from the nearby "L" train that makes a turn at Wabash and Lake. The hotel and staff are very nice, but if you stay here, try to ask for a room as far away from this noise as possible.

Hard to beat the history or location of the Waldorf but that is where it stops. We had an upgraded room and it still didn't even have a bath tub. Tiny bathroom with a tiny shower. At $500 bucks a night I was very disappointed. Skip the history and spend less for more at other hotels in Manhattan.

It looks like a lot of money has been spent to upgrade this place recently. Too bad the noise issue has not been addressed. The room to room and hallway to room noise is the worst I have experienced. It is like the walls are paper thin. I could see daylight around the wall mounted air conditioner so it is apparent that sealing and insulation, which could mitigate the noise, is absent.

We visited new York,june2012. On arriving at the Roosevelt we had no service on arrival with baggage!not even hello. We walked into reception still know one had greeted us,we waited to be checked in,the reception was friendly enough but not efficient.still no had taken our suitcases!.we got to our room it was tiny bearly enough room to move around lighting was very poor,bathroom was small and very un- kept...in need of updating! Location was fantastic. Over all the hotel did serve its purpose but wasn't as grand as the pictures made out!

We stayed here because of the great feedback I saw on Trip Advisor. The hotel is fine - some of the glowing reports seemed a bit overdone. Location is a little farther from the main points of downtown than I thought. But, price was great for Seattle, hotel was clean, people were nice.

I was surprised that the warwick accepted my priceline bid of $95/night but I was glad they did. We chose to pay to upgrade to a suite--room 721. It was a very nice suite with plenty of space. Everything was great. I really had no complaints at all..which for me is very unusual. Unfortunately we did not have time to swim in the pool...but it was a very nice rooftop/view/pool/etc. The front desk was very accomodating. Everything went smoothly. I would go back and I would also pay to upgrade again.

The pool and courtyard area is very attractive and well kept, the restaurant and bar are OK. The rooms, hallway and elevator are dirty. We had a weekly rate which was very economical.When we checked in we were given keys to a room that was not yet cleaned and had to move our luggage to the 4th floor, after I had requested a 1st floor room because of a disability. Other than that the staff was courteous and helpful.

When I pulled the bed linens back it was obvious the bedding had not been changed. I requested another room. The second room had fresh bedding but it was grubby, particularly the bathroom. The light switch looked like it had not been cleaned in a long time. There were splatters of something on the wall. There was a layer of dust on everything. Considering the nightly rate I was very disappointed. The front desk clerk apologized for the inconvenience of changing rooms and said the hotel was scheduled to be remodeled. That does not excuse the current state.

The hotel is under construction which they failed to mention. When we got in our rooms, I seriously thought there was a mistake. The room was tiny and pretty dirty. You are paying a lot of money for this hotel based solely on it's location and nothing else. We left after one night and went to the The Roosevelt Hotel and it's rooms were literally twice the size. Avoid this place.

Small hotel, small room, small service. For anyone used to quality of accommodation and customer service in Asia, brace yourself. This is well below what you are used to. Good - - easy check-in, check-out. - korean restaurants nearby, if you like the food. Bad - - no restaurant in the hotel, and limited bar. - gym is so small - no pool - forget about late check-out (they will hammer you with fees, US$109 for 4 hrs...) - concierge with no real expertise (only OK to give out free maps) - in-room dining platters in the corridors all day

Stayed at this intel for.a training session held at th Orel. The facilities are appropriate for large corporate events - mine had 550 participants. The meeting facilities were nice enough but nothing extraordinary. The fitness center was too small - I had to wait for access to fitness equipment due to the large number of attendees n the Orel. The gym was also way too warm for a poper workout. It should be must better ventilate and air-conditioned for a facility to handle hundreds in Dallas.

Room appeared clean and in working order. Bed was soft but it was ok. We were put in an end room, it was VERY noisy from the traffic going by. Staff was friendly and helpful. Spotted a couple of roaches in the room. Yuck!! Staff was understanding, gave me a partial discount and I was reassured that they had pest treatment every 2 weeks and that when we stayed there again there would be no problems.

We stayed in a 2 double bed suite for the weekend while in town for our daughter's volleyball tournament at the Convention Center. This was a very convenient drive into Uptown Charlotte (with or without getting on the interstate). The hotel itself seems recently redone and is very nice and clean. The breakfast is superb! Much more than we expected. We loved the extra space in the suite so we could spread out a bit and relax. I highly recommed this hotel! Next year when we return for volleyball, we will certainly stay here agan. Good price, too!

This hotel has really cool rooms and art work. The terrace is great for breakfast too. However, the staff are aloof and the clientele in the bar are obnoxious. I have stayed in hotels all over the world and have never been so annoyed as at this one. I came with with family and spent $1k a night. Don't stay here unless you are pretentious. It is to be avoided. Aweful!!

This is my favorite spot in Dallas - quiet, clean rooms, great beds, and helpful staff. The Library Bar is a great cozy spot too. A tip - to avoid the $26 overnight parking charge, weekday parking is plentiful on the nearby side streets. Not so much during the weekends when the neighborhood turns into a party town, but weekdays are really great.

I was there a full week...monday to friday. There was something on the check-in card about daily "signature service" and once a week "white glove service." I never saw any evidence of either, except after the first day, I thought somebody had turned on different lights when I got back to the room. In-room coffee means you buy the coffee downstairs and brew it in your room.

The staff at Omni Dallas was exceptional and made our trip to Dallas something to remember! Thank you to Sarah at the front desk for her hospitality and thank you to Monique and Heath at the pool bar for DELISH drinks and many laughs! We had an amazing afternoon (and into the evening) at the pool! The hotel is gorgeous and not too far from anything. We walked everywhere! The room was immaculate and luxurious, and room service was perfect. We will be back, but not soon enough!!!

i will keep it simple and to the point,this hotel was okay nothing special but for the price i wont be back,no free internet and construction was going on in the lobby and maintenance was rude..even little things matter with hotel stays and this stay had way to many little things go wrong to add up to a bad review

We came here for a small family event, sort of a reunion. We picked the Waldorf because it has an important place in my family's history. We were disappointed with how the hotel is maintained, very disappointed with the indifferent service. On the plus side, the rooms and baths are large. The location is amazing. This wonderful old place deserves better care.

Location was good. Did not feel unsafe at any point. Able to walk to Times Square in about 15 mins. Central Park in about 6 mins. Bed was very comfortable. Rooms were small, even by NYC standards. NO hot water to our bathroom sink. Overall, for the price, it was fine.

Have just returned from a trip during Hurricane Sandy. I had 20 students with me and we were confined to the hotel for almost 3 days. The staff could not have been more helpful. Special mention must be made of Jetto who went out at the height of the storm to collect pizza for my students. Thank you so much.

This was a surprise to be so close to the airport and not hear the constant noise of the planes. Beautiful grounds, wonderful beds and a gratis breakfast added to our stay. Great place if you need to be close to the airport; if not, you must have a rental car to get around. Very close to I-5, so it will take about 20 minutes to get downtown.The Southcenter mall is within 5 minutes of the lodge and offers a wide selection of stores and restaurants.

Stayed at The Colonnade July 18-21, 2012 to scout at a major lacrosse tournament, Champ Camp. The location was excellent as far as proximity to Johns Hopkins U., but I issues: bad odor on 2nd floor throughout the visit, irregular AC/ventilation, card access keys that malfunctioned. No show-stoppers, but the overall experience was just average. Stay here if you are visiting Hopkins, but I would not make this place a destination hotel to see Baltimore. Nice bar and decent food. Gym was tiny and no pool.

The valet worked jammed our luggage on to one cart instead of using two carts likes we asked. A wheel off our luggage broke and ruined the luggage. The asst hotel manager was useless and ignored the complaint. Stay away!! There are a lot better hotels in San Antonio to stay at!!

The elevator was damaged, I have a reservation for non smoking and I stay in smoking since they use my room...nastiest odor.....dirtiest towells they supouse to be white . Breakfast included but they just don't have enough for all the guest ..the clerk was very pollite but he cannot fix everithing by itself since he was alone an his manager didn't answer the phone.....shame on him

We stayed in this hotel for 5 Nights in July. Our room was great and spacious for a city hotel and the staff was very friendly and helpful. The location of the hotel is excelent rigth next to Penn Station and within walking distance to most attractions in central Manhattan. The hotel atmosphere is great with a perfect mix of modern features and 1920's interior.

Checked in last friday for three nights. If you are a light sleeper do not stay in this suit. I was woken up sunday morning at 7a.m. the bedroom is situated above the laundry-room, the noise from this room continued all day, again on monday 7a.m. such a shame for such a nice hotel.

Low price and a good location are the calling cards at this hotel. My modest-sized room was clean and in everything was in working order. the furnishings were plain but just fine. Many of the guests seem to smoke in the hallways, which smell strongly of cigarettes on multiple floors. The rooms smelled smoke-free however. It you want luxury or hip/boutique, this isn't it, but if you want a perfectly fine room at a low price for th eneighborhood, The Hotel is a good bet.

Location near Union Square is great and it has an interesting but quirky decorating scheme - the opposite of neutral beiges. But the other amenities were barely adequate: the towels were rough and nearly thread bare; the complimentary wine in the lobby between 5-6 was jug quality; the in-house bistro was barely adequate (several orders had to be sent back) and expensive. Would not stay here again.

I was here for one night in late August 2012. The staff was super friendly and welcoming. I arrived into the hotel late so I did not switch rooms but the room I had was quite tragic. Stains on the carpet. The fabric chair in the room was sun burned and worn to the last thread. Really a sad hotel. I was using points for my stay...had I paid half of what I imagine the hotel is charging for a room I would have been quite upset. On a positive note the gym is nice.

Stayed at the Curtis for a week in April, it was very windy and you could feel it in the room. I was upgraded to a corner but that might be a bad thing when it is that windy. Room was nice, the restaurant in the lobby is good. The only thing that should be addressed is someway to either make the door from the parking garage automatic, or sliding, or something!! It is a real pain to pull that door open when you are bring in luggage and have your hands full.

We stayed here in room 1304 for 3 nights, 4th, 5th and 6th Oct. I confess I was concerned at the prices for hotels in NYC, but after assurances from our Canadian travelling friends and a huge amount of research we joined HH and booked direct. Wonderful stay, huge quiet, clean comfortable rooms. We walked to and from Penn station with our suitcase. Easy walk to Times Sqare and a comfortable area. A great Value hotel in the thick of it. Nice breakfast for the money.Friendly efficient staff.

Location location location! In just steps you can be walking on the river, listening to the world class music on 6 th street, eating at one of the hundreds of restaurants around town or watching the bats fly over the bridge. The rooms are average but clean and comfy. There is a Starbucks and tgi Fridays right in the lobby which is very nice. There are extras you will have to pay for being downtown including parking and breakfast but it is worth it to be right in the center of it all.

We stayed at the Candlewood suites for 4 nights from the 7th June 2012, it was a lovely stay, staff very friendly and helpful, rooms great size and well equipped, reclining chair was just what we needed after a hard day walking round NYC. Very clean and tidy, candlewood cupboard had everything you would need and the starter items in the room were appreciated. Didn't get round to eating the popcorn though. Thank you for a lovely stay and will definitely stay again if we are back in NYC

This hotel is in a great location - right near central park, very close to restaurant row/Broadway and Lincoln Center. I visited 2x in January and was a bit disappointed with the hotel, however. I stay in Hiltons all the time and given the price of this hotel (compared to others in the chain) I found the service to be particularly sub-par. Room service (on an off hour) took a particularly long time and more than one employee was marginally rude. My felling is, if the location isn't a priority, stay at a different hotel in the chain.

Loved the high ceiling of the lobby Good location close to the back of the White House - CVS store just opposite, restaurants around the area. But room was a little old. The room safe was wobbly.. It is also not near the main hop on and hop off sightseeing bus routes.

I stayed in this Hotel for a convention from July till July 2012. This is the worst place I have ever stayed. Please be careful and watch your credit card close. They charge you for everything. They also charge you double for everything if its with a credit card. So on that note PLEASE BE CAREFUL where you stay and WATCH YOUR CREDIT CARD.

Although we were only able to be there for a short night as we had to get up really early to catch our flight, I was impressed with the hotel. Everyone was very willing to help, from the front desk to the shuttle driver. The room was large and the bed was comfy (sleep #). Hotel was quiet at night and we were able to leave our car for two weeks while we traveled.

Awesome checkin...really nice employee with lots of help with directions on a place to eat. they were full so for some reason they upgraded us to an executive suite!! was surprised with the change but very happy with the huge room. Great bed...Great hot water in the morning....great breakfast....super fast valet parking. There is city parking close by if you dont want to use valet. Sits right behind the alamo so we were able to walk to Joe's Crab Shack and enjoy a nice evening on the riverwalk....will go here again!

After paying in advance with a guaranteed late check in, we arrived at 11:00 PM. The lobby was closed but a sign said to call the number and they would answer. Three phone calls and 45 minutes later, we left and found lodging at a Best Western for close to the same price. It has been two weeks and they still have not answered the 3 messages left. Not what they promised.

The hotels location is very convenient to the convention center and inner harbour. Rooms are OK, on the large side, unfortunately no refrigerator (minibar) or safebox in the rooms, Free wireless internet only in the lobby, but there are a few PC's for use in the lobby and one in the business lounge. The best feature was SUPERB service by Lisa Adams at reception. Business lounge also a good feature for light breakfasts, dinner, and snacks 24hrs of the day. I would return to this hotel.

Stayed 1 night after late night flight. shuttle perfect. check in efficient. room clean but extremely dated and dowdy - however wouldn't be a deal breaker in choosing again. Quiet even so close to LAX. Breakfast was one of the very best we had on our trip. Would be hard to fault if only given a serious upgrade.

We got an Expedia secret deal and so stayed here. Given the price of hotels in SF it was a good deal. The hotel itself is dated and hadn't changed much it seems over the years and the rooms are very small. The area it's in is well connected by public transport but walking wise can be a bit dicey with all the derelicts around.

We stayed at this property for an extended date night "staycation" to go dining and shopping at the Domain. It's extremely convenient to walk to restaurants, bars and enjoy yourself in an upscale urban area without downtown hassles of parking and taxis. The hotel is clean, modern and hip. We had a decent size room, which was a little larger because it was a handicapped accessible room. Got a good rate through AAA and we enjoyed ourselves.

Room was clean and staff was friendly and accomodating. Two king beds is a nice touch. Breakfast was standard "Holiday Inn Express" but was hot and fresh. Internet connection was OK. Liked the cable TV but wish some sort of guide was provided that would show what was subscribed and what isn't. I would recommend this Holiday Inn Express location.

Hotel and staff were pleasant, however hotel is middle of $2M renovations. Rooms were good, clean and renovated. Wireless has complimentary and good, however, hallways were like a warzone. Elevators were filthy. Hotel is not really near the airport as advertised by Hotwire it is some 25 mins away although drivers are perfectly pleasant. There is no place in the area to walk to eat with the exception of Ruby Tuesday. Hotel is in the middle of an Executive park, however Driver will take you to wherever you need to go. Staff was very nice and breakfast was good.

My husband and I check into this hotel every year for the holidays, there are nicer places to stay but for the an overnight stay and parking (up to 2 weeks) for the price, you really can't complain. This time we took an unexpected vacation in August and them it another try, this time we stay on the 1st floor. We have stayed on every floor and by far it is much quieter on the first, the staff is very friendly and helpful, another add bonus is they will take or pick you up at the airport.

Hotel booked by our agent who obviously thought we were on a "student" budget! We had just been to Disney and Washington DC. Both hotels ie Disney and Fairmont Washington DC were fabulous! To our horror and utter disappointment, The Manhattan at Times Square is in a terrible,neglected state. It is filthy, old and dilapidated,wall paper peeling off the walls,no wifi in rooms,no bar fridge! it would make a good location for a B grade horror movie set!

No gift shop or store in hotel so therefore no milk, no air conditioning and it was 87 degrees out, hotel under construction no mention of on website. We should have stayed at the Holiday Inn at least we could have had ac. Also no pool. Definatley not a four star hotel maybe 2.5.

Booked via priceline and didn't know what to expect. However very pleased upon arriving, top notch service, location, and look & feel. Had a great stay and will stay here next time in Fort Worth, others in our group stayed at other hotels in the area, all agree, Renaissance Worthington is the nicest.

Located on "those blocks" on Market street - tons of junkies (harmless, though), adult cinema across the street, etc. So - noisy and I wouldn't recommend to park your car outside (I watched a car being stolen from my hotel window). The hotel is old, needs remodeling, the bed is awful and the elevator takes forever to arrive. On the bright side - it is not that expensive considering the close location to Union Square, has a BART/Muni station just under the building, and the stuff is friendly.

My husband & I frequently visit LA to visit our daughter. She booked us a different place every time we came until we found the Redbury, now it is our LA home away from home. The service is amazing, the rooms are spacious, beautiful and fun (thanks to the record player & records). Added advantage is having Cleo, a wonderful restaurant, on the premises. Reminds me of some of the great boutique hotels I have visited in Europe. A must place to stay.

The rooms are tiny. Bed sheets are sandpaper. a/c is super old and does not work (we were sweating all the time). You have to wait a long time for the elevators. We were hearing people in the next room all the time (coughing!), There is no hot water after 6 pm. Overall, very terrible experience for too much money.

My husband and I stayed this hotel for one night. It's easy for us to locate it, right off the highway, behind the Waffle House. It's an area whith a few other hotels around. We went there to visit Polaris Fashion Place, North Market, and an Asian Markent. Definitely worth what we've paid. We were pleased with our decision, and will stay there again next time.

From the moment I arrived this place was a disappointment. The front desk people were not helpful and did not check us in correctly, then I had to move rooms 3 times because of issues with the room. The rooms were hot and smelled musky. The air conditioner was so loud when it started up every time, it sounded like an ice machine dropping ice. A friendly staff would have made up for the deficiencies, but they were not friendly or helpful. Very disappointed.

Nice location..right in the downtown. helpful staff. Stayed in oct 2012 during business conference when all the hotels in downtown were booked. Had to pay a premimum to get the hotel room booked here because of its location. Rooms are small and the hotel has an old look. There was no remarkable view from the room. The complimentary coffee service was good. Overall a nice stay.

We stayed for five days & enjoyed every minute. Our 1 year old daughter was treated very well here -- they had some little stuffed animals for her and warmed up her bottle for us in the morning. The gym is outstanding, as is the pool. It is amply warm & the bottom is soft rubber, not scratchy on your feet. The staff was superb (though they mis-spelled both my name and my daughter's name, so their spelling could be improved).

We checked out faster than we checked in. The room stank of mildew, smoke, and animals. Carpet was filthy and wet, furniture was sticky, and the bed linens were not clean. After taking one look at the bathroom.....totally filthy and the shower was disgusting.....we left. Would not have slept in that motel for one night, even if it were for free! Do not ruin your vacation by staing here!!!!!

I was "stuck" in NYC due to Hurricane Sandy where the conference I attended was cancelled on Sunday but all flights were also cancelled. Anyway, I must admit that under the circumstances my stay at the hotel was pretty darn good. The staff that remained was pleasant and attentive and we still had a breakfast available. Also, I want to cite Mr. Robert Sierra -- Bellman. He was most helpful directing me to local restaurants that were open in the area -- even though most eateries were closed.

Just one night so could manage. But a great price! Halls are dark and weird. Rooms are a shoe box for real. Bathrooms are okay, new. BUT things are not clean! Just vacuum and dust. Housekeeping needs to step it up. Yes, some floors are rehabbing but our whole floor was due. Clean up well, and will put up with small rooms. TV nice but only on HD channels? No coffee in room....no place to put...All things could be better...

On the beach, great location, great view. Some rif-raft hanging around on the board walk late at night. Rooms very small. Square foot price is on the high side. Score C+ Parking was good and secure. Supply and demand. Maybe a little on the pricey side for what you get. This is an older property in need of updating.

The rooms in the Villa were ok. There is an ice bucket, but no ice machine in that building and they do not communicate that. The water park is so-so, but the gym is low rent. Not worth the resort fees. The biggest problem was they served expired yogurt and diet sodas. When it was pointed out the date expired then took them back. The next day they served me the exact same expired food. Pretty slick, pretty pathetic.

The recession must be affecting this brand because the lobby looks very nice, but that's not the whole story. The service is good, but the rooms are not what you would expect from Fairmont. We were in a normal room, not a upgrade or anything, and the room needs an update. This is 2012 people. Room seemed so outdated in pretty much all areas. Service and staff are well trained and friendly. Location is good. But it comes down to your room and they dropped the ball at that point.

My husband and I stayed at the Penn's View last month and enjoyed it immensely. The hotel is quaint, charming and very elegant. It is in an excellent location for touring some of Philadelphia's historic sites. The staff is extremely accomodating and friendly. We had dinner in Ristorante Panorama downstairs. The dinner was delicious and the wine bar is world class (as confirmed by Wine Spectator Magazine). I have already reserved for next year. I highly recommend this hotel. David & Roxanne M

horrible....room and hallways dirty, sheets and towels not changed for 3 days, miserable front desk....stay away it is not worth the price or trouble property was overbooked and the staff was useless in help finding other available properties calls for repairs / maintenance in the room did not produce a response for days from the staff. TV inoperable, the safe in the room was inoperable, I had to go steal new towels from the maids cart. generally speaking, a lousy place to stay.

Excellent location, they'll take my dog (and there's a good pet-sitting service across the street) and it's top value for money. Only caveats: the mattress is softer than those I've had at other Hampton Inn properties (but not annoyingly so), the two elevators (over 20 floors) can be very busy in the morning, and if they're making bacon for the breakfast buffet, the aroma will come up through the ventilation system (at least it did in my room). I'll definitely return here.

Stayed for one night. The man behind the desk was great. Checked us in quick and ordered us a taxi when requested, as well as giving us directions. He could not be faulted. The room wasn't fantastic but then again it wasn't bad. It was clean and tidy and had the basic things you expect. Booked the room before checking out other locations and found the Hilton down the road to be slightly cheaper and clearly better. All in all though, it was good enough for one night.

A good value Hotel in a great area of Philadelphia, within easy walking distance of the Historical Area. Friendly staff and cosy rooms, and the included breakfast was most welcome. The only downside was that our room on the 4th floor had really bad WIFI reception, and the Air-Conditioner was old and noisy, and couldn't keep the room cool on the hottest April day that Philadelphia has seen for some time. Overall a Good Hotel, but the air-con and WIFI Reception in some rooms need to join the 21st Century.

We were on our honeymoon and had asked for a room on a higher floor. When we arrived the receptionist congratulated us and gave us a room on the 43rd floor. The room was wonderful, with views over Ground Zero. There was some noise but this is to be expected due to the location of the hotel. There are 2 subways just outside the hotel, so getting around New York was easy. I would recommend this hotel to anyone and would love to stay here again.

The hotel has great views but the rooms are less than what you expect. NO amenities, not even a mini bar, and expensive internet even in the conference rooms. Great doorman and friendly people at front desk.Bathrooms are so dated, faucets get stuck. No way of setting the temperature of the AC, its on or off.

The rooms were in dirty as well as one door did not lock when shut. Our bus driver even complained of roaches in his room. The staff was great and very helpful but the condition of the rooms were terrible. Non Smoking rooms that smelled of smoke. If the National FFA doesn't drop Super 8 from their housing list I will be surprised. Scott Long Cabool Ag. Department 417.962.0082

Hotel was nice, staff was nice, location is great. Trendy hotel, with vibrant bar scene which is cool. Rooms are nice enough, but i was disappointed that there was a fair amount of mildew on the caulk in the shower. The bathroom could have been much more nicely maintained in my opinion.

Great location and nice service. The rooms are clean but would benefit from a renovation. I stayed in a one bedroom suite with a connecting room on the club floor and found the rooms to be outdated. The club lounge was very nice although gets very busy during breakfast as guests from other floors probably come up to enjoy the free breakfast that is being offered at the club lounge.

As noted great location. Check in smooth ask for up grade and received at no extra charge. Hotel section we stayed in, as there is three different sections, was being "up graded" and is in need of that. Room small and was "weather beaten". Was relatively clean. Price reasonable for NY City.

The room was great. Modern furnishings, clean, comfortable. Easy access from 35. Friendly front desk staff. Not one hassle and we showed up 2 hrs before check in, yet still did not have to wait for a room. The entrance needs some cleaning/updates as do the hallways but no complaints about the room and that is most important to us. We paid much more than we would have for a hotel of this class but we attributed the cost to the UT game that evening and the fact that we made last minute reservations.

Nice hotel for being in the same hotel chain as "The Knights Inn" Friendly staff and room priced right. I had only two issues the traffic noise (hotel is close to a major road) was unreal. I suggest a room on the third floor and toward the back of the hotel. Also the room had the smell of bug spray. Room had flat screen tv, microwave and frig. Again Nice Hotel overall!

We stayded there for 3 nights. Location is actually really good, room and toilet size are good as well. But rooms are not extremely clean, in fact, they are not very clean. Our room was located very far from the elevator and so wasn't very practical as it involved a long hallway walk. Service was ok and they did gave us a complimentary ticket for 1 day breakfast, that was nice. Overall I would say it pretends to be a 4 star hotel but it is a 3 star with a fancy dress.

Stayed here for trinity univ reunion plus airport convenice and this hotel is very convenient to both mainly due to its location near major roadways in san antonio. Breakfast a strong plus as well. Only fault....the typical heavy duty doors vibrate nearby rooms but thats the nature of the beast.

My husband and I stayed here for three nights. The hotel rooms were average rooms, nothing special about them. Bathrooms need to be updated. The tub had a big gash in it and it was peeling. the hallways look very old. Parking was hard to find at night. Check-in was a breeze. I would say again for one night. Beds were comfy.

Stayed at the Hyatt Regency recently. The location was amazing and the hotel looked great, this of course made me happy with the choice of hotel. However, the best part was the greeting I received at the front desk upon walking into the lobby. Stephanie greeted me with a friendly, welcoming greeting that made me feel at home! She smiled, was very helpful, and it's her service which would lead me to making the same choice again in the future!

This property has the feel that you've landed in the WRONG part of town, but if you don't mind that then it's a good place to stay because it's quite cheap! I had a good night's sleep. Seemed plenty clean, small kitchenette in the room was nice. A bit outdated. But I don't regret staying because of the $$ savings!

Great service. Awesome staff. Perfect location. Walkable to Fells Point, Canton, Inner Harbor and route 83 if you need to drive anywhere else in the city. Beautiful suite. Like a home away from home. Very clean, comfortable, well designed and fun. Best mattress ever. White fluffy comforter. Eco-friendly. Gay-friendly. Well priced. I can't say enough about this place. Also, the Black Olive restaurant is amazing. Anyone planning a trip or long weekend in Baltimore should stay here.

We stayed at the Sorrento in Seattle for our 5th wedding anniversary and wow what an amazing two nights. Talk about rolling out the red carpet, I could not have felt anymore pampered by a hotel. Such a beatiful accomodation. Wish we could have stayed a week! Can't wait to stay at the Sorrento again.

This is a very nice hotel. It's about 10 minutes or less from the airport and located near a few eating places which has fast food. The only concerns that I had was that there was no continental breakfast in the morning. Also, the pool was visible from the outside. There wasn't any privacy. I did enjoy the work out room. I got a decent rate on hotels.com. The hotel was very clean and the staff was very helpful.
