The hotel was ok. Be careful to not get a room at the end of the row - we were right by the entrance to the garage, and it was incredibly loud at all hours. BUT regardless of quality - be aware they charge 8 dollars a night for parking. I was appalled - this is not a cheap hotel, and hotels outside of downtown RARELY charge for parking. It seemed like an unfortunate way to nickel and dime people!

Very well-located, but not my favorite of the 4 sister hotels here in NYC. Wi-fi rarely worked (very important to my husband's work), shabby decor, and did not feel as welcome as we have at the other hotels. Stayed several nights, and felt the "hostesses" at the complimentary buffet thought we were imposing on them. Disappointing; won't stay again.

We stayed a few days in the Mark Hopkins and liked this old, prestigious building. The lobby is surprisingly small and you sort of would expect a bar down there. Standard room is good, some people may find the sounds of the cable tram outside annoying (we liked this 'couleur locale') and HD TV would have been nice for that big LCD screen. Staff very friendly: great people outside, excellent concierge, efficient reception desk, very helpful cleaning staff, etc. Breakfast on the 18th floor is ridiculously expensive, but hey: you can't beat the view and the quality is good.

The hotel itself is nice but dont fall for the "free" parking.They have about 5 available spaces.After those are taken ,you are on your own to find and pay for your own parking.I thought the "free "parking would compensate for the not-so-great neighborhood which is also far away from the inner harbor. Be warned, if it sounds too good to be true it probably is.

We returned to the Marriott for the first time in 15 years and very much enjoyed our stay. They have updated and kept the hotel very nicely. It was a bit crowded at the pool, but everything else was great. I was surprised at the decline at Sea Port Village and the mall up the street. Both places have gone downhill and are very dated. There are some great restaurants around though. I will definitely be returning.

This was our first time staying at a Hyatt, the location is great the hotel lobby is attractive but the rooms are dated and "very" dirty. Hard to see the pretty veiws with the nasty dirty windows. The bathroom was horrible. I called the front desk and they send someone to rinse out the bathtab but nothing else was done. There was something wrong with our door sensor and we had to constanly bring our keys to the front desk. We moved to the Serrano Kimpton Hotel after the secont night. I highly recommend the Serrano Hotel.

got and killed a bed bug, did get bit on my thigh , took pictures had to wake up my family at 4 am to check if they had any bites or bugs in the bed could not go back to sleep thinking my family or me will get bitten, the receptionist did not know what to say and she would tell her supervisor, but 2 days later and have not received a call or anything, will not stay again at that hotel

The location was fantastic! My boyfriend and I could easily get to all the great locations in Manhattan! The rooms were spotless and the bed was very comfy! The service was awesome too! The people were friendly, courteous and helpful! Overall, it was an awesome stay! Especially for the price!

This is a huge hotel, if you get your room far away in a long corridor you will be walking a lot. The poolarea is great. Noicy AC. Comfy beds. The area north of the hotel (Adams Morgan) is really nice for som great party nights. 15 min walk from Dupont Circle metrostation.

Rooms are very cool, like most other W Hotels. It has awesome views of Lake Michigan and the city from the rooms and from the bar at the top of the hotel. I actually can't remember if it was at the top of the hotel or close to the top. :( That reminds me, the drinks are very good. Very nice staff. But everybody in Chicago is nice anyway.

First of all I want to say that the staff was really great. The people behind the desk were helpful and the concierge was always there with great restaurant recommendations. However, for what we paid for the rooms, the rooms themselves were average. When we showered in the morning the humidity went throughout our room. The bathrooms need updating with fans. The location is great, however, which is partially why we chose the hotel. I would stay somewhere else next time.

Hotel is for long weekend trip okay, ideal place to start your city trip. Room (Queensize bed) for 2 person too small. Breakfast pretty fine (american standard , daily fresh Doughnuts and fruits) .Aircon sysytem in room quite old (loud and bad smell). Overall I would recommed this hotel for a stay.

Stayed at the Ritz the weekend of November 30. Very nice hotel, nice room, enjoyable restaurant and bar. Breakfast at the restaurant was very good. Room had no view but clean and nice size. Compared to our stay at the Pierre, I felt the attention to detail at this hotel was lacking. We didn't use the spa or gym (went for runs in central park). Can't best the location of this hotel.

This is about the most average business hotel one could imagine. I did not find the staff either particularly friendly or unpleasant. The accommodations were average. The only thing that stood out was that my room was completely passed over for cleaning one day. Other than that, I can't really complain or praise.

Best hotel if you're attending a conference at the Hynes center... can get to the hotel and back quickly and without going outside. Attached to a mall. Trader Joe's across the street! Rooms are typical for city tower hotels. Housekeeping nice. Nice enough neighborhood for walking. Check out Bukowski's bar across the street.

Recently stayed at the Essex Inn. Liked the location - it was an easy walk to the Adler Aquarium, Field Museum, Art Institute, and Millennium Park. The hotel rooms were fine, with decent space and a fridge, which was handy. The kids liked the pool and the rooftop garden area. Overall, I'd stay again. It was just an average place to stay, but if you're just looking for a place to crash, it'll be just fine.

The windows in our room were broken and did not stay shut, although we were on the second floor this was unsafe and noisy. There were no screens in the windows either. The location is great, but what a shame that the outer door is left open and again safety seemed to be the issue. The wi-fi did not work and when addressed with staff this was brushed off. The springs could be felt through the mattress and the pillows were covered with dirty pillow cases. Very disappointing.

Stayed at this hotel for 4 nights late in November, 2012. Hotel is relatively new and in good condition (work is being completed on the dining room but breakfast is served in an adjoining room). Good service, friendly and helpful staff. Indoor pool is a nice feature, as is free wi-fi and parking. Excellent bed- very comfortable. Nearby highway work cannot be heard but makes car trips difficult. Only complaint about hotel: poor soundproofing. We were on 2nd of 4 floors and we could hear footsteps and talking from both outside of our room as well as above us.

Great location, but the rooms are very dated; the concept of tower one, tower two went out with Frodo and Gandalf. This was not a favorite at all, but the staff were very nice and always there to greet you. I won’t be staying here again, but I noticed the place was full, so others liked it.

I reserved this hotel through Expedia unpublished rate because it was a good rate. Although, when we got there they said we paid for a petite room which mean a full size bed, there was a $20 to upgrade to king bed. This is information was not clear when the reservation was done. Hotel doesn't give free wifi on rooms. No complimentary bottle of water. Bathroom is extremely small, as the room as well. Towels smells to chlorine to much. Breakfast quite expensive. Excellent location!!

My husband & I booked in here the end of September.....on entering the hotel it was easy to see it was old and rundown....even the lift was a shock...our room had half the wall paper off and sheets lull creased. We asked to move rooms...our second room was no better and the sheets and towels were grubby. We decided to check out immediately and the receptionist did not even seem surprised and made no attempt to change our mind.

I stay at the Affinia two to four times a year for business and am never disappointed. The staff is courteous and friendly, the rooms are newly updated, beds are super comfy and I love the pillows which is a big deal! Bathroom products are excellent quality and the hotel is conveniently located. What more could you ask for?

I was there for a week at a meeting at the Convention Center that is most conveniently connected a short walk through a covered sky ridge. My room was clean and quiet, and that's all I can say that was good. Room service is well below Marriott standards with frequent mixups, and good luck getting an operator to answer the phone. The "service express" is a joke. Even the staff admitted that all it does is add middleman between the guest and the person you should be talking too which exponentially increases the opportunity for errors.
